Histology consistent with leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis
Direct immunofluorescence showing vascular IgA deposition
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly unilateral calf swelling
History of Crohn's disease
Use of weekly adalimumab
No reported abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, hematuria, or renal symptoms

data.description: A drug-associated immune-complex vasculitis in which tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitors, including adalimumab, can rarely trigger IgA-mediated leukocytoclastic vasculitis. It may present with lower-extremity palpable purpura and joint symptoms, sometimes after prolonged exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric rash predominantly involving the feet and legs
Vascular IgA deposition on direct immunofluorescence
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent upper respiratory infection, which more strongly suggests infection-triggered IgA vasculitis
Multiple prior self-limited upper respiratory episodes
No stated temporal relationship between adalimumab dosing or initiation and rash onset
No reported systemic drug-hypersensitivity symptoms such as diffuse urticaria or fever

data.description: A histopathologic pattern of immune-mediated inflammation of small dermal vessels, typically producing palpable purpura on dependent areas of the legs. It may be caused by infection, medications, inflammatory bowel disease, or systemic vasculitis. In this case, the IgA staining indicates that it is most specifically IgA vasculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric erythematous lesions on the lower extremities
Crohn's disease as an underlying inflammatory condition
Skin biopsy showing leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Ankle synovitis is less typical of skin-limited leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Prominent unilateral calf pain and swelling
Specific vascular IgA deposition, which favors IgA vasculitis rather than nonspecific cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis

data.diagnosis: Crohn's disease-associated peripheral inflammatory arthritis with vasculitic skin manifestation
data.description: Crohn's disease can cause extraintestinal manifestations including peripheral arthritis, usually affecting large joints of the lower limbs, and inflammatory skin disorders. Immune-complex vasculitis can rarely occur in association with inflammatory bowel disease, although the biopsy pattern here is more specifically diagnostic of IgA vasculitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Crohn's disease reportedly improved and controlled for the past 3 years
Recent upper respiratory illness immediately preceding the eruption
Vascular IgA, C3, and fibrin deposition strongly indicating IgA vasculitis
No reported gastrointestinal flare symptoms such as diarrhea, abdominal pain, or weight loss

data.description: A 47-year-old man presented to his primary care physician with a six-month history of left-sided sore throat, ipsilateral otalgia, and a six-week history of a left-sided neck mass. He had never smoked and drank less than 5 units of alcohol per week. On examination in the ENT clinic, a firm fixed lymph node was palpable in the upper anterior triangle.

data.diagnosis: HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma of the left base of tongue with cervical nodal metastasis
data.description: A squamous-cell cancer arising in the oropharynx, commonly the lingual tonsil/base of tongue. HPV-associated disease often occurs in relatively young patients with little or no smoking history and commonly presents with a cystic or firm upper-neck lymph-node metastasis. The CT and PET-CT show an FDG-avid left oropharyngeal/base-of-tongue mass and an FDG-avid left cervical nodal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Firm fixed upper anterior-triangle neck mass
Imaging evidence of an oropharyngeal mass with metabolically active cervical nodal disease

data.description: Squamous cell carcinoma can arise from the base of tongue, tonsil, or other oropharyngeal mucosa and spread to upper cervical lymph nodes. It classically occurs in patients with substantial tobacco and alcohol exposure, although it can occur without these risk factors.
symptoms_in_common: Referred ear pain on the same side
Imaging evidence of a left oropharyngeal mass
FDG-avid neck nodal lesion consistent with metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Never-smoker status
Very low alcohol consumption
Age 47, which is younger than the typical presentation for tobacco- and alcohol-associated disease

data.diagnosis: Oropharyngeal lymphoma involving the lingual tonsil/base of tongue with cervical lymphadenopathy
data.description: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can involve Waldeyer's ring, including the lingual tonsils at the base of tongue, and may produce a pharyngeal mass with enlarged FDG-avid cervical lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Neck mass due to cervical lymphadenopathy
FDG uptake in the primary-region lesion and cervical node on PET-CT
Absence of smoking and heavy alcohol exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Ipsilateral otalgia is less characteristic
A firm fixed solitary upper-neck node is more suggestive of metastatic head-and-neck carcinoma
No reported constitutional symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.diagnosis: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in a cervical lymph node from an occult oropharyngeal primary
data.description: Cervical nodal metastasis from an initially occult head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma is common, particularly from the palatine tonsil or base of tongue. PET-CT may reveal the small mucosal primary responsible for an apparently isolated neck mass.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent firm fixed left upper-neck mass
FDG-avid cervical lymph node on PET-CT
FDG-avid left oropharyngeal/base-of-tongue abnormality that could represent the primary site
symptoms_not_in_common: No major atypical symptoms; the imaging suggests that the primary is identifiable rather than truly occult

data.description: 72-year-old white woman with 10-year history of recurrent cystitis. No systemic symptoms. Physical exam showed slight anemia. Urine cultures were positive for Escherichia coli. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy detected by CT and ultrasound. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and subsequent biopsies were negative for both pathologic lymphoid infiltrate and Helicobacter pylori. Otolaryngologic examination and bone marrow biopsy were negative. Serology for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus was negative. No monoclonal component found in serum protein electrophoresis.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma) of the urinary bladder
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in extranodal mucosal tissue. Primary bladder MALT lymphoma is rare and is often associated with longstanding chronic cystitis or recurrent bacterial urinary infections. The images show a dense small lymphoid infiltrate beneath urothelium, compatible with lymphoma involving the bladder.
symptoms_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, supporting localized extranodal disease
Negative bone marrow biopsy, supporting primary localized bladder lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are atypical; recurrent bacterial cystitis is a recognized association rather than a contradiction

data.diagnosis: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia of the urinary bladder (chronic follicular cystitis)
data.description: A benign reactive accumulation of lymphoid tissue in the bladder wall caused by chronic irritation or recurrent infection. It may produce lymphoid aggregates and can mimic low-grade bladder lymphoma histologically.
symptoms_not_in_common: Slight anemia is not usually a feature of uncomplicated reactive follicular cystitis
The dense, apparently monomorphic lymphoid infiltrate in the images is more concerning for lymphoma than for purely reactive inflammation

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the urinary bladder
data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can rarely involve the bladder, either as primary disease or as part of systemic lymphoma. It usually consists of large atypical lymphoid cells and tends to have a more clinically aggressive presentation than MALT lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bladder mass or mucosal lesion
Bladder involvement can occur without lymphadenopathy in primary cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten-year history of recurrent cystitis is more characteristic of bladder MALT lymphoma or reactive cystitis
No systemic symptoms
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
The histologic images appear dominated by small lymphoid cells rather than large transformed cells
The apparently indolent localized presentation is less typical of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: 95-year-old woman admitted after a fall. Medical history includes Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Laboratory findings showed elevated white cell count and C reactive protein levels. Urine culture revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Blood cultures were negative.

A complicated urinary tract infection characterized by gas production within the bladder wall and/or lumen, most often caused by gas-forming organisms such as Klebsiella pneumoniae. It occurs particularly in older adults with diabetes.
symptoms_in_common: Urine culture positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae
Pelvic radiograph appearance of curvilinear gas outlining the bladder wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Fall
Alzheimer's disease
Hypertension
Negative blood cultures

data.diagnosis: Complicated lower urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) due to Klebsiella pneumoniae
data.description: A bacterial infection of the urinary bladder; in frail older adults it may present with nonspecific features and systemic inflammatory-marker elevation rather than classic dysuria or urinary frequency.
symptoms_not_in_common: Gas outlining the bladder wall on radiograph is not typical of uncomplicated cystitis
Fall
Alzheimer's disease
Hypertension
Negative blood cultures

data.description: An abnormal communication between bowel and bladder that can cause gas in the bladder and recurrent urinary infections, usually associated with diverticular disease, bowel malignancy, inflammatory bowel disease, or prior surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Gas projected over the bladder region on pelvic radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: The radiographic pattern of gas in the bladder wall favors emphysematous cystitis rather than a fistula
Klebsiella pneumoniae infection in a patient with diabetes more strongly supports emphysematous cystitis
No reported pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial urinary infections, or bowel symptoms
Fall
Alzheimer's disease
Hypertension
Negative blood cultures

data.description: 22-year-old athletic male presented with swelling and locking of the left knee. He had no recent trauma but had several football injuries as a child. Two years prior, he had experienced disabling knee pain.

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle
data.description: An osteochondral disorder in which subchondral bone and overlying cartilage of the femoral condyle become damaged and may partially detach, producing an unstable fragment or loose body. The radiographs show a subchondral osteochondral defect/sclerotic lesion in the femoral condyle, a typical location for knee osteochondritis dissecans.
symptoms_in_common: History of repetitive childhood football-related knee injuries
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent trauma

data.diagnosis: Unstable osteochondral fragment or intra-articular loose body secondary to osteochondritis dissecans
data.description: A detached or partially detached cartilage-and-bone fragment within the knee joint, often arising from an osteochondral lesion such as osteochondritis dissecans. It can intermittently obstruct joint movement and cause locking and effusions.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episodes of severe knee pain
Radiographic evidence of an osteochondral abnormality that could generate a fragment
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent acute injury preceding the current locking episode

data.description: A tear of the medial or lateral meniscus, commonly associated with twisting sports injuries and capable of causing pain, recurrent effusions, catching, and locking. It is an important clinical alternative for mechanical knee symptoms, although the radiographic osteochondral lesion favors osteochondritis dissecans.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent twisting or traumatic event
Visible osteochondral/subchondral lesion on radiographs is not typical of an isolated meniscal tear

data.description: 48-year-old male presented with 1-week history of jaundice, dark brown urine, pale stools, and nausea. Medical history and physical exam were unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed hepatic panel in cholestatic pattern: total bilirubin 117 μmol/L, conjugated bilirubin 66.8 μmol/L, alkaline phosphatase 173 IU/L, γ-Glutamyltransferase 380 IU/L, Alanine transaminase 468 IU/L. CA19-9 was 11783 IU/mL. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and β2-microglobulin were normal.

data.diagnosis: Primary pancreatic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
data.description: A rare extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma involving the pancreas, often presenting as a pancreatic head mass causing biliary obstruction. The imaging and histology are compatible with a lymphomatous pancreatic mass composed of large atypical lymphoid cells; immunohistochemical nuclear/cytoplasmic staining patterns support lymphoid malignancy rather than adenocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic head-region mass causing extrahepatic biliary obstruction
Normal LDH can occur despite lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated CA19-9 is more commonly associated with pancreaticobiliary epithelial malignancy, although it can rise substantially from biliary obstruction
Absence of constitutional B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the pancreas, most commonly arising in the pancreatic head and causing obstruction of the common bile duct. It commonly produces painless obstructive jaundice and elevated CA19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic head mass with biliary obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology appears lymphoid rather than gland-forming malignant epithelial cells
Immunohistochemical findings shown are more suggestive of lymphoma than pancreatic adenocarcinoma
No reported abdominal or back pain, weight loss, anorexia, or palpable gallbladder

data.diagnosis: Primary pancreatic lymphoma, follicular lymphoma subtype
data.description: An uncommon B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma involving the pancreas that may form a pancreatic mass and obstruct the bile duct. Follicular lymphoma is typically composed of centrocyte-like and centroblast-like cells and is often associated with germinal-center immunophenotypic markers.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of a significant prior pancreatic disease history
Normal LDH may be present in indolent lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid onset of severe biliary obstruction is less typical for indolent follicular lymphoma
Very high CA19-9 is not a characteristic lymphoma marker
The histology may be more consistent with diffuse sheets of large cells than a follicular growth pattern

data.description: A bile-duct adenocarcinoma arising in the distal common bile duct, often causing obstructive jaundice and elevated CA19-9. It may appear as a mass near the pancreatic head and can mimic a pancreatic neoplasm.
symptoms_in_common: Obstruction in the pancreatic head/distal bile-duct region
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy morphology is not typical of adenocarcinoma or malignant gland formation
Immunohistochemistry appears to favor a lymphoid neoplasm rather than biliary epithelial cancer
No reported weight loss, abdominal pain, pruritus, or constitutional decline

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: T-cell/histiocyte rich large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: 80-year-old woman with 6-month history of slowly increasing asymptomatic lumbar subcutaneous mass. History of chronic renal failure requiring dialysis three times weekly for 10 years. Poor compliance with phosphate-binding medications and dietary restrictions. Physical exam showed firm, immobile subcutaneous nodule measuring 9 cm in major axis. Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

data.diagnosis: Uremic tumoral calcinosis (secondary tumoral calcinosis due to chronic renal failure)
data.description: A periarticular lobulated mass composed of calcium-phosphate deposits, occurring in patients with long-standing renal failure and dialysis, usually driven by hyperphosphatemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism. Imaging typically shows dense, multilobulated 'cloud-like' calcified masses.
symptoms_in_common: Poor adherence to phosphate binders and dietary phosphate restriction
Elevated parathyroid hormone consistent with secondary hyperparathyroidism
Slowly enlarging painless firm subcutaneous mass
Large immobile mass near the pelvic/hip region
CT appearance of a dense lobulated calcified periarticular soft-tissue mass
Increased radiotracer uptake in the mass on bone scintigraphy
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild hypocalcemia, as calcium may be normal or elevated in some cases

data.diagnosis: Calcinosis cutis secondary to chronic kidney disease
data.description: Deposition of insoluble calcium salts within the skin and subcutaneous tissues. In chronic kidney disease, metastatic calcification may occur because of disturbed calcium-phosphate metabolism, especially severe hyperphosphatemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large 9 cm multilobulated periarticular mass is more characteristic of tumoral calcinosis than typical calcinosis cutis
No reported skin ulceration, chalky discharge, inflammation, or multiple smaller cutaneous lesions

data.description: A severe dialysis-associated disorder involving calcification and thrombosis of small dermal and subcutaneous vessels, usually causing intensely painful ischemic skin lesions that may ulcerate and become necrotic.
symptoms_in_common: End-stage renal disease treated with long-term dialysis
Subcutaneous calcium deposition may occur in affected tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is painless and asymptomatic
No livedo, purpura, skin necrosis, ulceration, eschar, or infection
Large circumscribed lobulated calcified mass is atypical
No evidence of ischemic cutaneous lesions

data.description: Abnormal bone formation in soft tissues, often after trauma, surgery, neurologic injury, or prolonged immobilization. It commonly produces a painful or stiff periarticular mass with organized peripheral ossification.
symptoms_in_common: Firm immobile soft-tissue mass near the hip/pelvic region
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of trauma, surgery, neurologic injury, or local inflammation
Mass is asymptomatic without pain or restricted movement
Severe hyperphosphatemia and dialysis-related mineral-bone disorder strongly favor uremic tumoral calcinosis
Imaging shows multilobulated amorphous calcification rather than organized mature bone formation

data.description: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

data.diagnosis: Lateral tibial plateau fracture (split-depression type, Schatzker II)
data.description: An intra-articular fracture of the lateral upper tibia involving a split component and depression of the tibial plateau. The radiographs show an irregular fracture line involving the lateral tibial plateau with articular surface disruption.
symptoms_in_common: Closed injury with intact neurovascular examination
Radiographic fracture involving the proximal tibia/tibial plateau

data.diagnosis: Tibial plateau fracture with traumatic knee hemarthrosis
data.description: A fracture extending into the knee joint can cause bleeding into the joint space, producing rapid diffuse swelling and pain. The imaging supports a proximal tibial articular fracture.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid generalized knee swelling after trauma
Intra-articular proximal tibial fracture on radiographs

data.diagnosis: Associated internal derangement of the knee (meniscal and/or anterior cruciate ligament injury)
data.description: Tibial plateau fractures from high-energy knee trauma are frequently associated with meniscal, cruciate ligament, and other soft-tissue injuries; these are not directly confirmed on the supplied plain radiographs and would require MRI or operative assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Tibial plateau fracture pattern associated with ligamentous and meniscal injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported knee instability or giving-way sensation
No reported locking or catching
Plain radiographs primarily demonstrate a bony fracture rather than a definite ligament or meniscal tear

diagnoses.name: Tibial plateau fracture
diagnoses.title: Fracture of lower end of tibia[Tibial Plateau]

data.description: A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

A rare mesenchymal tumor of the gastrointestinal tract arising from interstitial cells of Cajal. Rectal GISTs commonly present as well-circumscribed submucosal spindle-cell masses and may show KIT or PDGFRA mutations; immunohistochemistry is typically positive for KIT (CD117) and DOG1.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary well-delimited 6-cm rectal mass on CT and MRI
Spindle-cell morphology in the histologic images

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor arising from the muscularis mucosae or muscularis propria of the rectum. It typically forms a slow-growing, well-circumscribed submucosal mass and may cause obstructive symptoms when large.
symptoms_in_common: Anal/rectal pain from a low rectal mass
Smooth elastic mass on digital rectal examination
Spindle-cell appearance compatible with smooth-muscle differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging description of infiltration of the rectal wall, which is less typical of a benign leiomyoma

data.description: A malignant smooth-muscle tumor of the rectum. It can present as a large intramural or submucosal spindle-cell mass with local invasion and symptoms of rectal obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Mass compressing and infiltrating the rectal wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth, elastic and well-delimited clinical appearance, which can be more suggestive of a less aggressive mesenchymal tumor

data.description: An uncommon peripheral-nerve sheath tumor arising in the rectal wall. Most are benign and present as slow-growing submucosal spindle-cell masses; tumor cells are generally S100 and SOX10 positive rather than KIT/DOG1 positive.
symptoms_in_common: Constipation due to compression of the rectal lumen
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent infiltration of the rectal wall is less typical for a benign rectal schwannoma

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

data.description: Two-year-four-month-old female with intrauterine growth restriction at birth (39 weeks, C-section; birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, head circumference 31 cm, all 3rd percentile). She has persistent short stature and low body weight, with triangular face, prominent forehead, small chin, hypoplastic nasal alae, large mouth with thin downturned lips, low-set ears, deeply set eyes, delayed teething, microdontia, delayed bone age, thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels, and lipoatrophy. She had bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss detected at 3 months and uses hearing aids since 4 months. Psychomotor development has been normal, with sitting at 8 months, walking at 14 months, and talking at 13 months. Brain MRI was normal. Genetic testing showed a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*).

A rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic PIK3R1 variants, characterized by prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, partial lipodystrophy/lipoatrophy, thin or aged-appearing skin, characteristic facial features, delayed dentition, and metabolic risk including insulin resistance or diabetes later in life. SHORT refers to short stature, hyperextensibility/hernia, ocular depression, Rieger anomaly, and teething delay, although not all features are required.
symptoms_in_common: De novo heterozygous PIK3R1 c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) variant
Persistent short stature and low body weight
Triangular face with prominent forehead and small chin
Large mouth with thin downturned lips
Thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss is not a classic or consistently reported feature of SHORT syndrome
Low-set ears are not a core diagnostic feature

data.description: A premature-aging disorder, usually caused by de novo LMNA variants, with postnatal growth failure, loss of subcutaneous fat, thin wrinkled skin, and a characteristic aged facial appearance. Cardiovascular disease and skeletal complications typically develop over time.
symptoms_in_common: Marked growth failure and low body weight
Thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Growth restriction was already severe prenatally; progeria more often has relatively normal birth size followed by postnatal growth failure
Triangular facial appearance with hypoplastic nasal alae and deeply set eyes is more characteristic of SHORT syndrome
Microdontia is not a typical hallmark
Delayed bone age is not a defining feature
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not typical
The identified pathogenic PIK3R1 variant supports SHORT syndrome rather than LMNA-related progeria

data.description: A severe generalized congenital lipodystrophy, usually caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2, characterized by near-complete lack of body fat, muscular prominence, acromegaloid features, hepatomegaly, hypertriglyceridemia, and early insulin resistance.
symptoms_in_common: Visible superficial veins due to paucity of subcutaneous fat
Potential future risk of insulin resistance in a lipodystrophy disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrauterine growth restriction and short stature are not typical; affected infants may have normal or increased birth size
Triangular face, prominent forehead, hypoplastic nasal alae, and small chin are not typical
Thin wrinkled skin and progeroid appearance are less typical than in SHORT syndrome
Delayed teething, microdontia, and delayed bone age are not characteristic
No hepatomegaly, muscular hypertrophy, acromegaloid appearance, or metabolic abnormalities are described
Severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss is not typical
The heterozygous PIK3R1 variant is inconsistent with the usual genetic causes of this condition

data.description: A growth-restriction syndrome most commonly related to abnormalities of chromosome 11p15 imprinting or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7. It features prenatal and postnatal growth failure, triangular face, prominent forehead, feeding difficulty, body asymmetry, and relative macrocephaly at birth.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent postnatal short stature and low body weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Head circumference was also at the 3rd percentile rather than relative macrocephaly
Lipoatrophy, thin wrinkled skin, and visible vessels are not typical defining features
Hypoplastic nasal alae, large mouth, and thin downturned lips are more suggestive of SHORT syndrome
Delayed teething with microdontia is not a classic feature
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not typical
No limb/body asymmetry or feeding difficulty is described
The de novo PIK3R1 variant establishes an alternative molecular diagnosis

data.description: A rare craniofacial developmental syndrome characterized by a bird-like facies with micrognathia, dental abnormalities, hypotrichosis, skin atrophy, ocular abnormalities such as microphthalmia or cataracts, and proportionate short stature.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe prenatal growth restriction and generalized lipoatrophy are not typical core findings
Triangular face with hypoplastic nasal alae and deeply set eyes is more typical of SHORT syndrome
No microphthalmia, congenital cataracts, or other major ocular malformation is described
No hypotrichosis is described
Bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss is not a usual defining feature
The PIK3R1 pathogenic variant supports SHORT syndrome rather than Hallermann-Streiff syndrome

data.description: 56-year-old Ethiopian male with persistent fever, chills, cough, night sweats, and weight loss, with fatigue and dyspnea on exertion. History notable for type A thymoma resected 3 years earlier and recurrent sinopulmonary infections intermittently responsive to antibiotics, often occurring with diarrhea/IBS-D symptoms. On admission he had low-grade fever with otherwise normal vital signs and room-air oxygen saturation. Labs showed mild anemia, lymphopenia, and low albumin/protein. Extensive infectious workup was negative except induced sputum positive for Pneumocystis jiroveci and Moraxella catarrhalis. Cavitary lesion biopsy showed ulceration with acute and chronic inflammation, no malignancy. Immunologic testing showed absent pneumococcal antibody response, reduced lymphocyte proliferation to tetanus and candida, and marked B-cell lymphopenia.

A rare adult-onset combined immunodeficiency associated with thymoma, characterized by profound B-cell lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, impaired T-cell function, and recurrent bacterial and opportunistic infections.
symptoms_in_common: Poor or absent pneumococcal antibody response
Reduced lymphocyte proliferation to tetanus and Candida
symptoms_not_in_common: Cavitary pulmonary lesion is not a defining feature of Good syndrome itself, although it may result from an associated infection
Chills are nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.description: An opportunistic fungal pneumonia occurring primarily in patients with impaired cellular immunity; imaging commonly shows diffuse bilateral ground-glass pulmonary infiltrates, though atypical nodular or cavitary disease can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Induced sputum positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal room-air oxygen saturation despite respiratory symptoms is less typical in clinically significant PJP
Prominent cavitary lesion is uncommon in classic PJP
Recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections are not explained by PJP alone
Absent pneumococcal antibody response and marked B-cell lymphopenia indicate a broader immune defect

data.description: Mycobacterial infection of the lungs that can cause chronic constitutional symptoms and cavitary lung lesions, particularly in individuals from endemic regions or those with impaired immunity.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from Ethiopia, a country with higher tuberculosis prevalence
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive infectious workup was negative for tuberculosis
Induced sputum identified Pneumocystis jirovecii and Moraxella catarrhalis instead
Marked B-cell lymphopenia and absent vaccine antibody response are not caused by pulmonary tuberculosis alone
Biopsy showed nonspecific acute and chronic inflammation without granulomatous inflammation reported

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary infection due to Moraxella catarrhalis
data.description: A bacterial respiratory infection that may cause acute bronchitis, pneumonia, or exacerbations of chronic airway disease, especially in individuals with humoral immunodeficiency or recurrent respiratory infections.
symptoms_in_common: History of recurrent sinopulmonary infections intermittently responsive to antibiotics
symptoms_not_in_common: Night sweats and substantial weight loss are less typical of uncomplicated Moraxella infection
Cavitary lung lesion is unusual for Moraxella catarrhalis pneumonia
Pneumocystis jirovecii positivity indicates concurrent opportunistic infection
Chronic diarrhea and impaired T-cell proliferative responses are not explained by Moraxella infection alone

data.description: A primary antibody deficiency characterized by low immunoglobulins, poor vaccine responses, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sometimes reduced B-cell numbers; it can be complicated by chronic lung disease and opportunistic infections.
symptoms_in_common: Low albumin/protein suggesting possible chronic gastrointestinal disease or malnutrition
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior thymoma strongly favors Good syndrome over typical CVID
Reduced lymphocyte proliferation and Pneumocystis jirovecii infection suggest a more substantial combined T-cell defect than classic CVID
Cavitary lesion is not a typical primary manifestation of CVID
Night sweats and persistent fever suggest an active infection rather than CVID itself

data.description: A 26-year-old man presented with a firm, nontender palpable lymph node in his left cervical area. The patient had no specific past medical history. On admission, his vital signs were stable with blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and body temperature 36.5°C. Routine laboratory investigations showed a normal complete blood count, serum chemical tests, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Serologic tests for cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of mycobacteria yielded negative results. Serum immunoglobulin levels were within normal ranges: IgG 1,680 mg/dL (normal 700-1,700 mg/dL), IgA 117 mg/dL (normal 70-400 mg/dL), IgM 129 mg/dL (normal 40-230 mg/dL), and IgE 33.8 IU/mL (normal 0-100 IU/mL). The patient had no history of fever during the clinical course.

data.diagnosis: Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy)
data.description: A rare benign non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder, usually presenting with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Histology characteristically shows large S100-positive histiocytes with emperipolesis (intact lymphocytes within histiocyte cytoplasm), typically with negative or weak CD1a staining.
symptoms_in_common: Firm, painless cervical lymph node enlargement
Normal blood count and ESR can occur
Histology showing large histiocytes with apparent emperipolesis
Immunohistochemistry consistent with S100-positive histiocytic cells
symptoms_not_in_common: No marked massive bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy described
No extranodal skin, nasal, orbital, or bone involvement described

data.description: A malignant lymphoid neoplasm that commonly affects young adults and can present with painless cervical and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, weight loss, or other B symptoms
Normal ESR and routine laboratory results
Histology does not describe Reed-Sternberg cells or a typical Hodgkin lymphoma background
Histology instead suggests prominent histiocytic proliferation with emperipolesis

data.description: A clonal histiocytic disorder characterized by Langerhans cells, often involving bone, skin, lungs, or lymph nodes. The lesional cells are generally positive for CD1a and langerin and may be S100-positive.
symptoms_in_common: Potential S100 immunoreactivity in histiocytic cells
symptoms_not_in_common: No bone lesions, skin rash, pulmonary cystic disease, diabetes insipidus, or other common organ involvement
Painless isolated cervical lymphadenopathy is less characteristic
Emperipolesis is not typical of Langerhans cell histiocytosis
The immunohistochemical pattern shown is more consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease than CD1a/langerin-positive Langerhans cells

data.description: 26-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks’ gestation with monochorionic diamniotic twins, with history of childhood asthma, obesity, anxiety, depression, gestational diabetes, polyhydramnios in one fetus, and two prior uncomplicated pregnancies. Three weeks before presentation, after her children had an ear infection and sore throat, she developed eye erythema with greenish drainage, followed by nonproductive cough, sore throat, ear pain, and new leg edema. One week before admission, she developed progressive right leg pain. Initial exam showed pitting leg edema without erythema or warmth, tachycardia, and low blood pressure. Five days later she developed left leg tenderness with worsening bilateral edema, severe coughing episodes, expiratory wheezes, tachycardia, and continued low blood pressure with normal oxygen saturation. She then developed sudden severe crushing chest pain, became unresponsive and pulseless, and had cardiac arrest with monomorphic ventricular tachycardia.

Acute inflammation of the heart muscle caused by a viral infection, potentially producing severe ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, and cardiac arrest. The preceding conjunctivitis, pharyngitis, and respiratory illness are compatible with adenovirus infection.
symptoms_in_common: Recent conjunctivitis with greenish eye drainage
Recent sore throat, ear pain, and nonproductive cough
Pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions on chest imaging
No obstructive coronary lesion on coronary angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive focal right leg pain followed by left leg tenderness

data.description: Inflammation involving both the myocardium and pericardium, often after a viral respiratory infection. Severe myocardial involvement can cause heart failure, chest pain, arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Leg edema consistent with acute heart failure
Pulmonary congestion and pleural effusions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Eye erythema with greenish drainage
Ear pain
Progressive focal leg pain

data.description: Pregnancy-associated systolic heart failure that develops late in pregnancy or in the months after delivery. Twin gestation, obesity, gestational diabetes, and advanced hemodynamic stress of pregnancy may increase risk. Severe cases can cause pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock, and ventricular arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Cough and wheezing that may reflect pulmonary edema
Pulmonary edema and pleural effusions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctivitis with greenish drainage
Sore throat and ear pain preceding the cardiac illness
Progressive focal leg pain
Abrupt viral prodrome strongly preceding deterioration

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus, often arising from deep venous thrombosis. Pregnancy, obesity, twin pregnancy, and reduced mobility are important risk factors. Massive pulmonary embolism can cause shock and cardiac arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Three-week conjunctivitis and upper respiratory illness
Prominent wheezing and prolonged coughing episodes
Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia rather than the more typical pulseless electrical activity arrest
Normal oxygen saturation despite severe hemodynamic deterioration
Chest CT appearance not showing a pulmonary arterial embolus

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome from pregnancy-associated spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD)
data.description: SCAD is a nonatherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma of a coronary artery that can occur during pregnancy or postpartum and may cause myocardial infarction, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctivitis, sore throat, ear pain, and cough before the cardiac event
Progressive bilateral leg edema before chest pain
Wheezing and pulmonary congestion developing over several days
Normal coronary angiography without evidence of a coronary dissection or obstructive lesion
Progressive leg pain and tenderness

data.description: 73-year-old man with 2 days of worsening weakness, lethargy, chills, diarrhea, decreased oral intake, progressive confusion/irritability, and near-catatonia with inability to get out of bed; also recurrent epistaxis and chest/left arm pain. Past history: diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, prior exudative pericardial effusion that resolved spontaneously, hyperlipidemia, pancytopenia, obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, and headaches; lifelong recurrent epistaxis with family history in mother and daughter. Exam showed somnolence but easy arousability, waxing and waning attention, dry mucous membranes, dried blood around nares, multiple telangiectasias on the face/lips/trunk, nonblanching cherry angiomas on the chest, irregularly irregular heart rhythm, palpable liver edge 2 cm below the right costal margin, and chronic venous insufficiency changes in the legs. Admission labs showed anemia (Hgb 10.6 g/dL, Hct 31.7%), hypokalemia, elevated BUN/creatinine, prolonged PT/INR, mildly elevated ammonia, and a positive troponin T at 0.03 ng/mL.

An autosomal-dominant vascular disorder characterized by recurrent spontaneous epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectasias, and arteriovenous malformations in organs such as the liver, lungs, brain, and gastrointestinal tract.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of recurrent epistaxis in mother and daughter
Multiple telangiectasias on the face, lips, and trunk
Anemia consistent with recurrent blood loss
Possible hepatic vascular abnormalities on Doppler ultrasound and CT
History of high-output cardiovascular disease features including heart failure and pulmonary hypertension
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute diarrhea
Hypokalemia
Decreased oral intake and dry mucous membranes
Acute chest and left arm pain
Positive troponin

data.diagnosis: Hepatic arteriovenous malformations due to hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
data.description: Abnormal direct connections between hepatic arterial, portal venous, and hepatic venous vessels. Doppler findings may show turbulent, high-velocity, and abnormally pulsatile flow, while CT can demonstrate enlarged tortuous hepatic vessels. These shunts can cause high-output heart failure, portal hypertension, biliary ischemia, or encephalopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging findings suggestive of abnormal hepatic vascular shunting on color Doppler and CT
History of diastolic heart failure and pulmonary hypertension
Progressive confusion, lethargy, and near-catatonia that may reflect hepatic dysfunction or shunt-related encephalopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong epistaxis is due to systemic HHT rather than hepatic shunting alone
Diarrhea
Hypokalemia
Dry mucous membranes from poor intake
Chest and left arm pain
Recurrent nasal bleeding as the immediate presenting problem

data.description: A neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by impaired hepatic detoxification or portosystemic shunting, resulting in accumulation of neurotoxins such as ammonia. It commonly produces fluctuating attention, somnolence, confusion, irritability, and severe psychomotor slowing.
symptoms_in_common: Lethargy and inability to get out of bed
Prolonged PT/INR suggesting impaired hepatic synthetic function
Possible hepatic arteriovenous/portosystemic shunting on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent lifelong epistaxis
Facial and truncal telangiectasias
Diarrhea
Chest and left arm pain
Positive troponin
Hypokalemia and dehydration, which may precipitate encephalopathy but are not defining features

data.diagnosis: Acute metabolic encephalopathy from dehydration, diarrhea, acute kidney injury, and electrolyte disturbance
data.description: Acute delirium caused by systemic illness and metabolic derangements. Volume depletion from diarrhea and poor oral intake can produce prerenal azotemia, hypokalemia, weakness, and altered mental status, particularly in an older adult with cardiac and hepatic comorbidity.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated BUN and creatinine consistent with volume depletion or acute kidney injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong recurrent epistaxis
Family history of epistaxis
Multiple telangiectasias
Abnormal hepatic vascular imaging findings
Palpable liver edge
Mild hyperammonemia and prolonged PT/INR, which suggest an additional hepatic contribution

data.description: A 7-month-old female infant presented with a 2-month history of brown macules on the back and thighs, without prodromal erythema or trauma. Her birth history was unremarkable, and her growth and development were normal. Family history was unremarkable. Physical examination revealed 7 sharply marginated, irregularly shaped, polymorphic hyperpigmented macules of 10 to 15 mm in diameter, without scales, on the back and thighs. The hyperpigmented macules were of orange hue, with unevenness of the pigmentation. Vital signs were normal. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory test results, including complete blood cell count, liver function tests, and renal function, were normal.
A childhood form of cutaneous mastocytosis caused by increased mast cells in the skin, typically producing tan, brown, or orange-brown macules or patches on the trunk and proximal limbs.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple brown to orange-brown hyperpigmented macules
Lesions on the back and thighs
Normal complete blood count and liver and renal function tests
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported itching, flushing, blistering, or whealing after rubbing of lesions
No reported positive Darier sign
Lesions are described as sharply marginated and irregularly polymorphic rather than the more typical numerous round or oval macules

data.description: A benign non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis of infancy and childhood. Typical lesions are yellow-orange papules or nodules, but uncommon early or macular lesions may appear as flat orange-brown patches or macules.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are flat macules rather than the typical papules or nodules
No yellow coloration is specifically described
No facial or scalp lesions, which are common sites for juvenile xanthogranuloma
Multiple lesions are less typical than a solitary lesion

data.description: A self-limited non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis occurring in infants, characterized by asymptomatic red-brown, yellow-brown, or orange papules that may spread from the head to the trunk and limbs.
symptoms_in_common: Onset in the first year of life
symptoms_not_in_common: No lesions on the head, face, or neck, which are characteristic initial locations
Lesions are macules rather than the usual small papules
Only a limited number of relatively large 10 to 15 mm lesions are present

data.description: Flat, well-demarcated hyperpigmented patches caused by increased epidermal melanin. Multiple lesions can occur in otherwise healthy children but may warrant assessment for neurofibromatosis type 1 or other genetic syndromes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions appeared after birth rather than being clearly congenital or early persistent lesions
Orange hue and uneven pigmentation are less typical than the uniform light-brown color of café-au-lait macules
Irregular polymorphic shapes are less typical than smooth oval lesions
Lesion size of 10 to 15 mm is smaller than the usual neurofibromatosis diagnostic threshold of greater than 5 mm in prepubertal children

data.description: Residual darkening of the skin after dermatitis, infection, insect bites, trauma, or other inflammation; lesions may be brown and persist for weeks to months.
symptoms_in_common: No scale at the time of examination
Normal systemic examination and laboratory findings
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding erythema, rash, injury, insect bites, or trauma was reported
Orange-colored sharply marginated lesions are less typical
The lesions are multiple and morphologically similar without a reported triggering inflammatory process

data.description: A 17-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with constipation and bloodless vomiting for 3 weeks. The vomiting worsened after food ingestion. The patient was exhausted and underweight, although she did not suffer abdominal pain. At admission, the patient had unwillingly lost 10 kg over 2 years, resulting in a body mass index of 14. During this period, she started prevention medicine due to a loss of menstruation. The patient had no prior medical or surgical history. Blood tests revealed an increased sed rate (ESR) of 33 (normal range: 2-20) as the only outlier. A contrast-enhanced CT was ordered based on the acute exacerbating of vomiting and constipation, with ileus as the tentative diagnosis.

Mechanical compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and aorta, usually after loss of retroperitoneal fat from significant weight loss. The CT images show marked gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation with a narrowed aortomesenteric angle and distance.
symptoms_in_common: Marked underweight status with BMI of 14
Imaging evidence of gastric and proximal duodenal dilatation
Reduced aortomesenteric angle and distance on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain
Mildly elevated ESR

data.diagnosis: Anorexia nervosa or another restrictive eating disorder
data.description: A psychiatric eating disorder characterized by restricted caloric intake, low body weight, endocrine consequences of malnutrition, and potentially severe gastrointestinal dysmotility. Severe weight loss can precipitate superior mesenteric artery syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive 10 kg weight loss over two years
Vomiting may occur in advanced malnutrition or as a complication of associated superior mesenteric artery syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: No stated fear of weight gain or body-image disturbance
Weight loss is described as unwilling
Marked postprandial vomiting from apparent mechanical upper intestinal obstruction is not a core feature
CT evidence of duodenal compression is not explained by an eating disorder alone

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying due to impaired gastric motility, causing retention of food and gastric dilatation, nausea, vomiting, and early satiety. It may occur idiopathically or secondary to systemic disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Constipation is not a defining feature
No diabetes, neurologic disease, medication trigger, or prior surgery is reported
CT demonstrates a narrowed aortomesenteric angle and distance suggesting extrinsic duodenal compression rather than isolated gastric dysmotility
Amenorrhea is more consistent with severe malnutrition than primary gastroparesis

data.description: 41-year-old man with morbid obesity, hyperlipidemia, and prior cholecystectomy, status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 8 years earlier, presented with epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain worsened by eating, without melena or hematochezia. Exam showed abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding, and initial basic labs were unremarkable. He later developed 4 months of foul-smelling watery diarrhea 6–7 times daily with visible food particles, pale floating stools, increased flatus, and daily feculent eructation. He subsequently presented with progressive weakness, myalgias, muscle cramps, and marked weight loss from 95.3 kg to 72.6 kg, appearing cachectic and chronically ill with dry mucous membranes, feculent breath, and decreased skin turgor.

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula involving the gastric pouch and transverse colon after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
data.description: An abnormal communication between the gastric pouch and colon, allowing gastric contents to pass directly into the colon and colonic contents/gas to reflux into the stomach. The contrast study demonstrates a fistulous tract from the gastric pouch to the transverse/descending colon, and endoscopy shows an abnormal gastric opening.
symptoms_in_common: Visible undigested food particles in stool
Pale floating stools consistent with malabsorption
Progressive marked weight loss and cachexia
Weakness, myalgias, and muscle cramps due to malnutrition and electrolyte losses
Epigastric and left upper-quadrant pain worsened by eating
Dehydration signs including dry mucous membranes and decreased skin turgor
symptoms_not_in_common: No melena or hematochezia
Initially unremarkable basic laboratory tests

data.diagnosis: Marginal ulcer with fistulization into the colon
data.description: A marginal ulcer is a peptic ulcer near the gastrojejunal anastomosis after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Deep ulceration can rarely erode into adjacent structures, including the transverse colon, producing a gastrocolic fistula.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric mucosal abnormality/opening seen on endoscopy
Gastrocolic fistula demonstrated on contrast imaging
Diarrhea and malabsorption after fistula formation
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation is more characteristic of the resulting gastrocolic fistula than of an uncomplicated marginal ulcer
Watery diarrhea with visible food particles is not typical of an uncomplicated ulcer
No gastrointestinal bleeding symptoms such as melena or hematemesis
No rebound tenderness or guarding

data.diagnosis: Severe protein-calorie malnutrition and dehydration secondary to gastrointestinal fistula-associated malabsorption
data.description: Severe nutritional depletion and volume loss can occur when food bypasses normal intestinal digestion and absorption through a gastrocolic fistula, causing chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea-like stools, electrolyte abnormalities, and muscle wasting.
symptoms_in_common: Marked weight loss from 95.3 kg to 72.6 kg
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation is not explained by malnutrition alone and suggests an enteric fistula
Epigastric and left upper-quadrant pain worsened by eating suggests an underlying structural gastrointestinal lesion
Endoscopic fistulous opening and contrast passage into colon require a fistula diagnosis rather than isolated malnutrition

data.diagnosis: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) after altered Roux-en-Y anatomy
data.description: Excess bacterial colonization of the small bowel can occur after surgically altered gastrointestinal anatomy and may cause diarrhea, gas, malabsorption, steatorrhea-like stools, and weight loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation and feculent breath are unusual for SIBO alone
Visible food particles in stool are not a typical defining feature
A demonstrated fistulous tract between gastric pouch and colon is not caused by uncomplicated SIBO
Postprandial epigastric and left upper-quadrant pain is less typical

data.description: A 20-year-old woman with a history of asthma presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and sharp pains in her chest and neck. The pain worsened on deep inspiration. She had a cough producing small amounts of whitish sputum. She had experienced several previous asthma exacerbations and had not been using her inhalers regularly. On examination, her airway was patent with a generalized moderate wheeze in her chest, but no other obvious clinical signs. She could speak in full sentences and had normal oxygen saturations and temperature. She was mildly tachycardic and appeared slightly anxious. Blood tests showed a mild neutrophilia and elevated C reactive protein.
Free air in the mediastinum, often caused by alveolar rupture during coughing or an asthma exacerbation. Chest radiography may show subtle linear mediastinal air outlining the heart or great vessels.
symptoms_in_common: History of poorly controlled asthma with recurrent exacerbations
Chest radiograph appearance suggestive of subtle mediastinal air
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported palpable neck or chest subcutaneous emphysema
No reported Hamman sign
Mild neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein are not typical primary features

data.description: Acute worsening of reversible lower-airway obstruction, commonly causing wheeze, cough, chest tightness, and breathlessness. Poor adherence to inhalers is a common trigger.
symptoms_in_common: Normal oxygen saturation and ability to speak in full sentences, consistent with a non-severe exacerbation
symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp chest pain radiating to the neck
Pain worsened by deep inspiration
Possible mediastinal air on chest radiograph

data.description: Air in the pleural space causing partial lung collapse; it can occur as a complication of asthma and may produce acute pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea.
symptoms_in_common: Asthma as a potential risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized bilateral wheeze rather than unilateral reduced breath sounds
No hypoxemia
Chest radiograph does not show a clear pleural line or peripheral absence of lung markings
Neck pain is less typical

data.diagnosis: Acute bronchitis or lower respiratory tract infection triggering asthma
data.description: Inflammation of the bronchi, usually viral, can cause cough, sputum production, mild inflammatory-marker elevation, and worsening of underlying asthma.
symptoms_in_common: Asthma exacerbation potentially precipitated by respiratory infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest and neck pain
No fever
Normal oxygen saturation
No focal consolidation visible on chest radiograph

data.description: 47-year-old homeless man with 1 month of intermittent leg pain and paresthesias, starting in the toes and gradually spreading to the shins. History includes 33 years of intravenous heroin use with current use, hepatitis C infection, hypertension, 52 pack-year smoking history, and rare alcohol use. No family history of neuropathy. Exam: chronically ill-appearing, alert and oriented, afebrile, BP 170/110 mmHg. Cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, and skin exams were normal. Neurologic exam showed normal cranial nerves, strength, and reflexes, but unsteady gait with limited ambulation due to pain and decreased pinprick, light touch, and temperature sensation in both lower extremities.

A nutritional deficiency disorder, often related to malnutrition, poverty, malabsorption, or substance use, characterized by photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhea, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and peripheral neuropathic complaints.
symptoms_in_common: Homelessness and likely poor nutritional intake
Painful distal paresthesias beginning in the toes
Symmetric sensory loss in both lower extremities
Unsteady gait due to painful neuropathy
Photodistributed dermatitis on the hands/forearms resembling a glove-like eruption
Hyperpigmented scaly dermatitis around the neck consistent with a Casal necklace
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported diarrhea
No dementia, confusion, or major cognitive change
Normal strength and reflexes despite gait limitation

data.diagnosis: Hepatitis C-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia with peripheral neuropathy
data.description: An immune-complex vasculitic disorder associated with chronic hepatitis C that can cause painful distal sensory neuropathy, purpura, arthralgias, renal disease, and skin ulcers.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty walking because of neuropathic pain
Possible scattered skin lesions on the forearms
symptoms_not_in_common: The neck and hand dermatitis is photosensitive/scaly rather than classic palpable purpura
No reported arthralgias
No renal manifestations reported
No weakness or reduced reflexes
No systemic vasculitic symptoms such as fever or fatigue reported

data.diagnosis: Nutritional peripheral neuropathy due to vitamin B6, vitamin B12, thiamine, or other micronutrient deficiency
data.description: Malnutrition-related vitamin deficiencies can produce distal symmetric sensory neuropathy, burning pain, paresthesias, gait impairment, and sometimes skin or mucosal findings depending on the deficient nutrient.
symptoms_in_common: High risk of malnutrition because of homelessness and chronic heroin use
Pain beginning in the toes and extending toward the shins
Reduced pinprick, light-touch, and temperature sensation
Preserved motor strength early in a predominantly sensory neuropathy
symptoms_not_in_common: The characteristic photosensitive glove-like dermatitis and Casal-necklace-like neck rash are more specific for niacin deficiency than for most other vitamin deficiencies
No macrocytic anemia, glossitis, or cognitive impairment described
Reflexes are normal, whereas some nutritional neuropathies may reduce reflexes

data.description: Chronic arsenic exposure can cause painful peripheral neuropathy and characteristic skin changes, including diffuse hyperpigmentation, raindrop pigmentation, and palmar or plantar hyperkeratosis.
symptoms_in_common: Paresthesias and sensory impairment in a stocking distribution
Gait difficulty due to neuropathic pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No known arsenic exposure reported
No palmar or plantar hyperkeratosis described
No diffuse raindrop hyperpigmentation described
The neck rash resembles a Casal necklace rather than typical arsenic-related pigmentation
No gastrointestinal symptoms, anemia, or nail changes reported

data.description: 8-month-old male born at term, from a non-consanguineous family, with no relevant family history. He had two prior hospitalizations for bronchitis at 3 and 6 months of age, one with severe neutropenia that resolved without treatment. He presented with respiratory distress, fever, and fatigue. Examination showed no palpable lymph nodes or tonsillar tissue, bilateral lung crackles, and decreased breath sounds. Chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates without pleural effusion; labs showed low neutrophils percentage, marked lymphocytosis, and low IgG and IgM.

data.diagnosis: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA, Bruton agammaglobulinemia) due to BTK deficiency
data.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked BTK gene, leading to failure of B-cell maturation, profoundly reduced or absent mature B cells, very low immunoglobulins, and recurrent bacterial respiratory infections. The image demonstrates a BTK c.494G>A (p.Cys165Tyr) variant in the patient, absent/reduced BTK expression, and low-level maternal mosaicism.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with early-onset recurrent respiratory infections
Current pneumonia-like illness with fever, respiratory distress, crackles, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates
Relative/marked lymphocytosis, compatible with preserved T-cell numbers despite B-cell maturation failure
Transient severe neutropenia, which can occur during infections in XLA
BTK pathogenic variant shown on genetic testing
Markedly reduced BTK protein expression in patient monocytes on flow cytometry

data.description: A group of severe inherited immunodeficiencies characterized by major impairment of T-cell development or function, usually with secondary B-cell dysfunction and severe early-life infections.
symptoms_in_common: Absent or poorly developed lymphoid tissue can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lymphocytosis rather than the lymphopenia typical of many SCID forms
No reported opportunistic infections, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or failure to thrive
Imaging and molecular testing identify a BTK mutation and deficient BTK expression, supporting XLA instead
Low IgM is compatible with SCID but the selective B-cell maturation phenotype is more characteristic of XLA

data.description: A heterogeneous antibody-deficiency disorder with impaired antibody production, low IgG with low IgA and/or IgM, and recurrent sinopulmonary infections. It usually presents later in childhood or adulthood.
symptoms_in_common: Possible paucity of lymphoid tissue in severe antibody deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Very early presentation at 3 to 8 months of age is unusual for CVID
Complete absence of tonsils and palpable lymph nodes is more characteristic of XLA
A hemizygous pathogenic BTK variant directly supports XLA rather than CVID
Reduced BTK protein expression in the patient is not typical of CVID

data.diagnosis: Autosomal-recessive agammaglobulinemia or other early B-cell developmental defect
data.description: Rare inherited defects affecting B-cell development, such as defects in IGHM, CD79A, CD79B, BLNK, PIK3R1, or related pathways, can cause absent/very low B cells, hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent bacterial infections resembling XLA.
symptoms_in_common: Infantile onset of recurrent bacterial respiratory infections
Absent tonsils and nonpalpable lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: The patient has a demonstrated pathogenic BTK variant, which identifies the specific cause as X-linked agammaglobulinemia
Absent/reduced BTK expression is specifically consistent with BTK deficiency
The maternal low-level BTK variant mosaicism supports inheritance involving the X chromosome rather than a typical autosomal-recessive disorder

data.description: A 35-year-old patient presented to A&E with complaints of sudden onset pain in scrotum extending to perineum, scrotal swelling, loss of penile erection following sexual intercourse. On examination the patient had scrotal swelling and bruising at the base of the penis and scrotum, but no penile swelling.

data.diagnosis: Penile fracture (right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea rupture)
data.description: Acute rupture of the tunica albuginea surrounding an erect corpus cavernosum, usually during sexual intercourse. The MRI demonstrates a defect in the tunica albuginea of the right corpus cavernosum near the penile base with adjacent soft-tissue hematoma extending into the scrotum.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden pain during or immediately after sexual intercourse
Bruising at the base of the penis and scrotum
Imaging evidence of a right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea defect
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible penile shaft swelling, whereas many penile fractures cause marked penile swelling and deformity

data.diagnosis: Proximal penile fracture with extravasated hematoma into the scrotum
data.description: A subtype of penile fracture in which a proximal corporal tear near the penile root permits blood to track into the perineum and scrotal sac, potentially leaving the penile shaft relatively spared externally.
symptoms_in_common: Pain centered in the scrotum and perineum rather than the penile shaft
MRI showing a proximal right-sided corporal tunical defect
MRI and ultrasound evidence of soft-tissue/scrotal hematoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported penile bending, cracking sound, or obvious shaft deformity

data.diagnosis: Rupture of the superficial dorsal penile vein
data.description: Traumatic tearing of the superficial dorsal vein during intercourse can cause penile or scrotal bruising and hematoma and may clinically mimic penile fracture, but it does not produce a tunica albuginea defect.
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of erection is less characteristic
MRI demonstrates a defect of the tunica albuginea in the right corpus cavernosum, which supports true penile fracture rather than isolated venous rupture
No described dorsal penile cord-like swelling

data.diagnosis: Traumatic scrotal hematoma secondary to genital soft-tissue injury
data.description: Blood accumulation within scrotal soft tissues after trauma may cause painful scrotal enlargement and bruising. In this case, imaging indicates that the hematoma is secondary to a proximal corporal tear rather than an isolated scrotal injury.
symptoms_in_common: MRI evidence of hematoma extending into the scrotal sac
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of penile erection is not typical of an isolated scrotal hematoma
Pain began during sexual intercourse rather than direct scrotal trauma
MRI shows a right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea defect, indicating a penile source of bleeding

data.description: 8-year-5-month-old male with full-term birth to consanguineous Han parents, birth weight 2.5 kg. He has severe motor and cognitive developmental delay: never achieved head control or independent sitting, learned to roll over at age 5, and cannot speak or communicate. Examination showed myopathic facies, high-arched palate, nystagmus, generalized muscle weakness, marked hypotonia, absent deep tendon reflexes, bilateral knee and ankle contractures, and positive right Babinski sign with possible left Babinski sign. Serum CK was 1514 U/L.

An autosomal-recessive congenital muscular dystrophy caused most often by defective alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation. It combines severe congenital hypotonia and weakness, developmental impairment, eye abnormalities, elevated CK, and structural brain malformations.
symptoms_in_common: Severe congenital-onset hypotonia and generalized muscle weakness
Profound motor delay with inability to achieve head control or independent sitting
Nystagmus and probable ocular structural abnormalities on the images
Brain MRI showing marked ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus and cerebral structural abnormalities
Contractures of the knees and ankles
Consanguineous parents, supporting an autosomal-recessive disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Babinski sign is less typical of the predominantly peripheral neuromuscular presentation, although it may occur with severe brain involvement

data.description: A severe congenital muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy characterized by congenital muscular weakness, eye malformations, cobblestone cortical malformation, hydrocephalus, and profound developmental disability. It is usually autosomal recessive and can result from variants in POMT1, POMT2, POMGNT1, FKTN, FKRP, or related genes.
symptoms_in_common: Severe early-onset hypotonia and generalized muscle weakness
Failure to attain head control, sitting, or speech
Brain structural abnormalities on MRI compatible with a congenital malformation spectrum
symptoms_not_in_common: Survival to 8 years is less typical, because classic Walker-Warburg syndrome is often fatal in infancy or early childhood
The MRI does not clearly demonstrate the severe cobblestone lissencephaly/cerebellar hypoplasia usually expected in classic cases

data.description: An alpha-dystroglycanopathy causing congenital muscular dystrophy, intellectual disability, brain malformations, elevated CK, and sometimes ocular abnormalities. It is classically associated with FKTN variants and is most prevalent in Japan but can occur in other populations.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital or early-childhood muscle weakness and hypotonia
Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes
Brain MRI abnormalities including ventriculomegaly and cortical/white-matter abnormalities
Autosomal-recessive pattern supported by parental consanguinity
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe ocular abnormalities are generally more characteristic of muscle-eye-brain disease or Walker-Warburg syndrome
The patient is of Han Chinese ancestry rather than the more typical Japanese ancestry
The extremely severe inability to attain head control may be more severe than in many Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy cases

data.description: A recessive congenital muscular dystrophy due to laminin-alpha-2 deficiency, causing severe neonatal hypotonia, weakness, absent reflexes, contractures, and elevated CK. Brain MRI commonly shows diffuse white-matter signal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Generalized muscle weakness and myopathic facies
Severe motor delay and inability to sit independently
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound cognitive and communication impairment is less typical, as cognition is often relatively preserved in classic LAMA2-related disease
Nystagmus and major ocular abnormalities are not typical
Marked hydrocephalus/ventriculomegaly and cortical brain malformation are less characteristic
Positive Babinski sign is not a typical primary manifestation

data.description: A 69-year-old male patient presented with lower abdominal pain. Physical examination revealed a flat abdomen without varicose veins, soft abdomen, with a palpable 3 cm×4 cm hard mass in the left lower abdomen, positive lower abdominal tenderness without rebound tenderness. Bowel sounds were normal at 4 times per minute. The patient had a history of cataracts for over one year, denied history of coronary heart disease, diabetes, hypertension, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or other acute or chronic infectious diseases. He denied food or drug allergies, trauma, blood transfusion history, or other surgical history.

A rare malignant gland-forming tumor arising from the seminal vesicle, typically occurring in older men and presenting as a pelvic mass that may invade the bladder, prostate, or rectum. The pelvic location and glandular malignant cytology/histology support this consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable hard left lower abdominal/pelvic mass
Pelvic mass on CT in the region posterior/inferior to the bladder
Gland-forming malignant cells on cytology and histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hematuria
No reported urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, or obstructive urinary symptoms
No reported hematospermia
Cataracts are unrelated

data.description: Prostatic adenocarcinoma is a common malignancy in older men. Ductal variants can form glandular lesions near the prostatic urethra or bladder base and may present as a pelvic mass with malignant glandular cytology.
symptoms_in_common: Mass near the bladder base/prostate region on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported urinary obstruction, weak urinary stream, nocturia, or urinary retention
No reported hematuria
No reported bone pain or weight loss
The relatively discrete left pelvic mass is less typical of ordinary prostate adenocarcinoma
Cataracts are unrelated

data.description: Primary bladder adenocarcinoma is an uncommon gland-forming carcinoma of the bladder, often arising near the trigone or bladder dome and potentially producing a mass with malignant glandular cells in urine or aspirate cytology.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass adjacent to or involving the urinary bladder on CT
Malignant glandular architecture on tissue examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported gross or microscopic hematuria
No irritative urinary symptoms such as dysuria, urgency, or frequency
No reported recurrent urinary tract infections
No reported mucousuria
Cataracts are unrelated

data.diagnosis: Colorectal adenocarcinoma with pelvic extension or metastasis
data.description: Colorectal adenocarcinoma is a common gland-forming cancer in older adults and can present with lower abdominal pain and a pelvic mass when locally advanced or metastatic.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable hard pelvic/left lower abdominal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported change in bowel habits
Normal bowel sounds
No reported constipation, diarrhea, rectal bleeding, melena, or weight loss
No reported anemia or systemic symptoms
Imaging appearance centered in the bladder/prostate-seminal-vesicle region would be less typical for a primary colorectal tumor
Cataracts are unrelated
