data.description: 32-year-old woman with a history of dissociative and depressive disorders treated as an outpatient with multiple psychiatric medications, admitted to the emergency department for somnolence after a presumed suicide attempt. On arrival she was somnolent but otherwise physically unremarkable and hemodynamically stable, with GCS 11/15, BP 140/85 mmHg, pulse 90/min, temperature 37.3°C, respiratory rate 16/min, and normal oxygen saturation. Initial labs showed severe metabolic acidosis with marked hyperlactatemia and hyperosmolality: pH 7.22, bicarbonate 9.1 mmol/L, lactate 25.9 mmol/L, anion gap 23 mmol/L, and osmolality gap 84 mmol/kg.

Toxicity from propylene glycol, a solvent found in some intravenous medications and occasionally ingested products, causing high anion-gap metabolic acidosis, hyperosmolality, elevated osmolality gap, and lactic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Initially stable hemodynamic status can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented exposure to intravenous propylene-glycol-containing medication or propylene glycol product
No reported acute kidney injury
No reported seizures

data.description: Ethylene glycol is a toxic alcohol, commonly found in antifreeze, that produces an early osmolality gap followed by severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis as toxic metabolites accumulate.
symptoms_in_common: Initially relatively stable vital signs can be seen early after ingestion
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lactate elevation is less characteristic than glycolate-related acidosis
No reported calcium oxalate crystals in urine
No reported acute kidney injury or flank pain
No reported hypocalcemia
No known antifreeze exposure

data.description: Methanol is a toxic alcohol that causes an elevated osmolality gap early and severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis after metabolism to formic acid; neurologic and visual toxicity are common.
symptoms_in_common: Initially normal or near-normal vital signs may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No visual disturbances, blurred vision, or blindness reported
Very marked hyperlactatemia is not the usual primary abnormality
No known methanol-containing product exposure
No reported abdominal pain, headache, or vomiting

data.description: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis is severe lactic acidosis occurring after metformin overdose or accumulation, especially in renal failure, hypoxia, shock, or liver dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Severe metabolic acidosis with low bicarbonate
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked osmolality gap is not typical
No history of diabetes or metformin use is provided
No reported renal failure
No hypotension, shock, hypoxemia, or severe systemic illness reported

data.description: Cyanide toxicity inhibits cellular oxygen utilization and can rapidly cause severe lactic acidosis, altered consciousness, cardiovascular collapse, and respiratory failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked osmolality gap is not typical
No hypotension or cardiovascular collapse
No respiratory distress or hypoxemia
No seizures reported
No reported smoke inhalation, industrial exposure, or cyanide-containing substance exposure

data.description: 15-year-old girl with 6 weeks of lower abdominal pain that began midline, was sharp/crampy, worsened with movement and improved when lying down, then shifted to the right within 24 hours. Initial exam showed mild bilateral lower abdominal tenderness, greater on the right, with a soft nondistended abdomen and no rebound or guarding. Labs showed leukocytosis, anemia, and elevated CRP. She was discharged with presumed ruptured ovarian cyst. Six weeks later, she returned with recurrent similar pain, missed school, and increased waist size over 2 weeks. She had no fever, gastrointestinal, urinary, or vaginal symptoms. History was otherwise unremarkable; menarche had not occurred. Exam showed a firm, distended right lower abdomen with mild tenderness and Tanner stage 4 pubertal development. Repeat labs showed worsening leukocytosis, anemia, and markedly elevated CRP.

data.diagnosis: Ovarian yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor)
data.description: A highly malignant ovarian germ-cell tumor occurring mainly in children and adolescents. It typically presents as a rapidly enlarging unilateral adnexal mass with hemorrhage and necrosis. The pathology images are compatible with a yolk sac tumor, including reticular/microcystic architecture, Schiller-Duval body-like structures, and hyaline globules.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute lower abdominal and right-sided pelvic pain
Firm distended right lower abdomen consistent with a large adnexal mass
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated CRP, which can occur with tumor necrosis, hemorrhage, or inflammation
Imaging appearance of a large complex predominantly solid right adnexal mass with hemorrhagic/necrotic components
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No gastrointestinal symptoms
No urinary symptoms
Primary amenorrhea despite Tanner stage 4 pubertal development

data.description: A malignant ovarian germ-cell tumor that most often affects adolescents and young women. It usually forms a large unilateral solid ovarian mass and may cause abdominal pain, distension, and constitutional or inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Large unilateral pelvic or abdominal mass
Abdominal distension and increased waist size
Leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers can occur in advanced or necrotic tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked hemorrhagic and necrotic gross appearance is less characteristic than for a yolk sac tumor
No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or fatigue were reported
No menstrual irregularity after established menses; the patient has not yet had menarche

data.diagnosis: Juvenile granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
data.description: A sex-cord stromal ovarian tumor that occurs predominantly in children and adolescents. It may become large and present with abdominal pain or distension; many tumors produce estrogen and cause precocious puberty or abnormal uterine bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Age compatible with an adolescent ovarian tumor
Anemia may occur with tumor hemorrhage
Complex ovarian mass with cystic or hemorrhagic areas can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No vaginal bleeding
No precocious menstruation or estrogen-excess symptoms
Primary amenorrhea rather than early menarche or menstrual irregularity
Marked leukocytosis and CRP elevation are not typical primary features

data.diagnosis: Ovarian torsion involving a large ovarian neoplasm
data.description: Twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle, usually due to an enlarged ovary or ovarian mass, causing venous obstruction, edema, hemorrhagic infarction, and abdominal pain. The imaging appearance of a very large adnexal mass with possible twisted pedicle and hemorrhagic changes can suggest torsion complicating a tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Acute sharp crampy lower abdominal pain initially centered in the midline and then localizing to the right
Large right adnexal mass predisposes to torsion
Anemia may result from hemorrhagic infarction
Leukocytosis and elevated CRP can occur with ischemia and necrosis
Recurrent pain episodes can occur with intermittent torsion and detorsion
symptoms_not_in_common: The prolonged 6-week course with progressive abdominal enlargement is more suggestive of an underlying tumor than isolated torsion
No nausea or vomiting
No peritoneal signs such as rebound tenderness or guarding
No fever

diagnoses.title: Juvenile granulosa cell tumour unknown behaviour of unspecified site

data.description: 32-month-old Korean boy presented with irritability and fever. Born at 40 weeks gestation with 2.9kg birth weight via normal vaginal delivery to a healthy 28-year-old G3P2 mother. Had flexion deformity of both middle fingers at birth. Showed mild general hypotonia in early infancy with weak cry and poor sucking. History of epileptic seizures 6 times since age 15 months. Developmental delay: raised head at 7 months, sat at 26 months, not yet standing. Physical exam showed prognathism, low-set ears, small crashed nose, widely spaced incisors, round back. Demonstrated repeated stereotyped behavior like hitting chin with palm. Neurologic exam showed decreased muscle tone (grade IV/IV bilaterally) but normal deep tendon reflexes, no spasticity or pathologic reflexes, normal sensory function, and no meningeal signs.

An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency, resulting in dermatan/heparan sulfate accumulation. Severe forms cause progressive developmental delay, coarse facial features, skeletal deformities and joint contractures; leukocytes may show coarse granulations (Alder-Reilly-like inclusions) on peripheral smear.
symptoms_in_common: Male child with early-onset developmental delay
Generalized hypotonia and weak cry/poor sucking in infancy
Coarse/dysmorphic facial features including depressed nasal bridge, low-set ears and prognathism
Congenital flexion deformities/contractures of the fingers
Round back suggestive of skeletal involvement/kyphosis
Granular/inclusion-like abnormalities in leukocytes on the blood-smear images
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly is described
No recurrent respiratory or ear infections are described
No umbilical/inguinal hernia is described
Fever is not a characteristic primary manifestation

data.description: A severe autosomal-recessive lysosomal trafficking disorder caused by defective mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal enzymes. It produces congenital skeletal abnormalities, joint contractures, coarse facial features, severe developmental delay and cellular inclusions/vacuolation.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital flexion deformity of both middle fingers
Hypotonia, weak cry and poor feeding/sucking during infancy
Dysmorphic/coarse facial appearance with depressed nasal bridge, low-set ears and prognathism
Round back consistent with skeletal disease
Abnormal granular or vacuolated leukocyte appearance in the images, compatible with a lysosomal storage disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: The child does not have described severe growth failure
No gingival hypertrophy is described
No severe hip dislocation or diffuse skeletal dysplasia is reported
Survival and relatively limited systemic findings at 32 months may be less typical of classic severe I-cell disease
Fever is not a core manifestation

data.description: A lysosomal storage disease caused by beta-galactosidase deficiency, leading to GM1 ganglioside accumulation in the brain and other tissues. The late-infantile form causes hypotonia, developmental delay or regression, seizures, dysmorphic/coarse facial features and skeletal abnormalities; vacuolated lymphocytes may be present.
symptoms_in_common: Early hypotonia and delayed motor milestones
Skeletal findings including finger deformities and rounded back
Leukocyte inclusions/vacuolated appearance on blood-smear images
symptoms_not_in_common: No developmental regression is explicitly reported
No hepatosplenomegaly is described
No cherry-red macular spot or visual impairment is described
No marked macroglossia or gingival hypertrophy is described
Fever is not typical of the underlying disorder

data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disease due to alpha-mannosidase deficiency. It commonly causes developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, coarse facial features, skeletal deformities, hearing impairment, immune dysfunction and vacuolated lymphocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Developmental delay with profoundly delayed sitting and inability to stand
Dysmorphic/coarse facial features including low-set ears and depressed nasal bridge
Skeletal abnormalities including finger contractures and rounded back
Abnormal vacuolated or granular leukocytes in the blood-smear images
symptoms_not_in_common: No hearing loss is described
No recurrent bacterial infections or immune deficiency is described
No ataxia is described
No hepatosplenomegaly is described
Fever alone is nonspecific and not diagnostic

data.description: A rare autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency. It can cause progressive intellectual disability, hypotonia, seizures, coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, recurrent infections, behavioral problems and cytoplasmic vacuoles in leukocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Infantile hypotonia with poor feeding and weak cry
Skeletal abnormalities including finger deformities and rounded back
Leukocyte inclusion/vacuolation-like findings on peripheral blood images
symptoms_not_in_common: No angiokeratomas are described
No excessive sweating is described
No recurrent sinopulmonary infections are described
No hepatosplenomegaly is described
No progressive loss of acquired developmental skills is specifically reported

diagnoses.name: X-linked alpha-thalassemia/mental retardation syndrome
diagnoses.title: X-linked alpha thalassaemia with mental retardation

data.description: A previously healthy 58-year-old male presented with two weeks of lumbar pain and fever, accompanied by asthenia, anorexia, and recent weight loss of 3kg. He was a non-smoker with no drug abuse, recent travel, or animal contact history. On examination, he had a fever of 39.3°C with hemodynamic stability, bilateral painless swollen legs, and respiratory crackles on the right side. Laboratory tests showed hemoglobin 116 g/l, leukocyte count 33.3*109 cells/l, C-reactive protein 114.6mg/l, creatinine 56 μmol/l, elevated liver enzymes (AST 174 U/l, ALT 209 U/l, ALP 406 U/l, GGT 517 U/l), total bilirubin 76 μmol/l, conjugated bilirubin 66 μmol/l, and INR 1.38. Serology for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV were negative. Urinary sediment was unremarkable.

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic lumbar spondylodiscitis (vertebral osteomyelitis/discitis) with left psoas abscess
data.description: Bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates, often causing severe back pain, fever, inflammatory-marker elevation, and extension into the psoas muscle as an abscess. The CT appearance is consistent with lumbar disc/endplate involvement and an adjacent left psoas collection.
symptoms_in_common: CT evidence of lumbar vertebral/disc abnormality
CT evidence of an adjacent left psoas inflammatory collection/abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with markedly elevated cholestatic liver enzymes
Bilateral painless leg swelling
Right-sided respiratory crackles

data.description: A collection of pus within the iliopsoas muscle, usually caused by spread from nearby spinal, gastrointestinal, urinary, or pelvic infection. In this case, the psoas abnormality is likely secondary to adjacent lumbar spondylodiscitis.
symptoms_in_common: CT evidence of a left psoas collection
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjugated jaundice and markedly elevated liver enzymes
Bilateral painless leg edema
Right-sided respiratory crackles

data.diagnosis: Spinal epidural abscess complicating pyogenic vertebral infection
data.description: A purulent infection in the epidural space that may arise from vertebral osteomyelitis or bacteremia. It presents with fever and focal spinal pain and can progress to radicular pain, weakness, sensory loss, or bladder dysfunction; MRI is required to assess it reliably.
symptoms_in_common: CT evidence suggesting adjacent lumbar spinal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported neurologic deficit
No reported urinary retention, incontinence, or bowel dysfunction
Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and cholestatic liver-enzyme elevation
Bilateral painless leg swelling
Right-sided respiratory crackles

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott disease) with psoas abscess
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine can cause vertebral destruction, disc-space disease, paraspinal or psoas abscesses, and constitutional symptoms. It is an important differential diagnosis for spondylodiscitis with a psoas collection, although the acute high-grade inflammatory presentation favors pyogenic infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute two-week presentation
High fever of 39.3°C
Marked leukocytosis of 33.3 × 10^9/L
Markedly elevated C-reactive protein
No reported tuberculosis exposure or travel risk
Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with marked cholestatic liver-enzyme elevation
Bilateral painless leg edema

data.description: A 67-year-old man with advanced alcoholic cirrhosis presented with progressive dyspnea. Physical examination after thoracentesis revealed right lung crackles, and the patient developed coughing, tachypnea, and tachycardia. His oxygen saturation was 82% while breathing ambient air.

Acute noncardiogenic pulmonary edema occurring after rapid re-expansion of a chronically collapsed lung following thoracentesis or drainage of a large pleural effusion. Imaging commonly shows unilateral ground-glass and alveolar opacities in the re-expanded lung.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia with oxygen saturation of 82% on room air
Right-lung unilateral air-space/ground-glass opacities on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive dyspnea before the thoracentesis
Advanced alcoholic cirrhosis

data.description: Pulmonary infection or chemical pneumonitis caused by aspiration of gastric or oropharyngeal contents, often producing dependent unilateral consolidation and hypoxemic respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided pulmonary consolidation/air-space opacity on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset immediately after thoracentesis
No reported fever
No reported purulent sputum
No reported aspiration event
Advanced alcoholic cirrhosis

data.description: Infectious inflammation of lung parenchyma that may cause focal or multilobar consolidation, cough, crackles, tachypnea, and hypoxemic respiratory failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms developing directly after thoracentesis
No fever reported
No sputum production reported
No leukocytosis or infectious laboratory findings reported

data.description: Pulmonary interstitial and alveolar fluid accumulation due to elevated cardiac filling pressures, usually causing dyspnea, crackles, hypoxemia, and bilateral perihilar or diffuse pulmonary opacities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly unilateral right-lung opacity rather than typical bilateral edema
Temporal relationship to thoracentesis
No reported history of heart failure
No reported cardiomegaly or bilateral pleural effusions

data.description: 52-year-old woman with exertional right buttock and thigh pain that resolves within 2 minutes of rest. Exercise tolerance worsened over past year, now limited to several blocks. Previously able to run 5-6 miles per day. Recently diagnosed hypertension controlled with lisinopril (5 mg daily). No other cardiovascular risk factors. Physical exam shows blood pressure 124/76 mm Hg bilaterally, high-pitched systolic bruit over right subcostal region and umbilicus, normal peripheral pulses. Ankle brachial index (ABI) at rest borderline normal (0.91) on right and normal (1.03) on left. Remainder of examination normal.

data.diagnosis: Multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia involving the renal and right iliac arteries
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arteriopathy affecting medium-sized arteries, classically producing a 'string-of-beads' angiographic appearance from alternating stenoses and small aneurysmal dilatations. Renal artery involvement can cause hypertension, while iliac involvement can cause exertional claudication.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional right buttock and thigh pain relieved rapidly by rest
Normal peripheral pulses despite proximal arterial disease
Angiographic beading/alternating stenoses consistent with fibromuscular dysplasia
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical symptoms are clearly discordant; the presentation is consistent with renal and iliac artery involvement by fibromuscular dysplasia

data.diagnosis: Right external iliac artery fibromuscular dysplasia causing proximal lower-extremity claudication
data.description: Fibromuscular dysplasia of the external iliac artery may produce segmental arterial stenoses and beading, limiting blood flow to the buttock and thigh during exertion. It may occur with fibromuscular dysplasia in other vascular beds, particularly the renal arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral right buttock and thigh exertional pain
Rapid resolution of pain with rest
Reduced ability to exercise compared with baseline
Preserved distal pulses, which can occur with proximal iliac disease
Angiographic abnormality of the right iliac artery with a beaded stenotic appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertension is not directly explained by isolated external iliac artery disease
Right subcostal abdominal bruit suggests additional renal or visceral arterial involvement rather than isolated iliac disease

data.diagnosis: Renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia causing renovascular hypertension
data.description: Renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia is a common cause of secondary hypertension in women and typically has a multifocal 'string-of-beads' appearance on angiography. It may coexist with fibromuscular dysplasia in iliac, carotid, vertebral, or other medium-sized arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Woman in the typical demographic range for fibromuscular dysplasia
Angiographic beading of a renal artery consistent with multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia
Lack of major conventional atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Exertional right buttock and thigh claudication is not explained by renal artery disease alone
Borderline reduced right ABI is not expected from isolated renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia

data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of the aortoiliac arteries can cause buttock, hip, or thigh claudication due to reduced blood flow during exertion. It is more common in patients with smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or advanced age.
symptoms_in_common: Borderline reduced ABI on the symptomatic side
Abdominal bruit can occur with aortoiliac arterial stenosis
Hypertension is a vascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young woman with few atherosclerotic risk factors
No reported smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or known systemic atherosclerosis
Normal peripheral pulses despite symptoms
Angiographic string-of-beads morphology is more characteristic of fibromuscular dysplasia than atherosclerotic plaque
Renal artery beading is atypical for atherosclerosis

data.description: External iliac artery endofibrosis is a nonatherosclerotic arterial narrowing seen most often in high-level endurance athletes, particularly cyclists and runners. It causes exertional thigh, buttock, or leg symptoms, often with near-normal findings at rest.
symptoms_in_common: Previously high endurance exercise level, including running 5 to 6 miles daily
Progressive exertional thigh and buttock pain
Resting ABI that is only borderline abnormal
symptoms_not_in_common: New hypertension and an abdominal/right subcostal bruit are not typical features
Renal artery involvement is not explained by endofibrosis
Angiographic multifocal beading is more typical of fibromuscular dysplasia than endofibrosis
Endofibrosis is classically associated with competitive cycling and usually affects the external iliac artery without systemic arterial involvement

data.description: A 66-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with episodes of palpitations, dizziness, and near fainting that had lasted for a few hours. Her medical history included removal of a left atrial myxoma 15 years ago, after which she experienced recurrent atrial tachycardia managed with modified release verapamil 240 mg once daily. She had recently started sotalol 120 mg twice daily in addition to verapamil and underwent direct current cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia one week prior to presentation. Initial workup showed normal urea and electrolytes including magnesium. An echocardiogram revealed normal left ventricular systolic function with no recurrence of left atrial myxoma.

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced torsades de pointes (polymorphic ventricular tachycardia due to QT prolongation)
data.description: A potentially life-threatening polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that occurs in the setting of a prolonged QT interval. In this case, sotalol, potentiated by concomitant verapamil-related bradycardia, is a strong precipitating factor. The ECG shows prolonged repolarization followed by a rapid polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia with changing QRS axis/amplitude, consistent with torsades de pointes.
symptoms_in_common: Recent initiation of sotalol, a QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic
Concurrent verapamil use, which can contribute to bradycardia and increase torsades risk
Recent cardioversion, with possible post-cardioversion bradycardia
ECG appearance consistent with prolonged QT followed by polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Normal electrolytes do not exclude drug-induced torsades de pointes
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented loss of consciousness
No reported cardiac arrest
No reported chest pain

data.description: An acquired prolongation of ventricular repolarization caused by medications, particularly class III antiarrhythmics such as sotalol. It predisposes to early afterdepolarizations and torsades de pointes, especially in older women and in the presence of bradycardia or concomitant rate-slowing drugs.
symptoms_in_common: Sotalol 120 mg twice daily was started recently
Female sex and older age, both risk factors for drug-induced QT prolongation
ECG evidence of marked QT prolongation before the ventricular arrhythmia
Normal magnesium and other electrolytes, supporting a medication-related rather than electrolyte-mediated cause
symptoms_not_in_common: Acquired long QT syndrome itself may be asymptomatic until an arrhythmia occurs
No documented family history of congenital long QT syndrome
No known congenital deafness or prior lifelong syncope history

data.description: A supraventricular tachyarrhythmia arising from an atrial focus or re-entry circuit. This patient has a prior history of recurrent atrial tachycardia after left atrial myxoma surgery and recently required cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent persistent atrial tachycardia requiring direct-current cardioversion
symptoms_not_in_common: The image shows a polymorphic wide-complex ventricular tachycardia rather than a typical narrow-complex atrial tachycardia
Marked QT prolongation is not a typical feature of atrial tachycardia
The acute event occurred after starting sotalol, favoring drug-induced ventricular arrhythmia
Near-syncope is more concerning for ventricular tachycardia than for stable atrial tachycardia

data.description: 18-year-old pregnant woman. Healthy with no history of smoking, drug abuse, or family history of chromosomal disease or encephalodysplasia. Experienced mild flu-like symptoms during first month of pregnancy that resolved after three days without medication.

30-year-old male with 6 weeks of low-grade fever, fatigue, and progressive polyarthritis of the large joints of the arms and legs, without small joint involvement or diurnal variation. No significant past history; denied tuberculosis contact and high-risk sexual behavior. Exam showed fever (38.9°C), multiple dull red tender nodules on the forehead, left cheek, and sternum, a solitary 1 cm firm right cervical lymph node, bilateral active arthritis of the knees, hips, and elbows, and a palpable liver 4 cm below the right costal margin. Labs: normal blood count, ESR 6 mm/h, CRP 131 mg/L, negative ANA, RF, ANCA, ASO, anti-DNase B, blood cultures, gonococcal and syphilis tests; calcium and ACE were normal.

A multisystem granulomatous inflammatory disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas. The chest radiograph suggests bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and the skin biopsy is consistent with noncaseating granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Acute progressive polyarthritis involving large joints
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph
Noncaseating granulomas with giant cells on skin histology
Negative ANA, rheumatoid factor, and ANCA
symptoms_not_in_common: No respiratory symptoms were reported despite thoracic lymph node involvement
The skin nodules are on the face and sternum rather than the more typical lower legs

data.description: An acute sarcoidosis phenotype classically characterized by bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, acute ankle-predominant arthritis or periarthritis, and fever.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Arthritis involves knees, hips, and elbows rather than predominantly the ankles
Skin nodules are located on the forehead, cheek, and sternum rather than typically on the shins
Cervical lymphadenopathy and hepatomegaly are less characteristic of classic Lofgren syndrome

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with cutaneous and musculoskeletal involvement
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can produce fever, lymphadenopathy, granulomatous skin lesions, hepatomegaly, and inflammatory arthritis; tissue granulomas are often caseating but may occasionally appear noncaseating.
symptoms_not_in_common: No tuberculosis contact history
No reported cough, weight loss, night sweats, or pulmonary infiltrates
Polyarthritis of several large joints is less typical than monoarthritis in osteoarticular tuberculosis
The biopsy appearance is more consistent with noncaseating sarcoidal granulomas than typical caseating tuberculosis granulomas

data.diagnosis: Disseminated fungal infection causing granulomatous disease
data.description: Disseminated fungal infections, such as histoplasmosis, can cause fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, skin lesions, and granulomatous inflammation, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
symptoms_not_in_common: No immunosuppression or relevant exposure history was reported
Normal blood count is less suggestive of disseminated fungal infection
Prominent symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis is not a typical dominant manifestation
Histology does not describe fungal organisms or necrotizing granulomas

data.description: A rare systemic histiocytic disorder causing papulonodular skin lesions and destructive inflammatory polyarthritis, usually affecting the hands and face and often associated with malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Constitutional symptoms including fever and fatigue
symptoms_not_in_common: No small-joint or hand involvement
No erosive or destructive arthritis was described
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is not typical
Skin histology shows granulomas with giant cells rather than the characteristic histiocytic ground-glass appearance
Hepatomegaly is not a typical presenting feature

data.description: 13-year-old girl with a multiply recurrent hypothalamic/chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases. Had never received steroids or bisphosphonates. After 16 courses of treatment, complained of wrist pain. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation of the left dorsal wrist with decreased range of motion.

data.diagnosis: Kienböck disease (avascular necrosis/osteonecrosis of the lunate)
data.description: Osteonecrosis of the lunate bone caused by impaired blood supply. The coronal wrist MRI shows abnormal low marrow signal in the lunate relative to the surrounding carpal bones, supporting lunate osteonecrosis.
symptoms_in_common: MRI abnormality centered in the lunate
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical traumatic precipitant is described
Underlying recurrent hypothalamic-chiasmatic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases is not a usual presenting feature

data.description: Medication- or cancer-treatment-associated impairment of bone vascularity can cause focal osteonecrosis. In this case, the imaging appearance is most consistent with lunate osteonecrosis, while the absence of corticosteroid or bisphosphonate exposure suggests another treatment-related or multifactorial mechanism.
symptoms_in_common: New focal wrist pain during prolonged oncologic treatment
Abnormal low signal within the lunate on MRI compatible with osteonecrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior steroid exposure
No prior bisphosphonate exposure
No multifocal bone or joint pain is described

data.diagnosis: Lunate stress injury or occult fracture
data.description: An occult carpal stress injury can produce wrist pain, tenderness, and marrow-signal abnormality on MRI. However, the relatively diffuse low signal of the lunate and the clinical context favor osteonecrosis over a fracture.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal MRI appearance involving a carpal bone
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute trauma or repetitive overuse history is reported
No discrete fracture line is evident on the provided MRI image
The imaging pattern is more suggestive of lunate osteonecrosis than a focal fracture

data.description: 10-month-old male admitted with fever. Born at 38 weeks gestation after unremarkable pregnancy, birth weight 2,960g. History of cephalhematoma over parietooccipital region at birth, bilateral inguinal hernia repair at 2 months, recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection. Growth parameters below 3rd percentile (weight: 7,500g, length: 73.7cm). Physical exam showed pale skin, sparse/light/curly hair with pili torti on microscopy. Neurologic exam revealed diffuse hypotonia with poor head/trunk support, no visual fixing/following, hyperreflexic deep tendon reflexes bilaterally with ankle clonus, bilateral Babinski extension. Lab results: serum copper 27 μg/dL (normal 70-130), ceruloplasmin 9.07 μg/dL (normal 20-60).

An X-linked disorder of copper transport causing systemic copper deficiency, impaired copper-dependent enzymes, neurodegeneration, characteristic sparse/kinky hair, vascular tortuosity, and failure to thrive.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with onset in the first year of life
Sparse, light, curly hair with pili torti on microscopy
Poor growth and weight/length below the 3rd percentile
Diffuse hypotonia and poor head/trunk control
Hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral extensor Babinski responses
Recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection
MRI evidence of bilateral white-matter diffusion restriction/ischemic injury
MR angiographic appearance of markedly tortuous cerebral arteries
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a primary manifestation of Menkes disease, although it may occur with an intercurrent infection

data.diagnosis: Occipital horn syndrome (mild ATP7A-related copper transport disorder)
data.description: A milder allelic form of ATP7A-related copper transport disease, characterized by connective-tissue abnormalities, vascular tortuosity, bladder diverticula, lax skin/joints, and sometimes low copper and ceruloplasmin.
symptoms_in_common: Tortuous cerebral arteries on MR angiography
Hypotonia and developmental impairment can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe early infantile neurologic deterioration
Marked sparse light curly hair with pili torti
Severe failure to thrive
Prominent pyramidal signs including hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski extension
Bilateral acute-appearing white-matter ischemic lesions
No occipital horns or other characteristic skeletal findings are described

data.description: Copper deficiency due to inadequate intake, malabsorption, excessive zinc exposure, or prolonged parenteral nutrition; it can cause low serum copper and ceruloplasmin, anemia, impaired growth, and neurologic dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and neurologic developmental impairment can occur
Recurrent infections may occur in severe deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti and characteristic sparse kinky/light hair
Congenital connective-tissue features such as cephalhematoma and early inguinal hernias
Marked tortuosity of cerebral arteries
Typical early severe X-linked neurodegenerative presentation
Bilateral ischemic white-matter lesions related to vascular fragility
No history of malnutrition, malabsorption, zinc exposure, or prolonged parenteral nutrition is provided

data.description: 47-year-old female with an incidentally discovered right adrenal mass noted 3 years ago, initially 2.2 × 3.1 cm and untreated, now enlarged on CT 10 days ago to 5.8 × 4.7 cm. She remained asymptomatic throughout. Past history negative for hypertension, diabetes, cardiac, pulmonary, and cerebrovascular disease; no smoking or alcohol use; reports reduced menstrual flow. Physical examination was normal, with stable vital signs and no abdominal mass, tenderness, or renal percussion pain.

A rare adrenal cortical tumor composed of oncocytic cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. Most are nonfunctioning and are discovered incidentally; they may become large and can appear heterogeneous on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Normal vital signs and no hypertension
Large unilateral right adrenal lesion with progressive enlargement
Imaging appearance of a well-defined heterogeneous adrenal mass
Histology showing cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature of a nonfunctioning adrenal oncocytoma

data.description: A common benign tumor of the adrenal cortex. Many adenomas are nonfunctioning incidentalomas, although some produce cortisol or aldosterone.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of diabetes or overt Cushingoid symptoms
No abdominal pain or palpable abdominal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked growth from approximately 3 cm to nearly 6 cm over 3 years is less typical for a benign adenoma
Large heterogeneous appearance is less typical than the usually small homogeneous lipid-rich adenoma
Eosinophilic oncocytic histologic appearance is not typical of a conventional adrenal adenoma
Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical finding

data.description: A catecholamine-producing tumor arising from adrenal medullary chromaffin cells. It may be incidentally detected and can be radiologically heterogeneous, especially when large; some tumors are biochemically silent.
symptoms_in_common: Potentially heterogeneous large adrenal mass on CT
May occasionally be asymptomatic if nonfunctioning or minimally secreting
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No episodic headache
No palpitations
No diaphoresis
No tremor or panic-like episodes
Histology shown is more suggestive of oncocytic adrenal cortical cells than classic pheochromocytoma architecture
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical

data.description: A rare malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that often presents as a large enlarging adrenal mass. It may be hormonally functional or nonfunctioning and can cause symptoms from hormone secretion or local invasion.
symptoms_in_common: Large adrenal mass greater than 4 cm
Substantial interval growth over several years
May be clinically silent when nonfunctioning
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal or flank pain
No palpable abdominal mass
No hypertension, diabetes, or Cushing syndrome features
No virilization or other overt androgen-excess manifestations
No evidence provided of local invasion, metastases, or lymphadenopathy
Reduced menstrual flow alone is not a typical specific presentation

data.description: 34-year-old white male presented with an indurated plaque on the forehead that extended onto the scalp over approximately 1 year. Initial laboratory findings showed positive antinuclear antibodies (1:200) and slightly increased C3d complement; other laboratory tests were normal.

A chronic cutaneous lupus variant causing lymphocytic inflammation of subcutaneous fat, often producing firm indurated plaques, lipoatrophy, and scalp alopecia. The biopsy appearance of deep lymphocytic inflammation involving adipose tissue supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive indurated plaque over approximately 1 year
Localized alopecia over the scalp lesion
Histology showing deep inflammatory infiltrates involving subcutaneous fat
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical discoid lupus surface scale, follicular plugging, or dyspigmentation was described
No systemic lupus symptoms or other abnormal laboratory findings were reported

data.diagnosis: Linear morphea (linear scleroderma, including en coup de sabre variant)
data.description: A localized scleroderma subtype characterized by a linear band of skin thickening and fibrosis, commonly affecting the forehead and scalp in the en coup de sabre pattern and potentially causing hair loss.
symptoms_in_common: Scalp hair loss within the involved area
Clinical distribution compatible with a linear forehead/scalp lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy shows prominent deep inflammatory involvement of fat, which is more characteristic of lupus panniculitis than uncomplicated morphea
Positive antinuclear antibodies are possible but not a defining feature
The lesion appears erythematous and infiltrated rather than clearly depressed, ivory-colored, or markedly sclerotic

data.description: A deep form of localized scleroderma involving the dermis, subcutis, fascia, or muscle, causing firm bound-down plaques and sometimes atrophy.
symptoms_in_common: Potential involvement of deeper skin and subcutaneous tissues
Forehead and scalp involvement can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymphocyte-rich lobular panniculitis on biopsy is less typical than dermal and septal fibrosis
Localized scalp alopecia is less characteristic than in lupus panniculitis or linear scleroderma
Positive ANA may occur but is not specifically diagnostic

data.diagnosis: Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp
data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus disorder that commonly affects sun-exposed skin and scalp, producing inflammatory plaques and potentially permanent scarring alopecia.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is described primarily as deeply indurated rather than as a scaly discoid plaque
No adherent scale, follicular plugging, dyspigmentation, or classic atrophic scarring was described
Deep subcutaneous fat inflammation on biopsy favors lupus panniculitis over isolated discoid lupus

data.description: A rare cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that infiltrates subcutaneous adipose tissue and can clinically resemble inflammatory panniculitis, often with persistent plaques or nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous inflammatory infiltrate involving adipose tissue on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Forehead and scalp localization is less typical than lesions on the trunk or extremities
No systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, fatigue, or hepatosplenomegaly were reported
Positive ANA and the overall clinicopathologic context favor an autoimmune lupus panniculitis process
No atypical lymphocytes, adipocyte rimming by neoplastic cells, or cytotoxic lymphoma features were described

data.description: A 14-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain for 2 days, accompanied by non-bilious vomiting. Physical examination revealed pallor, diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding, and sluggish bowel sounds but no rigidity. Her recent history included two episodes of multiple oral ulcers that had resolved spontaneously. Laboratory findings showed hemoglobin 88 g/L, total leucocyte count 3.6 × 10⁹/L, platelets 96 × 10⁹/L, and ESR 54 mm/h. Urinalysis was normal, and blood and urine cultures were sterile. Initial ANA testing by indirect immunofluorescence with HEp-2 cell substrate was negative. Subsequent repeat ANA testing at a different laboratory remained negative, but dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies were strongly positive with low concentrations of C3 and C4. Echocardiography showed a mild pericardial effusion.

data.diagnosis: ANA-negative systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus enteritis (mesenteric vasculitis) and intussusception
data.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus can rarely be ANA-negative by indirect immunofluorescence, particularly when other lupus-specific antibodies are present. Lupus enteritis results from immune-complex-mediated small-vessel inflammation and bowel-wall edema, which may cause obstruction or intussusception. The imaging is consistent with dilated bowel loops and bowel-wall edema/target appearance compatible with intussusception or lupus enteritis.
symptoms_in_common: Severe diffuse abdominal pain with guarding
Sluggish bowel sounds and radiographic bowel dilatation suggesting intestinal obstruction
CT appearance of bowel-wall edema and target-like bowel configuration compatible with intussusception/lupus enteritis
Low C3 and C4 complement levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeatedly negative ANA by HEp-2 indirect immunofluorescence is unusual for SLE, although rare ANA-negative cases occur
Normal urinalysis without evidence of lupus nephritis

data.description: Intussusception is telescoping of one segment of bowel into another, causing bowel obstruction, vomiting, abdominal pain, and a target-like appearance on CT. In lupus, bowel-wall edema from mesenteric vasculitis can act as a transient lead point.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe abdominal pain for 2 days
Abdominal radiograph showing dilated bowel loops
CT target-like configuration suggestive of intussusception
No documented infectious growth in blood or urine cultures
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent oral ulcers
Leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and anemia
Strong anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibody positivity
Low complement levels
Pericardial effusion
Elevated ESR
Negative ANA testing

data.description: Behçet disease is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis characterized primarily by recurrent oral and genital ulceration, ocular inflammation, skin lesions, and sometimes intestinal ulceration causing abdominal pain or obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported recurrent genital ulcers
No ocular inflammation or uveitis
No characteristic skin lesions
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are not typical core features
Strong anti-dsDNA antibody positivity is not typical
Low C3 and C4 complement levels are not typical
Pericardial effusion is less typical
CT evidence favoring diffuse bowel-wall edema/intussusception rather than characteristic ileocecal ulceration

data.diagnosis: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura) with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: IgA vasculitis is a small-vessel vasculitis in children that can cause colicky abdominal pain, bowel-wall edema, gastrointestinal bleeding, and intussusception. It is usually associated with palpable purpura, arthralgia, and sometimes renal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Bowel-wall edema and possible intussusception on CT
Normal urinalysis can occur early in the disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable purpura described
No arthralgia or arthritis described
No gastrointestinal bleeding reported
Recurrent oral ulcers are not typical
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are not typical
Strong anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro positivity are not typical
Low complement levels are not typical
Pericardial effusion is not typical

data.description: 41-year-old woman with recurrent chest pain: 1 year of intermittent left-sided chest and shoulder tightness, then 5 days before presentation acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders with dyspnea during exertion, lasting 1 hour and resolving spontaneously; the day before presentation, similar pain recurred with walking, accompanied by light-headedness and dyspnea. History includes laparoscopic ovarian cyst surgery and miscarriage 1 month earlier. Family history notable for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in multiple first-degree relatives and a maternal cousin who died of cerebral aneurysm at 51. On examination, she was diaphoretic; vitals were stable, and there were no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Troponin T increased from 0.03 to 0.21 ng/mL over 8 hours.

data.diagnosis: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) of the left anterior descending coronary artery
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma within a coronary artery wall that narrows the true lumen and can cause myocardial ischemia or infarction. The coronary angiogram is compatible with a long, smooth narrowing/dissection of the LAD.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Rising troponin T consistent with myocardial injury
Recent miscarriage, a hormonal/pregnancy-associated setting linked to SCAD
symptoms_not_in_common: One year of intermittent left-sided chest and shoulder tightness is longer than the usual acute presentation of a single SCAD event

data.diagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) secondary to SCAD
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction caused by reduced coronary blood flow without persistent diagnostic ST-segment elevation. In this case, the likely mechanism is LAD spontaneous coronary artery dissection rather than atherosclerotic plaque rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal exertional chest pain lasting approximately 1 hour
Pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Dynamic rise in troponin T from 0.03 to 0.21 ng/mL
ECG changes compatible with myocardial ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: A year of intermittent chest and shoulder tightness is less typical of an acute NSTEMI episode

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder that commonly affects renal and cerebrovascular arteries and is strongly associated with SCAD. The abdominal vascular images show multifocal arterial irregularity/beading compatible with renal-artery FMD.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary artery dissection/long LAD narrowing on angiography, which is strongly associated with FMD
Chest pain and myocardial infarction symptoms due to possible coronary involvement
Possible vascular-family-history signal, including a relative with cerebral aneurysm
symptoms_not_in_common: Jaw-radiating exertional chest pain is not a typical direct symptom of renal FMD unless coronary dissection occurs
Dyspnea and diaphoresis are not typical primary symptoms of renal FMD
No hypertension, headache, pulsatile tinnitus, flank pain, or known stroke symptoms are reported

data.diagnosis: Vascular connective-tissue disorder, including vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
data.description: Inherited connective-tissue disorders can predispose to arterial fragility, aneurysm, and spontaneous arterial dissection. Although the family history specifically reports hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, the combination of arterial dissection and a family history of cerebral aneurysm warrants consideration of a vascular connective-tissue disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in multiple first-degree relatives
Relatively young age for acute coronary syndrome without described atherosclerotic risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported easy bruising, translucent skin, characteristic facial features, organ rupture, or prior major arterial rupture
No reported joint hypermobility or skin hyperextensibility in the patient
Dyspnea, diaphoresis, and elevated troponin are consequences of myocardial ischemia rather than typical primary connective-tissue-disorder symptoms

data.description: Patient is a 2 month-old male, full-term infant, with severe malnutrition and failure to thrive, admitted to the intensive care unit, with long term feeding difficulties. The study was performed initially to rule out malrotation.

A rare esophageal motility disorder caused by impaired relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter. The contrast study appearance is consistent with a dilated esophagus and smooth distal tapering at the gastroesophageal junction ("bird-beak" appearance), with delayed passage into the stomach.
symptoms_in_common: Contrast-study evidence of esophageal dilatation with distal narrowing
symptoms_not_in_common: No regurgitation or vomiting is reported
No recurrent aspiration pneumonia or chronic cough is reported

data.description: A congenital fixed narrowing of the esophagus, often in the distal esophagus, which can cause impaired swallowing, proximal esophageal dilatation, feeding intolerance, and poor weight gain in infancy.
symptoms_in_common: Possible proximal esophageal dilatation on contrast imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The smooth tapered distal narrowing on imaging is more characteristic of achalasia than a short fixed stenosis
No dysphagia, choking, or recurrent respiratory infections are specifically reported

data.description: Narrowing of the esophageal lumen, usually acquired from reflux injury, caustic exposure, infection, or prior instrumentation. It may produce feeding intolerance and poor growth due to obstruction of swallowed feeds.
symptoms_in_common: Possible impaired passage of contrast through the distal esophagus
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of caustic ingestion, severe reflux, surgery, or esophageal instrumentation is provided
The diffuse esophageal dilatation and tapered gastroesophageal-junction narrowing favor achalasia over an acquired stricture
No painful swallowing or food impaction is reported

data.description: 47-year-old man with hypertension presented with 3 days of left periorbital swelling, throat tightness, hoarseness, and dysphagia to solids with a sensation of food sticking. He denied pain, pruritus, visual symptoms, dyspnea, wheezing, fever, or recent illness. Exam showed faint erythema and edema around the left eye, mildly diffusely enlarged tongue, hoarse muffled voice, and no stridor; extraocular movements and pupils were normal. Two weeks later, he developed worsening dysphonia, increased throat swelling, nasal regurgitation of liquids, shoulder and hip pain, and proximal weakness with difficulty jumping and rising from a seated position. Re-exam showed anterior/lateral neck tenderness, subcutaneous edema in both upper arms, normal arm strength, and reduced hip strength. Labs revealed elevated ALT, AST, and markedly elevated creatine kinase, mild ESR/CRP elevation, positive ANA, and negative myositis-specific antibodies. Left deltoid biopsy showed mild fiber size variability, perivascular inflammatory infiltrate, and patchy MHC class I staining on nonnecrotic fibers.

data.diagnosis: Dermatomyositis with prominent facial, pharyngeal, and subcutaneous edema (edematous dermatomyositis)
data.description: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by immune-mediated skeletal-muscle inflammation, typically causing proximal weakness, elevated creatine kinase, dysphagia, and characteristic skin findings. Rarely, marked periorbital, facial, limb, and upper-airway edema can be a presenting feature. The MRI pattern of diffuse edema in facial, tongue, pharyngeal, and cervical muscles and the biopsy showing perivascular inflammation and MHC class I expression support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Periorbital erythema and edema resembling a heliotrope eruption
Tongue, pharyngeal, soft-palate, and neck swelling
Nasal regurgitation of liquids from pharyngeal muscle involvement
Proximal muscle weakness, especially reduced hip strength and difficulty rising from a chair
Subcutaneous edema of the upper arms
Elevated AST and ALT consistent with muscle injury
MRI evidence of diffuse inflammatory edema in facial, masticatory, tongue, pharyngeal, and cervical muscles
Muscle biopsy with perivascular inflammatory infiltrates and patchy MHC class I staining on nonnecrotic fibers
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of a clear Gottron papule or Gottron sign
No reported photosensitive shawl sign, V-sign, or holster rash
Initial unilateral rather than bilateral periorbital edema
No pruritus
Normal arm strength despite clinically apparent upper-arm edema

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy causing symmetric proximal skeletal-muscle weakness, myalgia, elevated muscle enzymes, and possible bulbar or pharyngeal muscle involvement. It may occur with positive ANA and may lack myositis-specific antibodies, although the marked edema and periorbital changes favor dermatomyositis over classic polymyositis.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty rising from a seated position and jumping
Dysphonia and hoarseness due to pharyngeal or laryngeal muscle involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital erythema and edema, which is more characteristic of dermatomyositis
Prominent facial, tongue, and subcutaneous edema
Marked upper-airway and floor-of-mouth swelling as the initial presentation
Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates, which are more supportive of dermatomyositis
Initial unilateral periorbital swelling

data.description: Acute noninfectious swelling of deeper skin and mucosal tissues, often involving the eyelids, lips, tongue, pharynx, and larynx. It can cause throat tightness, voice change, and dysphagia. However, it does not explain the subsequent inflammatory myopathy, severe creatine kinase elevation, proximal weakness, MRI muscle inflammation, or biopsy findings.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of pruritus can occur in bradykinin-mediated angioedema
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive proximal muscle weakness
Difficulty rising from a seated position
Shoulder and hip pain
Markedly elevated creatine kinase
Persistent elevation of AST and ALT from muscle injury
MRI evidence of diffuse skeletal-muscle edema involving facial and pharyngeal muscles
Muscle biopsy with perivascular inflammation and MHC class I upregulation
Subcutaneous edema of both upper arms associated with inflammatory myopathy

data.description: 11-year-old boy who received his first black henna tattoo while on holiday in Portugal in August 2013. One week after getting the tattoo, the area became hot, red, raised and itchy. Physical exam showed bullae with clear yellow-orange discharge and golden crusting on a background of erythematous plaque.

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis due to paraphenylenediamine (PPD) in black henna tattoo
data.description: A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction to PPD, a common additive in black henna that intensifies and accelerates tattoo staining. It typically develops days to weeks after exposure and closely follows the tattoo design.
symptoms_in_common: Onset approximately one week after black henna tattoo application
Eruption precisely following the tattoo pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Golden crusting may indicate secondary bacterial infection rather than uncomplicated allergic dermatitis

data.diagnosis: Bullous allergic contact dermatitis with secondary impetiginization
data.description: Severe allergic contact dermatitis causing vesicles or bullae, with secondary superficial bacterial infection—usually Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes—producing honey-colored or golden crusts.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed reaction after black henna exposure
Raised eczematous plaque in the tattoo outline
Image shows erosions and crusting in the exact decorative tattoo pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, malaise, or other systemic infectious symptoms are described
No report of spreading pain or diffuse surrounding cellulitis

data.description: A superficial Staphylococcus aureus skin infection characterized by fragile flaccid bullae that rupture and leave erosions with yellow crusting. It may occur secondarily in skin damaged by dermatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Clear yellow-orange drainage after blister rupture
symptoms_not_in_common: Intense itch is more characteristic of allergic contact dermatitis than primary impetigo
Lesions sharply reproduce the black henna tattoo design
The eruption began after a one-week delayed exposure to black henna
No systemic symptoms are described

data.diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis from tattoo chemicals
data.description: Inflammation caused by direct chemical injury to the skin from tattoo ingredients or solvents. It often causes burning, erythema, scaling, and occasionally blistering, generally soon after exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Reaction at the site of tattoo exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: One-week delay and marked itching favor allergic rather than irritant dermatitis
Bullous morphology is more typical of severe allergic PPD contact dermatitis
Golden crusting suggests superimposed infection
Black henna tattoos are particularly associated with PPD allergy

data.description: A bacterial infection of the deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, usually causing spreading erythema, warmth, tenderness, and swelling. It can complicate excoriated or blistered dermatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Yellow-orange drainage and crusting could occur with bacterial involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Itch rather than pain is emphasized
Bullae and erosions are confined to the tattoo pattern rather than diffuse spreading skin
No fever, chills, malaise, or rapidly expanding erythema are described
The delayed patterned eruption after black henna exposure strongly favors contact dermatitis

data.description: 59-year-old man with multiple nodules on his joints. Patient had history of gouty arthritis (confirmed by visualization of negative birefringent crystals in joint aspirate), hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination showed multiple gouty nodules in the auricle, knee, ankle, and toe joints, with severe loss of flexion and extension in hands. Laboratory findings showed elevated creatine (137 μmol/L; normal range 62–115 μmol/L) and uric acid (725 μmol/L; normal range 208–428 μmol/L).
Advanced gout caused by longstanding monosodium urate crystal deposition, producing large subcutaneous and periarticular tophi, erosive joint disease, and deformity.
symptoms_in_common: History of gouty arthritis confirmed by negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Multiple large nodules over finger, hand, toe, ankle, knee, and auricular joints
Photographs show extensive lobulated periarticular hand masses consistent with tophi
Severe loss of hand flexion and extension due to chronic joint/tendon involvement
Mildly elevated creatinine, which may contribute to impaired urate excretion
Hypertension and type 2 diabetes, common comorbidities associated with gout

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that can cause symmetric hand deformities and firm subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules, usually over pressure points.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hand deformity and restricted flexion and extension
Multiple periarticular nodules involving the hands and elbows/other pressure areas can occur in nodular rheumatoid arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Joint aspirate showing negatively birefringent crystals supports gout rather than rheumatoid arthritis
Marked hyperuricemia
Auricular nodules are much more characteristic of gouty tophi
Very large lobulated nodules over multiple distal hand and foot joints are more typical of tophi
No reported chronic symmetric inflammatory small-joint pain, prolonged morning stiffness, or positive rheumatoid serology

data.description: Deposition of calcium salts in skin and periarticular soft tissues, sometimes producing large calcified nodules around joints and restricting movement.
symptoms_in_common: Possible involvement of large joints such as the knee and ankle
symptoms_not_in_common: Proven monosodium urate crystals in joint fluid
Marked hyperuricemia
Auricular and toe-joint tophi-like lesions are more typical of gout
No reported calcium/phosphate abnormality or connective-tissue disease
The clinical history and photographed soft-tissue masses strongly favor gouty tophi rather than calcium deposition

data.description: A 25-year-old man was referred to the oncology unit with a three-week history of a progressively enlarging neck lump and atypical lymphoid cells found on fine needle aspiration cytology. He reported mild exertional dyspnea and drenching night sweats, but denied weight loss, occupational exposure to harmful substances, recent travel, or high-risk sexual behavior. He had a smoking history since age 16. On physical examination, a palpable right supraclavicular lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter was found. Chest radiography revealed a widened mediastinum but no lung lesions. Core biopsy of the lymph node showed partial effacement of nodal architecture by scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells with some collagen fibrosis. These large cells stained positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly affects young adults and typically presents with cervical/supraclavicular lymphadenopathy and a bulky anterior mediastinal mass. It is characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells that are usually CD15-positive, CD30-positive, and CD45-negative, often within a background of fibrosis and mixed inflammatory cells.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Widened mediastinum and anterior mediastinal mass on imaging
Mild exertional dyspnea from mediastinal disease
Large atypical lymphoid cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells
Collagen fibrosis in the lymph node biopsy
Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss, although this is not required for diagnosis

data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the anterior mediastinum, often causing a bulky mediastinal mass with respiratory symptoms. It is more common in young women and usually expresses B-cell markers such as CD20, PAX5, and CD45.
symptoms_not_in_common: Large tumor cells are CD15-positive and CD30-positive, which is less typical
Tumor cells are CD45-negative, whereas primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma is generally CD45-positive
Biopsy shows a mixed inflammatory background with eosinophils and fibrosis more characteristic of classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Male sex is less typical because this lymphoma has a female predominance

data.description: A rare lymphoma with overlapping clinical, morphologic, and immunophenotypic features of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. It often involves the mediastinum and may express CD30 and sometimes CD15 along with B-cell markers.
symptoms_in_common: Mediastinal mass on CT and widened mediastinum on chest radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: The CD15-positive and CD45-negative phenotype strongly favors classical Hodgkin lymphoma rather than gray-zone lymphoma
No reported B-cell marker expression such as CD20, OCT2, BOB1, or strong PAX5
Reactive eosinophil-rich inflammatory background and fibrosis are more typical of nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that can present with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms. ALK-positive disease often affects younger patients, but the tumor cells typically express leukocyte and T-cell-associated markers rather than the classic Hodgkin immunophenotype.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity is less typical
CD45 negativity is less typical because anaplastic large cell lymphoma usually retains CD45 expression
Mediastinal mass with fibrosis and eosinophil-rich inflammatory background is more characteristic of nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported ALK, EMA, cytotoxic marker, or T-cell marker expression

data.description: An aggressive immature T-cell neoplasm that frequently presents in adolescent or young adult males with a large anterior mediastinal mass, lymphadenopathy, and respiratory symptoms due to thymic involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy shows scattered large cells rather than sheets of lymphoblasts
Eosinophil-rich reactive background and collagen fibrosis are not typical
CD15-positive and CD30-positive large cells are not the usual immunophenotype
CD45-negative tumor cells are not typical
No reported TdT, CD3, CD7, or other immature T-cell marker expression

data.description: A 45-year-old man presented with dry cough and breathlessness. During the investigation, he was found to be infected with HIV. Physical examination and other baseline clinical details were not specifically described in this brief case report.

An opportunistic fungal pneumonia occurring most commonly in advanced HIV infection, typically causing subacute nonproductive cough, progressive dyspnea, hypoxemia, and bilateral diffuse interstitial or perihilar ground-glass pulmonary infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a major risk factor
Bilateral diffuse perihilar/interstitial pulmonary opacities on chest radiograph

data.description: A viral opportunistic pneumonia seen in severely immunocompromised patients, including people with advanced HIV, which may produce diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates and respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever was reported
No systemic symptoms such as malaise, fatigue, or weight loss were described

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can present atypically in HIV, with diffuse or lower-lung infiltrates rather than the classic upper-lobe cavitary pattern; cough and dyspnea may occur.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection increases susceptibility to tuberculosis
Bilateral pulmonary infiltrative abnormalities can occur in HIV-associated tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The cough is described as dry rather than persistent productive cough
No fever was reported
No night sweats were reported
No weight loss was reported
No focal upper-lobe cavitation is apparent on the radiograph

data.description: Atypical bacterial or viral pneumonias can cause dry cough, dyspnea, and bilateral patchy or interstitial radiographic infiltrates, although HIV-associated opportunistic infection is more concerning in this setting.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral patchy/interstitial pulmonary opacities on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever was reported
No sore throat, myalgia, or other viral prodrome was described
Known HIV infection makes an opportunistic pneumonia such as PJP more likely

data.description: A 65-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a one-month history of worsening breathlessness and chest discomfort on walking. He came to hospital following a collapse that occurred after self-administering sublingual glyceryl trinitrate to relieve his symptoms. He reported no history of cough or coryza, had not lost weight, and experienced no haemoptysis. Laboratory testing revealed a raised serum D-dimer level.

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis (likely from occult primary lung adenocarcinoma)
data.description: Diffuse infiltration of pulmonary lymphatic vessels by metastatic carcinoma, often from lung adenocarcinoma or another solid malignancy. CT typically shows asymmetric or unilateral interlobular septal and peribronchovascular thickening, sometimes with a small pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Older age and substantial smoking history
Raised D-dimer level can occur with malignancy-associated thrombosis
Chest radiograph and CT show diffuse predominantly right-sided reticular/interstitial and septal thickening
Small right pleural effusion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No cough
No haemoptysis
Collapse immediately after sublingual glyceryl trinitrate is not a typical direct manifestation

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arterial circulation by thrombus, commonly causing acute or subacute dyspnoea, chest pain, syncope, and an elevated D-dimer. It may coexist with an underlying malignancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms evolved progressively over one month rather than abruptly
Chest imaging shows asymmetric right-sided interstitial/septal thickening and pleural fluid, which are not classic primary findings of uncomplicated pulmonary embolism
No haemoptysis
No reported pleuritic chest pain

data.diagnosis: Unilateral pulmonary oedema due to cardiac disease
data.description: Pulmonary oedema is accumulation of fluid in the lung interstitium and alveoli, usually from elevated pulmonary venous pressure. It can produce septal thickening and pleural effusions; marked unilateral oedema is uncommon and may occur with asymmetric pulmonary venous flow or mitral regurgitation.
symptoms_in_common: Chest discomfort potentially compatible with myocardial ischaemia
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate could reflect hypotension in a patient with cardiac disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging abnormalities are strongly right-sided and relatively focal/asymmetric, which is atypical for routine cardiogenic pulmonary oedema
No described orthopnoea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
No reported peripheral oedema
Raised D-dimer is not a typical feature

data.diagnosis: Smoking-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with possible acute cardiopulmonary decompensation
data.description: COPD is chronic airflow limitation, usually caused by cigarette smoking, and commonly produces progressive exertional dyspnoea. It may coexist with coronary disease, pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary embolism, or lung cancer.
symptoms_in_common: Chest radiograph suggests hyperinflation of the left lung
symptoms_not_in_common: No chronic cough
No sputum production reported
No coryzal or infective symptoms
Predominantly right-sided interlobular septal/peribronchovascular thickening and a pleural effusion are not typical findings of uncomplicated COPD
Raised D-dimer is not explained by uncomplicated COPD

data.description: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of shortness of breath and sore throat. Her medical history included smoking, obesity, type 2 diabetes On examination, her oxygen saturation was 81% on room air, dropping to 71% with exertion. She was afebrile with a normal white blood cell count. Chest examination revealed soft heart sounds, decreased air entry, wheeze, and aegophony at the lung bases bilaterally. Abdominal examination was normal except for obesity.

data.diagnosis: Right hemidiaphragm eventration with compressive right middle/lower lobe atelectasis
data.description: Eventration is an abnormal, usually longstanding elevation of an intact hemidiaphragm due to thinning or weakness of diaphragmatic muscle. The chest radiograph and sagittal CT show marked smooth elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with compression/collapse of adjacent right lung.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry at the lung bases
Obesity, which can worsen restrictive respiratory mechanics
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Acute 1-week onset, as eventration is often chronic or asymptomatic
Smoking history

data.description: Paralysis or marked weakness of the right phrenic nerve/hemidiaphragm causes elevation of the right hemidiaphragm and reduced ventilation of the ipsilateral lung. It may produce basal atelectasis and clinically important dyspnea, particularly in obese patients or those with underlying lung disease.
symptoms_in_common: Obesity as a factor increasing symptomatic respiratory impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Aegophony is not a primary feature, although it can occur from associated atelectasis
No stated history of recent thoracic surgery, trauma, or neurologic disease

data.diagnosis: Compressive atelectasis of the right lung secondary to elevated hemidiaphragm
data.description: Atelectasis is partial collapse or underinflation of lung tissue. In this case, the elevated right hemidiaphragm compresses the adjacent lung, producing reduced basal ventilation and contributing to hypoxemia.
symptoms_in_common: Low oxygen saturation at rest and with exertion
Decreased air entry at the lung bases
Imaging evidence of elevated right hemidiaphragm with adjacent lung compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
No fever
Normal white blood cell count

data.description: COPD is chronic airflow limitation, most commonly related to cigarette smoking. An acute exacerbation can cause worsening dyspnea, wheeze, and hypoxemia, often triggered by a viral upper-respiratory infection.
symptoms_in_common: Sore throat suggesting a possible viral respiratory trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm on imaging
Focal compressive right lung atelectasis
Aegophony is less typical of uncomplicated COPD
No documented chronic cough, sputum production, or prior COPD diagnosis

data.description: 67-year-old female patient presented with chief complaint of swelling in right cheek. History of unhealed tooth extraction sockets from right upper posterior tooth extraction performed approximately one month previously. Past medical history significant for colorectal cancer treatment. Intraoral examination revealed localized, well-defined swelling measuring 4 cm × 5 cm obliterating buccal and palatal vestibules in region of unhealed extraction sockets of teeth 14, 15, and 16. Laboratory examination showed abnormal GTP level and slightly elevated serum CRP level.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS), activated B-cell phenotype
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can arise at extranodal sites, including the oral cavity and maxilla. The images show a soft-tissue maxillary mass and sheets of atypical large lymphoid cells; BCL6 and MUM1 positivity with limited/negative CD10 staining supports a non-germinal-center/activated B-cell phenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly apparent localized right cheek and posterior maxillary swelling
Large well-defined 4 cm × 5 cm oral soft-tissue mass
Obliteration of buccal and palatal vestibules
Persistent unhealed extraction sockets, which can be an initial manifestation of oral lymphoma
CT evidence of a right maxillary soft-tissue lesion
Cytology/histology showing atypical large lymphoid cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Slightly elevated CRP is nonspecific and may reflect local inflammation
Abnormal GTP level is not a typical defining manifestation of DLBCL

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma of the maxilla
data.description: A lymphoma originating in the maxillary alveolus, gingiva, palate, or adjacent soft tissues rather than in lymph nodes. DLBCL is the most common histologic subtype of oral/maxillary extranodal B-cell lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Nonhealing extraction wounds in the posterior maxilla
Atypical lymphoid-cell proliferation on pathologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: History of colorectal cancer is not required for a primary oral lymphoma
Abnormal GTP level is not characteristic
Mild CRP elevation is nonspecific rather than a typical lymphoma feature

data.diagnosis: Post-extraction odontogenic infection or maxillary osteomyelitis
data.description: Bacterial infection involving an extraction socket, maxillary alveolar bone, or adjacent soft tissues can produce swelling, delayed healing, and inflammatory marker elevation. It is an important clinical mimic of malignancy after dental extraction.
symptoms_in_common: History of recent posterior maxillary tooth extraction
Unhealed extraction sockets after one month
Vestibular swelling adjacent to extraction sites
symptoms_not_in_common: The large atypical lymphoid cells on cytology/histology are not typical of infection
BCL6 and MUM1-positive atypical lymphoid proliferation is not expected in routine odontogenic infection
A discrete extensive soft-tissue mass without a described abscess or destructive osteomyelitic pattern is less typical
No reported fever, purulent drainage, or severe dental pain

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the maxilla/oral cavity
data.description: Colorectal carcinoma can rarely metastasize to the oral cavity or jaw and may present as a rapidly enlarging gingival or extraction-socket mass, particularly in a patient with a prior cancer history.
symptoms_in_common: Past history of colorectal cancer treatment
