Laboratory tests showed liver function abnormalities with alkaline phosphatase 327, aspartate aminotransferase 358, and bilirubin 109 suggesting cholestasis. White cell count was elevated at 20.8, C reactive protein was raised at 17, and platelets were low at 168. Monospot test was positive for Epstein Barr virus, confirmed by positive Epstein Barr virus serology. Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative.

data.diagnosis: Epstein-Barr virus infectious mononucleosis with cholestatic hepatitis
data.description: Primary Epstein-Barr virus infection can cause infectious mononucleosis with hepatitis, sometimes producing marked cholestasis and jaundice. Imaging may show periportal edema and gallbladder wall edema without biliary stones or duct obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and right upper quadrant tenderness
Elevated alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and aminotransferases
Positive Monospot test and Epstein-Barr virus serology
Imaging findings compatible with gallbladder wall edema and inflammatory hepatic/periportal changes without an obstructing stone

data.diagnosis: Acute acalculous cholecystitis associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection
data.description: Acute inflammation of the gallbladder without gallstones. It is an uncommon complication of Epstein-Barr virus infection and may result from gallbladder wall edema, biliary stasis, and systemic inflammation. Ultrasound and MRI can demonstrate gallbladder wall thickening/edema without calculi.
symptoms_in_common: No visible gallstones or clear obstructive lesion on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Prominent pharyngitis and generalized cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy are not typical primary manifestations of cholecystitis
Pale stools and dark urine suggest substantial cholestasis, which is less common in isolated cholecystitis

data.diagnosis: Acute bacterial cholangitis due to extrahepatic biliary obstruction
data.description: Cholangitis is infection of the biliary tract, usually caused by obstruction such as a common bile duct stone. It classically presents with fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain, but imaging generally shows biliary dilatation or an obstructing lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Cholestatic liver biochemistry with elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported bile duct stone, obstructing mass, or biliary duct dilatation on imaging
Positive Epstein-Barr virus testing with pharyngitis and generalized lymphadenopathy favors infectious mononucleosis instead
Gallbladder wall edema without demonstrated obstruction is more consistent with viral-associated acalculous cholecystitis

data.description:
41-year-old man presented with sudden, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right groin and flank, associated with nausea and one episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting. Two weeks earlier, he had a similar but milder episode in the left lower quadrant radiating to the left flank that resolved spontaneously. He also reported several months of fatigue. He denied fever, weight loss, chest pain, diarrhea, and urinary symptoms.  

On examination, he was uncomfortable-appearing, afebrile, with diffuse abdominal tenderness on deep palpation without rebound or guarding and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness, worse on the right. Labs showed leukocytosis, mild anemia, elevated creatinine, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, elevated ESR and CRP, and urinalysis with 1+ protein and bland sediment. Serologic testing for ANCA, hepatitis B/C, HIV, ANA, and hypercoagulability panel was negative or normal.

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) with renal arterial involvement
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause microaneurysms, stenoses, thrombosis, and renal infarctions. Renal angiography commonly shows multiple small aneurysms and irregular branch-vessel narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe flank and abdominal pain
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase consistent with tissue infarction
Mild proteinuria with bland urinary sediment
Bilateral renal perfusion defects/infarcts on CT
Renal angiographic abnormalities with multiple small aneurysmal or irregular medium-vessel lesions
Negative ANCA, which is typical because PAN is usually ANCA-negative
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No weight loss
No skin rash, livedo reticularis, or nodules reported
No peripheral neuropathy reported
No hypertension reported

data.diagnosis: Renal infarction due to renal artery branch thrombosis or embolism
data.description: Acute interruption of renal arterial blood flow causes renal ischemia and infarction, producing sudden flank or abdominal pain, elevated LDH, kidney dysfunction, and wedge-shaped perfusion defects on contrast imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe right lower quadrant and flank pain
Prior transient left-sided flank and lower abdominal pain
Bilateral renal infarct-like perfusion defects on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue
Marked inflammatory marker elevation may suggest an underlying vasculitis rather than isolated embolism
Angiographic microaneurysmal/irregular branch-vessel changes are not typical of a simple cardioembolic renal infarction
No reported atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, recent myocardial infarction, or other embolic source

data.description: A rare noninflammatory arteriopathy of medium-sized abdominal visceral arteries that can produce arterial dissections, stenoses, aneurysms, thrombosis, and organ infarction, including renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe abdominal and flank pain
Renal arterial branch irregularities and aneurysmal changes on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue
Elevated ESR and CRP are less typical because SAM is generally noninflammatory
Leukocytosis may occur with infarction but is not a defining feature
Mild anemia is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Fibromuscular dysplasia involving the renal arteries
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder causing alternating stenosis and dilation, often described as a string-of-beads appearance. It can rarely cause renal artery dissection, thrombosis, or renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Renal arterial irregularity/aneurysmal appearance on angiography
Flank and abdominal pain if complicated by renal artery dissection or infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Male sex and age 41 are less typical, as fibromuscular dysplasia more commonly affects women
Elevated ESR and CRP are not typical
Leukocytosis is not typical
Months of systemic fatigue is not typical
Bilateral multifocal renal infarcts are less typical without dissection
No hypertension reported

data.description: 80-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, coronary arteriosclerosis, congestive heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and gout, admitted for anorexia, weight loss, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. He had emigrated from Southeast Asia 22 years earlier. On examination, he was thin and chronically ill, with tachycardia, posterior lower-lung crackles, mild abdominal tenderness, and leg edema.

data.diagnosis: Ileocecal tuberculosis with tuberculous aortitis (tuberculous mycotic abdominal aortic aneurysm)
data.description: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving the ileocecal bowel and potentially the aortic wall, causing inflammatory aneurysmal degeneration. The imaging suggests an abdominal aortic aneurysm with adjacent inflammatory change, ileocecal abnormality, and a pulmonary lesion compatible with disseminated or reactivated tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: Southeast Asian origin, a risk factor for prior tuberculosis exposure
Ileocecal/colonic ulcerative lesion on imaging and endoscopy
Abdominal aortic aneurysm with inflammatory appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg edema
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Tachycardia

data.description: Tuberculosis involving the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly the ileocecal region, causing ulceration, bowel-wall thickening, abdominal pain, diarrhea, anorexia, and wasting. It may coexist with pulmonary tuberculosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg edema
Congestive heart failure findings
Abdominal aortic aneurysm
Peripheral arterial disease

data.diagnosis: Colorectal adenocarcinoma of the cecum or ascending colon
data.description: Cancer of the colon can present with constitutional symptoms, abdominal discomfort, altered bowel habits, and a mass or ulcerated lesion in the cecum/ascending colon. It may produce FDG uptake on PET imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Ileocecal/ascending-colon mass-like or ulcerative lesion on imaging/endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-lung lesion suggestive of granulomatous infection
Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
Southeast Asian origin as a specific epidemiologic clue
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Leg edema

data.diagnosis: Amebic colitis (Entamoeba histolytica infection), possibly with ameboma
data.description: Invasive Entamoeba histolytica infection causes colitis with abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and colonic ulcerations. A mass-like inflammatory lesion, termed an ameboma, can occur in the cecum or ascending colon and mimic colon cancer.
symptoms_in_common: History of residence in Southeast Asia, where exposure may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary upper-lobe lesion
Abdominal aortic aneurysm
Leg edema
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Coronary and peripheral vascular disease

data.diagnosis: Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (mycotic aneurysm), including Salmonella-associated infection
data.description: A mycotic aneurysm is infection of the aortic wall resulting in rapid aneurysm formation, periaortic inflammation, pain, and risk of rupture. Elderly patients with diabetes and extensive atherosclerotic disease are at increased risk; Salmonella species are a classic cause.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with surrounding inflammatory changes on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Ileocecal ulcerative lesion
Upper-lung lesion
Longstanding weight loss and anorexia without reported fever
Southeast Asian origin as a specific clue for this diagnosis

data.description: A 62-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C virus infection and alcohol-induced cirrhosis presented with 10 days of epigastric pain and vomiting. Laboratory findings revealed an elevated serum lipase level of 6715 U per liter (reference range 0 to 160). On hospital day five, the patient developed nodules measuring 1 cm by 1 cm that became increasingly tender over the following days.

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic panniculitis associated with acute pancreatitis
data.description: A rare form of lobular panniculitis caused by release of pancreatic enzymes into the bloodstream, leading to enzymatic fat necrosis in subcutaneous tissue. It is classically associated with acute pancreatitis, pancreatic pseudocyst, or pancreatic malignancy. The biopsy image is consistent with lobular fat necrosis with characteristic anucleate adipocytes ('ghost cells').
symptoms_in_common: CT findings consistent with acute pancreatic inflammation
Erythematous to violaceous nodules on the legs
Histologic lobular panniculitis with fat necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic hepatitis C infection
Alcohol-induced cirrhosis

data.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas, commonly caused by alcohol use or gallstone disease. It typically presents with acute epigastric abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, and elevated pancreatic enzymes; imaging may show pancreatic edema and peripancreatic inflammatory changes.
symptoms_in_common: Serum lipase of 6715 U per liter
CT image showing pancreatic and peripancreatic inflammatory changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Tender erythematous subcutaneous nodules on the legs
Skin biopsy showing lobular fat necrosis

data.description: A reactive inflammatory panniculitis that causes tender erythematous nodules, most commonly on the anterior lower legs. It is a septal panniculitis and may occur with infections, inflammatory disorders, medications, or systemic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous to violaceous lesions on the lower extremities
Acute onset of painful skin lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated serum lipase
Epigastric pain and vomiting consistent with pancreatitis
CT evidence of pancreatic inflammation
Histology showing lobular fat necrosis and ghost adipocytes rather than septal panniculitis

data.description: A 50-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of back pain and a skull mass that had been growing slowly for 7 months. Physical examination revealed a smooth, firm, and non-tender mass on his skull that gave him the appearance of having a high domed forehead. Laboratory investigations showed renal impairment, hypercalcaemia, anaemia, and immunoparesis. Lambda light chains were detected in both urine and serum. Bone marrow aspirate showed a low level infiltration of plasma cells, though the patient could not tolerate a bone marrow biopsy. A biopsy of the thoracic lesion revealed a monomorphic population of plasma cells that were strongly positive for CD138 and lambda light chain restricted.

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with extensive calvarial plasmacytoma
data.description: A malignant clonal plasma-cell disorder causing monoclonal light-chain production, osteolytic bone disease, anemia, renal dysfunction, and hypercalcaemia. The skull mass represents an extensive osseous/extramedullary plasmacytoma involving the calvarium.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly enlarging firm skull mass with high-domed forehead appearance
Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Plasma-cell infiltration in bone marrow aspirate
Thoracic lesion composed of CD138-positive, lambda-restricted monoclonal plasma cells
Imaging appearance of diffuse expansile calvarial involvement/soft-tissue skull mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Low-level rather than extensive plasma-cell infiltration on bone marrow aspirate

data.description: A variant of multiple myeloma characterized by multiple destructive bone or soft-tissue plasmacytomas despite relatively limited bone-marrow plasma-cell involvement. Monoclonal protein/light-chain production and end-organ injury may still occur.
symptoms_in_common: Lambda light chains in blood and urine
symptoms_not_in_common: Immunoparesis is less specifically characteristic of macrofocal disease than of conventional multiple myeloma

data.description: Plasmacytomas are localized masses of monoclonal plasma cells arising in bone or soft tissue. More than one osseous lesion, especially with systemic monoclonal light chains and CRAB features, generally represents systemic plasma-cell myeloma rather than truly isolated disease.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic lesion showing monomorphic CD138-positive lambda-restricted plasma cells
Low-level plasma-cell infiltration in bone marrow aspirate
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal impairment
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Lambda light chains in both urine and serum
Presence of multiple systemic end-organ features favors multiple myeloma rather than isolated/multiple localized plasmacytomas

data.diagnosis: Solitary osseous plasmacytoma of the skull
data.description: A localized tumor of monoclonal plasma cells arising from a single bone, often presenting as a painless enlarging skull mass. It is distinguished from multiple myeloma by absent or minimal marrow involvement and no myeloma-related systemic end-organ damage.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly enlarging smooth, firm, non-tender skull mass
Only low-level plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate
symptoms_not_in_common: Back pain with a separate thoracic lesion
Renal impairment
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Lambda light chains detected in both serum and urine
Multiple lesions/systemic findings, which argue strongly against a solitary plasmacytoma

data.description: A 13-year-old male presented with pain in the right hypochondrium and loss of appetite for 1 month. There was no history of fever. The patient has a history of a successfully treated abdominal tuberculosis, for which he had taken anti-tubercular treatment for 1 year.

data.diagnosis: Hepatic tuberculosis with tubercular liver abscesses
data.description: Tuberculous involvement of the liver can produce multiple hypodense nodules or larger coalescent abscess-like lesions with peripheral enhancement on contrast CT. It may occur as recurrence or reactivation in a patient with previous abdominal tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal hypodense hepatic lesions on CT, including a larger central lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, although fever is common in active hepatic tuberculosis
No reported weight loss or night sweats
No reported jaundice

data.description: A pyogenic liver abscess is a bacterial collection of pus in the liver, often appearing on CT as a low-attenuation lesion with rim enhancement; multiple abscesses can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Focal hypodense liver lesions with an abscess-like appearance on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No reported chills or toxic appearance
No reported leukocytosis or other evidence of acute bacterial infection
History of treated abdominal tuberculosis favors a tuberculous rather than pyogenic cause

data.description: Lymphoma can involve the liver as solitary or multiple hypoattenuating masses and may cause abdominal pain, anorexia, and constitutional symptoms. In children, lymphomatous hepatic involvement is usually associated with nodal, splenic, or systemic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal low-attenuation liver lesions on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever, weight loss, or night sweats
No reported lymphadenopathy
No reported hepatosplenomegaly or other systemic lymphoma findings
Previous abdominal tuberculosis and abscess-like imaging pattern are more suggestive of hepatic tuberculosis

data.description: A man in his 70s with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and mild aortic stenosis presented with altered mental status, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, and painful, dusky skin discoloration on his distal extremities. Three weeks prior to presentation, he had undergone coronary angiography and coronary artery bypass graft surgery after myocardial infarction. Laboratory examination revealed a white blood cell count of 9100/μL with 22% eosinophils, blood urea nitrogen level of 70 mg/dL (25 mmol/L), and creatinine level of 6.1 mg/dL (539.2 μmol/L). Urinalysis showed 1+ blood and 2+ protein.

Systemic showering of cholesterol crystal emboli from disrupted atherosclerotic plaques, often after angiography or vascular surgery. It commonly causes blue/purple toes, livedo-like skin lesions, eosinophilia, and subacute kidney failure.
symptoms_in_common: Recent coronary angiography and coronary artery bypass surgery
Painful dusky-purple discoloration of distal toes and fingers (blue toe syndrome)
Mottled/purpuric skin lesions on the extremities
Altered mental status, potentially from systemic embolization or uremia
symptoms_not_in_common: None of the major reported findings are atypical; the presentation is highly characteristic

data.description: A necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis that can cause skin infarction, livedo reticularis, peripheral ischemia, renal injury, hypertension, and systemic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal skin ischemia and dusky discoloration
Possible livedo-like or purpuric skin lesions
Altered mental status can occur with severe renal dysfunction or vascular involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Temporal onset shortly after coronary angiography and bypass surgery strongly favors cholesterol embolization instead
Prominent eosinophilia is not typical
Urinalysis with hematuria and proteinuria is less typical because polyarteritis nodosa generally spares glomeruli
No reported constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, myalgias, or neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with septic peripheral emboli
data.description: Infection of a cardiac valve or endocardial surface that may produce embolic skin lesions, renal injury, neurologic manifestations, and systemic inflammatory findings.
symptoms_in_common: Distal painful purple skin lesions that could resemble embolic ischemia
Acute kidney injury with hematuria and proteinuria
Recent major cardiac surgery is a risk factor for bloodstream infection and endocarditis
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or reported bacteremia
White blood cell count is not markedly elevated
Marked eosinophilia is not typical of infective endocarditis
The close relationship to angiography and the combination of blue toes, eosinophilia, and renal failure more strongly support cholesterol embolization
No reported new murmur, valve vegetation, splenomegaly, or classic infectious embolic lesions

data.description: A 79-year-old man with a history of hypertension, stroke, and glaucoma was brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive by a caregiver. He was cold to the touch with vital signs showing blood pressure of 85/55 mm Hg, heart rate of 36/min, respiratory rate of 14/min, and pulse oximetry of 100% on ambient air. Multiple temperature measurements, including core temperature assessment via rectal method, did not yield a detectable temperature. Physical examination revealed clear bilateral chest auscultation. Chest radiographs and computed tomography of the head were negative for any acute pathology.
A life-threatening reduction in core body temperature, often causing depressed consciousness, hypotension, marked bradycardia, and characteristic ECG J (Osborn) waves.
symptoms_in_common: No detectable core temperature by rectal measurement
ECG findings consistent with prominent J (Osborn) waves, especially in precordial leads
No acute intracranial pathology on head CT to otherwise explain the unresponsiveness

data.description: Decompensated severe hypothyroidism causing altered mental status, hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, and potentially respiratory failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known history of hypothyroidism is provided
No mention of typical hypothyroid features such as chronic fatigue, weight gain, dry skin, coarse hair, constipation, facial puffiness, or nonpitting edema
Prominent Osborn waves are more characteristic of severe hypothermia itself than of hypothyroidism

data.description: Severe infection can produce altered mental status and shock; elderly patients may develop hypothermia rather than fever.
symptoms_in_common: Hypothermia can occur in severe sepsis, particularly in older adults
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked bradycardia is less typical than tachycardia in septic shock
No infectious symptoms or focal source are described
Clear bilateral chest examination
Chest radiograph showed no acute pulmonary pathology
ECG Osborn waves favor primary severe hypothermia rather than sepsis alone

data.description: An elevated serum potassium level can cause life-threatening bradyarrhythmias, conduction abnormalities, weakness, and altered mental status.
symptoms_in_common: Unresponsiveness can occur in severe electrolyte-related cardiac instability
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound undetectable core temperature is not typical of hyperkalemia
ECG does not show the classic prominent peaked T waves, progressive PR prolongation, QRS widening, or sine-wave pattern expected in severe hyperkalemia
Osborn waves strongly suggest hypothermia
No renal failure, potassium-raising medication use, or other hyperkalemia risk factor is provided

data.description: 34-year-old man, previously well, presented with a generalized tonic-clonic seizure and transient right-sided weakness, along with recurrent hemoptysis for 1 month. Examination and tests showed normal renal ultrasound, hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, normal white blood cell count, normal complement and creatinine, and urinalysis without protein but with a few old red blood cells. Anti-GBM antibodies, ANCA, dsDNA, and anti-smooth muscle antibodies were negative; bronchoscopy cultures, viral serology, and echocardiography were negative. Immunofluorescence showed extensive linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissues.

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (atypical Goodpasture syndrome)
data.description: An autoimmune pulmonary-renal syndrome caused by antibodies targeting basement membranes, usually producing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Rarely, circulating anti-GBM antibodies are negative despite diagnostic linear IgG staining on tissue immunofluorescence.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent hemoptysis consistent with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Anemia with hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, compatible with pulmonary blood loss
Chest CT with bilateral patchy ground-glass pulmonary opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Urinalysis with red blood cells, suggesting glomerular involvement
Linear IgG deposits in renal and lung tissue, strongly supportive of anti-GBM disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative circulating anti-GBM antibody test
Normal creatinine and absence of overt proteinuria
Only a few old red blood cells in urine rather than active nephritic sediment
Generalized seizure and transient right-sided weakness are unusual manifestations

data.diagnosis: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis with mild renal immune-complex involvement
data.description: A rare disorder characterized by recurrent diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, iron-deficiency anemia, and pulmonary hemosiderin deposition, usually without a defined autoimmune, infectious, cardiac, or renal cause.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral ground-glass pulmonary infiltrates on CT, compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Negative infectious studies and negative echocardiography
Negative ANCA, anti-GBM antibodies, dsDNA, and normal complement
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear IgG deposits in renal and pulmonary tissues are not typical of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
Microscopic hematuria suggests renal involvement, whereas idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis is generally kidney-sparing
Seizure with transient focal neurologic deficit is not typical

data.diagnosis: ANCA-negative small-vessel vasculitis causing pulmonary capillaritis
data.description: A small-vessel inflammatory vasculitis can cause pulmonary capillaritis with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. Although commonly ANCA-positive, some cases are ANCA-negative.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis and CT ground-glass infiltrates compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Anemia consistent with recurrent pulmonary bleeding
Microscopic hematuria suggesting possible glomerular inflammation
Neurologic manifestations such as seizure or focal weakness can occur with central nervous system vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: ANCA is negative
Normal renal function and lack of proteinuria are less typical when renal vasculitis is clinically significant
Linear IgG deposition is not typical, since pauci-immune vasculitis usually has little or no immune staining
Normal white blood cell count and lack of systemic inflammatory symptoms

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (lupus pneumonitis/capillaritis)
data.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus can produce immune-complex glomerulonephritis and, rarely, life-threatening diffuse alveolar hemorrhage. Neurologic lupus may cause seizures and focal deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis with bilateral ground-glass lung opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Microscopic hematuria that may indicate glomerulonephritis
Granular IgG immune deposits can occur in lupus nephritis
Seizure and transient focal weakness can occur in neuropsychiatric lupus
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative dsDNA antibodies
Normal complement levels
Male sex and absence of reported rash, arthritis, serositis, or other systemic lupus features
Prominent linear IgG deposition is more characteristic of anti-GBM disease than lupus
No proteinuria and normal creatinine

data.diagnosis: IgA vasculitis or IgA nephropathy with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
data.description: IgA-mediated disease primarily affects the kidneys but can rarely involve pulmonary capillaries, causing hemoptysis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; neurologic events are uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis and bilateral ground-glass pulmonary opacities compatible with pulmonary hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Immunofluorescence reports IgG rather than dominant IgA deposition
No proteinuria or renal impairment
No reported purpura, abdominal pain, arthralgia, or other IgA vasculitis manifestations
Seizure and transient right-sided weakness are not typical

data.description: 30-year-old Hispanic male with history of heavy NSAID use. Presented with melena and severe abdominal pain for 3 weeks, with similar but milder symptoms over prior 4-5 months. Initial hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume 78 fL. Later endorsed having a right swollen testicle (initially missed on previous exams). Physical exam revealed nontender enlarged right testicle. Laboratory markers showed: human chorionic gonadotropin 50 mIU/mL (normal <10), α-fetoprotein 1,990 ng/mL (normal <8), lactate dehydrogenase 534 IU/L (range 25-175).

data.diagnosis: Metastatic nonseminomatous testicular germ-cell tumor (mixed germ-cell tumor) with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: An aggressive testicular cancer containing nonseminomatous elements, often including yolk-sac tumor and embryonal carcinoma, that can spread through retroperitoneal lymph nodes and rarely metastasize to the stomach or duodenum, causing ulceration and bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Severe microcytic anemia consistent with chronic gastrointestinal blood loss
Endoscopic ulcerated, friable upper gastrointestinal lesions compatible with metastatic tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy NSAID use is not a typical cause of testicular germ-cell tumor, although it may initially suggest peptic ulcer disease

data.diagnosis: Testicular yolk-sac tumor with metastatic gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: A nonseminomatous germ-cell tumor characterized by production of alpha-fetoprotein. In adults it commonly occurs as part of a mixed testicular germ-cell tumor and may spread to retroperitoneal lymph nodes and distant organs.
symptoms_in_common: Melena from ulcerated gastrointestinal tumor involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Beta-human chorionic gonadotropin elevation is less characteristic of a pure yolk-sac tumor and suggests a mixed germ-cell tumor component
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated to yolk-sac tumor development

data.diagnosis: Testicular choriocarcinoma or mixed germ-cell tumor with choriocarcinoma component
data.description: A highly vascular nonseminomatous germ-cell tumor component that produces beta-human chorionic gonadotropin and has a strong tendency toward hematogenous metastasis and hemorrhage, including bleeding from gastrointestinal metastases.
symptoms_in_common: Severe anemia due to blood loss
Ulcerated and hemorrhagic-appearing gastrointestinal lesions on endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: The markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein is not produced by pure choriocarcinoma and supports an accompanying yolk-sac or other nonseminomatous component
The relatively modest beta-human chorionic gonadotropin elevation is less typical of pure choriocarcinoma
Heavy NSAID use is not typical of choriocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: NSAID-associated peptic ulcer disease with upper gastrointestinal bleeding
data.description: Gastric or duodenal mucosal injury caused by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which can produce painful ulcers, melena, and iron-deficiency anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Microcytosis consistent with chronic blood loss
Ulcerated upper gastrointestinal lesions on endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender enlarged right testicle
Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein
Elevated beta-human chorionic gonadotropin
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Retroperitoneal mass/adenopathy on CT suggestive of metastatic malignancy
Infiltrative tumor-like gastrointestinal pathology is not typical of uncomplicated NSAID ulcer disease

data.description: 55-year-old man with a history of heart failure, obesity, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and HFpEF presented with 3 days of sudden-onset right foot and calf swelling and pain, progressing to the upper leg, with new dusky discoloration of the right toes on the day of presentation. He had intentional 22.7 kg weight loss over 6 months and a 30-pack-year smoking history, quit 5 years earlier. Medications included warfarin, sotalol, torsemide, and lisinopril. Exam showed afebrile vital signs, marked asymmetry with 4+ pitting edema of the right upper thigh and 2+ pitting edema of the left calf, and the right leg/foot was dusky and cold with distal pulses detectable only by Doppler.
A severe form of extensive deep venous thrombosis causing near-total venous outflow obstruction, massive edema, cyanosis, pain, and potentially limb-threatening arterial compromise.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden onset of severe right foot and calf pain and swelling
Rapid progression of swelling to the upper right leg
Marked unilateral right thigh pitting edema
Dusky blue-black discoloration of the right toes and foot
Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler, suggesting compromised arterial inflow from severe venous congestion
Clinical images showing severe edema and cyanotic/ischemic discoloration of the foot
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild left calf edema
Intentional weight loss

data.diagnosis: Extensive acute right iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis
data.description: Acute thrombosis involving the deep veins of the lower extremity, especially the femoral and iliac venous system, producing unilateral pain, swelling, and venous congestion.
symptoms_in_common: Progression of edema from the lower leg to the upper thigh
Severe pitting edema of the right thigh
Dusky discoloration caused by venous obstruction
Angiographic image consistent with extensive venous thrombosis/obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Cold foot with markedly impaired distal pulses, which suggests progression beyond uncomplicated DVT to phlegmasia
Toe ischemia/near-black discoloration
Mild edema in the contralateral left calf

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the stomach. Advanced gastric adenocarcinoma can cause weight loss and can produce a hypercoagulable state associated with venous thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Former heavy smoking history, a risk factor for gastric malignancy
Unprovoked extensive venous thrombosis despite warfarin therapy, compatible with malignancy-associated hypercoagulability
CT image suggesting abnormal gastric wall/mass lesion
Endoscopic images showing a large irregular gastric tumor
Histologic images consistent with invasive gastric adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute unilateral leg pain and edema are not direct typical presenting symptoms of gastric cancer
Dusky cold foot and weak pulses are manifestations of severe venous thrombosis rather than the primary gastric tumor
No reported abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding, or early satiety

data.description: A cancer-related prothrombotic state in which occult or advanced malignancy, particularly adenocarcinoma, leads to recurrent or unusually extensive venous thromboembolism.
symptoms_in_common: Severe thrombosis progressing to phlegmasia cerulea dolens
Thrombosis occurring despite chronic warfarin use
Imaging and pathology evidence of gastric adenocarcinoma
No clear transient provoking factor for the severe venous thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Cold cyanotic foot and diminished pulses are consequences of the severe thrombosis rather than defining features of hypercoagulability itself
History of heart failure and atrial fibrillation are alternative cardiovascular contributors but do not specifically indicate Trousseau syndrome

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma of gastric origin
diagnoses.title: Adenocarcinoma of stomach

data.description: 76-year-old man from the Indian subcontinent presented with fever and priapism. Physical exam showed painful, engorged penis with intact skin, no lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly. No skin rash or nodules were found.

data.diagnosis: Penile leishmaniasis due to Leishmania donovani complex
data.description: A rare extrapulmonary manifestation of leishmaniasis in which amastigote-filled macrophages infiltrate penile/cavernosal tissue, potentially causing painful priapism. The histology is consistent with intracellular small oval organisms with kinetoplast-like structures, and the imaging shows metabolically active penile involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from the Indian subcontinent, where visceral leishmaniasis is endemic
Histology showing macrophage-rich inflammation containing small intracellular organisms
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatomegaly
No splenomegaly
No lymphadenopathy
No typical cutaneous leishmaniasis rash, ulcer, or nodules

data.diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis with isolated genital involvement
data.description: Visceral leishmaniasis is a systemic infection caused mainly by Leishmania donovani in South Asia. It usually affects the reticuloendothelial system but can rarely involve unusual sites such as the penis and corpora cavernosa.
symptoms_in_common: Residence or origin in a leishmaniasis-endemic region
Tissue morphology compatible with Leishmania amastigotes in macrophages
symptoms_not_in_common: No splenomegaly, which is usually prominent in visceral leishmaniasis
No hepatomegaly
No lymphadenopathy
Priapism is an exceptionally unusual manifestation
No reported pancytopenia, weight loss, or marked constitutional decline

data.description: Histoplasmosis is a fungal infection in which small intracellular yeast forms can be seen within macrophages and can resemble Leishmania on routine histology. Disseminated disease may produce fever and rare genitourinary involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Macrophage-rich tissue infiltrate containing small intracellular organisms that can resemble yeast forms
Possible involvement of an unusual extrapulmonary site
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful priapism is very uncommon
No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly
No lymphadenopathy
No skin lesions or mucosal lesions
No respiratory symptoms described
Indian-subcontinent epidemiology and apparent kinetoplast-containing organisms favor leishmaniasis over histoplasmosis

data.description: 50-year-old postmenopausal woman with 1-year postmenopause presented with abdominal distention, anorexia, and exertional dyspnea. Exam showed a markedly distended abdomen. Imaging revealed gross ascites and a heterogeneous left adnexal/pelvic mass with enhancing solid components and small calcifications, without lymphadenopathy or peritoneal dissemination. MRI showed a left pelvic mass with low T1 and low T2 signal in solid parts/thick septa and strong enhancement, with no fatty component. CA 125 was elevated at 1237 U/mL; CEA, CA 19-9, and SCC were normal. Repeated paracentesis cytology showed benign mesothelial cells without malignant cells. Thyroid scintigraphy showed normal thyroid uptake, and thyroid function tests were normal without signs of thyroid dysfunction.

A rare monodermal ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue. It may cause ascites, pleural effusion, marked CA-125 elevation, and occasionally pelvic radioiodine uptake despite normal cervical thyroid function.
symptoms_in_common: Gross ascites causing marked abdominal distention
Right pleural effusion with exertional dyspnea
Solid enhancing ovarian mass with low T1 and low T2 signal components and septa
Pelvic uptake on thyroid scintigraphic imaging
Normal thyroid function tests, which can occur in struma ovarii
symptoms_not_in_common: No fatty component within the mass, whereas teratomatous tumors may contain fat
Absence of clinical hyperthyroidism, although most struma ovarii are euthyroid and this is not exclusionary

data.description: A benign sex-cord stromal ovarian tumor, often occurring in peri- or postmenopausal women, that can be associated with ascites and pleural effusion (Meigs syndrome). Fibrous tumors commonly show low T2 signal and enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Low T2 signal within solid tumor components, compatible with fibrous tissue
Elevated CA-125 can occur secondary to extensive serosal irritation from ascites
symptoms_not_in_common: Pelvic thyroid-scintigraphy uptake is not typical of ovarian fibroma or thecoma
Heterogeneous mass with calcifications and strong enhancement is less characteristic than a predominantly homogeneous fibrous mass
Very high CA-125 level is possible but raises concern for another ovarian process

data.description: Malignant epithelial ovarian tumors, particularly high-grade serous carcinoma, often present with an adnexal mass, ascites, abdominal symptoms, pleural effusion, and elevated CA-125.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional dyspnea due to pleural effusion
Adnexal/pelvic mass with solid enhancing components and septa
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated ascitic-fluid cytology showed no malignant cells
No peritoneal dissemination or omental disease was identified
No lymphadenopathy was identified
Pelvic thyroid-scintigraphy uptake is not typical
Low T2 fibrous-appearing solid components are less typical than the complex cystic-solid morphology commonly seen in high-grade serous carcinoma

data.description: A usually benign epithelial ovarian tumor composed of transitional-type epithelium in a fibrous stroma. It can be solid, calcified, low on T2-weighted MRI, and may occasionally be associated with ascites or elevated CA-125.
symptoms_in_common: Solid mass with low T2 signal due to fibrous stroma
Elevated CA-125 may occur in the setting of ascites or associated ovarian pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive ascites with pleural effusion is uncommon for a benign Brenner tumor
Pelvic thyroid-scintigraphy uptake is not typical
CA-125 elevation to 1237 U/mL is unusual for an uncomplicated benign Brenner tumor
Brenner tumors are often relatively small and may be incidental

data.description: A 32 year-old male presented to his primary care provider with unremitting neck pain. He denied any history of trauma. The patient was unresponsive to conservative therapy and plain-film radiographic evaluation was negative. Patient was subsequently referred for a cervical spine MR for further evaluation.

A rare, slow-growing but locally aggressive tumor derived from notochord remnants. It most often arises in the clivus, sacrum, or upper cervical spine and typically produces a destructive midline osseous mass with substantial soft-tissue extension.
symptoms_in_common: Pain not responsive to conservative treatment
MRI appearance of an infiltrative destructive midline upper cervical/clival-region mass with soft-tissue extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No neurologic deficits were reported
No dysphagia, hoarseness, or cranial-nerve symptoms were reported

data.diagnosis: Chondrosarcoma of the skull base or upper cervical spine
data.description: A malignant cartilaginous tumor that can involve the skull base or cervical vertebrae. It may cause destructive bone change and a lobulated soft-tissue mass, although skull-base lesions are more often eccentric rather than strictly midline.
symptoms_in_common: Destructive osseous lesion with associated soft-tissue mass on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears predominantly midline, whereas chondrosarcomas are often off-midline
No cranial-nerve dysfunction or headache was reported

data.diagnosis: Primary bone lymphoma involving the cervical spine
data.description: Lymphoma can involve vertebral marrow and extend into adjacent epidural or paraspinal soft tissues. Radiographs may initially be unrevealing despite extensive marrow disease on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Negative plain radiographs despite abnormal MRI findings
Marrow-replacing cervical vertebral lesion with soft-tissue extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, weight loss, or lymphadenopathy were reported
The apparent midline skull-base/upper cervical location is more characteristic of chordoma

data.description: Infection of the vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs can produce severe persistent neck pain, marrow edema or replacement, bony destruction, and prevertebral or epidural inflammatory soft tissue.
symptoms_in_common: No response to routine conservative treatment
Abnormal cervical vertebral marrow and adjacent soft-tissue changes on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, infectious risk factors, or elevated inflammatory markers were reported
The imaging appearance is more mass-like than typical disc-centered infection
No reported disc-space destruction

data.diagnosis: Metastatic disease involving the cervical spine
data.description: Metastases may infiltrate cervical vertebral marrow and create destructive lesions with epidural or paraspinal soft-tissue extension, causing persistent focal pain.
symptoms_in_common: MRI evidence of infiltrative vertebral marrow abnormality and soft-tissue mass
Normal or nondiagnostic initial plain radiographs can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 32 years makes metastatic disease less likely
No known primary malignancy, weight loss, or systemic symptoms were reported
A midline upper cervical/clival lesion is more suggestive of chordoma

data.description: A 13-month-old male infant presented to the Department of Dermatology with a single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back that was first noticed by parents at approximately 4 months of age. During observation, the lesion gradually became larger and firmer, and intermittent sweating on the surface was noticed.

A benign congenital proliferation of dermal smooth-muscle bundles, often involving arrector pili muscles. It typically presents in infancy as a skin-colored or hyperpigmented plaque on the trunk, sometimes with hypertrichosis, firmness, or sweating.
symptoms_in_common: Clinical image showing a subtly elevated skin-colored to brownish plaque
Histologic image compatible with prominent disorganized smooth-muscle bundles in the dermis and subcutis

data.description: A benign hamartoma composed of increased eccrine sweat glands and vascular structures, usually present at birth or during childhood. Localized hyperhidrosis is characteristic, and lesions may be painful, bluish, or nodular.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-back location is less typical than distal extremity involvement
No pain or tenderness
No obvious blue, violaceous, or vascular coloration
Histology appears dominated by smooth-muscle proliferation rather than eccrine and vascular proliferation

data.description: A benign pediatric soft-tissue tumor that usually develops during the first two years of life as a painless, slowly enlarging, poorly circumscribed subcutaneous mass, commonly on the trunk or upper extremities.
symptoms_in_common: Male sex is somewhat more common
symptoms_not_in_common: Localized sweating is not typical
The lesion appears primarily cutaneous rather than a deeper subcutaneous mass
Histology does not show the characteristic mixture of fibrous tissue, primitive mesenchyme, and mature adipose tissue

data.description: A benign melanocytic proliferation present at birth or appearing early in infancy, usually presenting as a pigmented plaque that may enlarge proportionally with the child and can develop hypertrichosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible subtle brown pigmentation in the clinical image
symptoms_not_in_common: Increasing firmness is not a typical prominent feature
Localized intermittent sweating is not typical
No clearly defined dark melanocytic pigmentation
Histology is not suggestive of a melanocytic nevus and instead supports smooth-muscle hamartomatous tissue

data.description: A 15-year-old boy presented with recent onset of breathlessness, weight loss, and tiredness for two months and a crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months. The investigations revealed neutrophilia, raised C-reactive protein (CRP), and Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). The blood urea and electrolytes, thyroid function tests, anti-nuclear antibodies, and clotting studies were normal

data.diagnosis: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with pulmonary involvement
data.description: A clonal histiocytic disorder that can involve skin, lungs, bone, liver, and other organs. Pulmonary disease characteristically produces a mixture of nodules, cavitated nodules, and irregular cysts, often most marked in the upper lungs; scalp lesions are a common cutaneous manifestation in children.
symptoms_in_common: Raised ALT, which may suggest hepatic involvement
Chest radiograph and CT showing bilateral diffuse nodular/cystic lung abnormalities with upper-lung predominance
Possible osseous abnormality involving the sternum on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophilia is nonspecific and is not a defining feature
Normal clotting studies despite elevated ALT do not strongly support advanced hepatic involvement

data.description: A lung-predominant form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis characterized on high-resolution CT by centrilobular nodules, cavitating nodules, and bizarre-shaped cysts, usually with relative sparing of the lung bases and costophrenic angles.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse reticulonodular/cystic changes on chest radiograph
CT evidence of multiple bilateral irregular cysts and nodular/cavitating lesions, particularly in the upper lungs
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not explained by isolated lung-limited disease
Raised ALT is not typical of isolated pulmonary disease
Neutrophilia and elevated CRP are nonspecific
Age 15 years is less typical than adult presentation

data.description: An inherited CFTR-related disease causing chronic suppurative airways disease, upper-lobe-predominant bronchiectasis, recurrent respiratory infection, nutritional impairment, and possible hepatobiliary disease.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilia and raised CRP, compatible with airway infection/inflammation
Raised ALT, which can occur with CF-related liver disease
CT appearances that could include extensive cystic bronchiectatic change
symptoms_not_in_common: A crusting erythematous scalp rash is not a typical manifestation
No history of chronic cough, sputum production, recurrent chest infections, sinus disease, malabsorption, or pancreatic insufficiency is provided
The combination of pulmonary cysts/nodules and scalp disease is more suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis

data.diagnosis: Primary immunodeficiency with chronic suppurative lung disease, such as hyper-IgE syndrome
data.description: Some primary immunodeficiency disorders cause eczema-like skin disease, recurrent bacterial lung infections, pneumatoceles or bronchiectasis, and systemic inflammation. Hyper-IgE syndrome is one example, usually associated with markedly elevated IgE and eosinophilia.
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of recurrent severe skin or respiratory infections is reported
No eosinophilia, markedly elevated IgE, characteristic skeletal findings, or retained primary teeth are reported
Raised ALT is not a usual key feature

data.description: A 40-year-old woman presented with a palpable lump in her left superior breast. Mammography and US and biopsy performed, confirming invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2. MRI performed pre-operatively due to occult on mammography. Subsequent left breast mastectomy and reconstruction with right breast mastopexy.

data.diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), grade 2, left breast
data.description: The most common form of invasive breast cancer, previously termed invasive ductal carcinoma. It arises from breast ducts and infiltrates surrounding breast tissue. In this case, biopsy has confirmed grade 2 invasive carcinoma NST.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable lump in the superior left breast
Irregular hypoechoic breast mass on ultrasound measuring approximately 37 mm
Markedly enhancing irregular left-breast lesion on contrast-enhanced MRI
Biopsy confirmation of invasive carcinoma NST, grade 2
Mammographically occult lesion in dense breast tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No breast pain was reported
No nipple discharge was reported
No skin erythema, peau d'orange, or nipple retraction was reported
No systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fatigue were reported

data.diagnosis: Locally extensive or multifocal left breast invasive carcinoma
data.description: Breast MRI demonstrates a larger region of abnormal enhancement than may be visible on mammography, suggesting substantial local tumor extent and potentially multifocal or multicentric invasive disease within the left breast.
symptoms_in_common: MRI shows prominent irregular enhancing tissue in the left breast beyond what is apparent on mammography
Mastectomy was performed, consistent with disease extent unsuitable for straightforward breast-conserving treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: No multiple separately palpable breast lumps were reported
No diffuse breast enlargement was reported
No inflammatory skin changes were reported
No nipple symptoms were reported

data.diagnosis: Internal mammary lymph-node metastasis from left breast carcinoma
data.description: Metastatic spread of breast carcinoma can involve internal mammary lymph nodes along the parasternal chest wall. The MRI images show a suspicious enhancing focus in the internal mammary nodal region, which may represent nodal metastatic involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Known invasive carcinoma of the left breast
MRI-visible suspicious enhancing focus along the left internal mammary chain/chest-wall region
Primary breast lesion of sufficient size and enhancement to raise concern for regional nodal spread
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable internal mammary or chest-wall mass was reported
No chest pain was reported
No shortness of breath was reported
No systemic metastatic symptoms were reported

data.description: A 68-year-old woman with a longstanding history of non-specific inflammatory arthritis presented with a three-month history of flashing lights and blurred vision. She had been taking 400 mg hydroxychloroquine daily for 15 years, along with meloxicam, omeprazole, and amitriptyline. She was of normal body weight. Ophthalmological assessment revealed reduced visual acuity at 6/18 in the right eye and 6/12 in the left eye, with mild depression in color vision on Ishihara plate testing. Early cataracts were present.

Dose- and duration-related toxic retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor injury caused by hydroxychloroquine, classically producing bilateral parafoveal damage, ring scotomas, and a bull's-eye macular appearance.
symptoms_in_common: Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure: 400 mg daily for 15 years
Reduced visual acuity in both eyes
Fundus photographs consistent with subtle bilateral parafoveal pigmentary change
Fluorescein angiography showing bilateral parafoveal retinal pigment epithelial window defects consistent with bull's-eye maculopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Early cataracts, which may contribute to reduced acuity but do not explain the characteristic visual-field and angiographic abnormalities

data.description: An inherited retinal degeneration in which cone dysfunction occurs first, causing impaired central vision, color vision deficits, photopsias, and progressive visual-field loss; pigmentary macular changes may resemble a bull's-eye pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral macular retinal pigment epithelial changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Late onset at 68 years is less typical
No reported family history of retinal dystrophy
Very strong exposure history for hydroxychloroquine toxicity
The visual-field pattern and angiographic findings are more characteristic of hydroxychloroquine retinopathy in this clinical context
Early cataracts are not a defining feature

data.description: A degenerative macular disease of older adults characterized by drusen and retinal pigment epithelial atrophy, resulting in central visual impairment and reduced contrast or color perception.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral macular retinal pigment epithelial abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are not typical of uncomplicated dry AMD
Mild color vision loss is less characteristic as an early dominant feature
Ring-shaped paracentral visual-field defects are not typical
The images do not show prominent drusen or geographic atrophy typical of AMD
Long-term high-risk hydroxychloroquine exposure provides a more likely explanation

data.description: Lens opacification causing gradual painless reduction in visual acuity, glare, reduced contrast sensitivity, and sometimes reduced color discrimination.
symptoms_in_common: Early cataracts documented on ophthalmological examination
Mild reduction in color perception can occur with cataracts
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are not typical
Bilateral dense paracentral/ring visual-field defects are not explained by cataracts
Macular pigmentary changes on fundus examination are not caused by cataracts
Fluorescein angiographic parafoveal window defects are not caused by cataracts
The degree and pattern of retinal dysfunction are disproportionate to early cataracts

data.description: 50-year-old woman with right nasal congestion and right parotid swelling, unresponsive to antibiotics and steroids. Exam and nasal endoscopy showed right-predominant adenoid/nasopharyngeal swelling; CT demonstrated a 4.1 cm nasopharyngeal soft tissue mass. Initial biopsy showed atypical lymphoid hyperplasia with scattered large atypical cells. After adenoidectomy, MRI at 3 months showed recurrence; repeat endoscopic excision revealed a nodular lymphocytic infiltrate. PET-CT showed isolated FDG avidity in the nasopharynx without lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow biopsy was negative, consistent with stage IEA disease. Current smoker with a 35 pack-year history; otherwise no significant past medical history.

data.diagnosis: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, likely nodular sclerosis subtype, primary nasopharyngeal
data.description: A B-cell lymphoma characterized by rare Reed-Sternberg cells in a mixed inflammatory background. The image shows large atypical cells with morphology compatible with Reed-Sternberg cells and immunoreactivity for CD30 and CD15, supporting classic Hodgkin lymphoma. Disease confined to the nasopharynx is consistent with stage IEA extranodal Hodgkin lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided nasal congestion due to upper-airway obstruction
Atypical lymphoid infiltrate with scattered large atypical cells on biopsy
Large atypical cells positive for CD30 and CD15
No bone marrow involvement, compatible with early-stage disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Right parotid swelling is not a typical primary manifestation
No reported painless cervical or mediastinal lymphadenopathy
No reported B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss
Isolated nasopharyngeal involvement is rare for classic Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that can contain large pleomorphic malignant cells and may involve extranodal sites. It may mimic classic Hodgkin lymphoma histologically, but typical cases are usually CD15-negative and show T-cell-marker expression and/or ALK expression depending on subtype.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity favors classic Hodgkin lymphoma rather than anaplastic large cell lymphoma
The described Reed-Sternberg-like morphology in a mixed inflammatory background is more typical of classic Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported ALK positivity or T-cell immunophenotype
No reported systemic symptoms or disseminated nodal/extranodal disease

data.diagnosis: EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified
data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that may occur in extranodal locations and can feature large atypical cells, occasionally with Hodgkin-like morphology. It generally requires confirmation of B-cell marker expression and Epstein-Barr virus positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical lymphoid cells on biopsy
Persistent and recurrent lesion despite antibiotics and steroids
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 and CD30 coexpression in rare Reed-Sternberg-like cells is more characteristic of classic Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported diffuse sheets of large B cells
No reported B-cell-marker positivity such as CD20 or PAX5
No reported EBV testing or EBV positivity
Localized stage IEA disease without nodal involvement is less characteristic of this typically aggressive lymphoma

data.description: 83-year-old woman with hypertension and biopsy-proven vaginal melanoma diagnosed 4 months earlier, with invasive locoregional disease and a 3-mm left upper lobe lung nodule on PET-CT. She received four cycles of ipilimumab, last dose 3 weeks before admission. After the third dose she developed pruritus, lethargy, and malaise; after the fourth dose, diarrhea. For 2 weeks before admission, she had progressively worsening substernal chest pain and dyspnea. On admission, ECG showed sinus tachycardia and 1 mm ST elevations in I, V2, and V3; troponin-I was elevated. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 50% with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Cardiac angiography showed 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus.

An immune-mediated inflammatory myocarditis caused by CTLA-4 checkpoint inhibition, potentially producing myocardial injury, ST-segment changes, arrhythmias, heart failure, and nonobstructive coronary angiography findings.
symptoms_in_common: ST-segment elevations in leads I, V2, and V3
Only mild nonobstructive LAD disease on angiography
Recent ipilimumab treatment, with the last dose 3 weeks earlier
Systemic immune-related symptoms after treatment, including pruritus, lethargy, malaise, and diarrhea
Abnormal myocardial metabolic activity on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve is not a classic primary finding of myocarditis
Biopsy-proven vaginal melanoma is not caused by myocarditis

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium, sometimes with associated pericardial inflammation, that can mimic acute myocardial infarction with chest pain, ST elevation, and troponin release despite unobstructed coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: No angiographic thrombus or obstructive coronary lesion sufficient to explain the presentation
Possible inflammatory myocardial uptake on PET imaging
Recent immune-stimulating cancer therapy that can provoke cardiac inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No described pleuritic or positional chest pain
No reported pericardial friction rub or pericardial effusion
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior motion are not typical hallmark features

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction or ischemic myocardial injury meeting acute coronary syndrome criteria but without a flow-limiting epicardial coronary obstruction; potential mechanisms include coronary spasm, microvascular dysfunction, embolism, or myocarditis mimicking infarction.
symptoms_in_common: ST elevations in anterior and lateral leads
Only 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus on coronary angiography
Hypertension and advanced age as cardiovascular risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: The temporal relationship to ipilimumab and associated immune-related symptoms favors immune-mediated myocarditis over primary ischemic MINOCA
Pruritus and diarrhea are not typical manifestations of acute coronary syndrome
PET evidence of myocardial inflammatory activity would be atypical for simple ischemic MINOCA

data.diagnosis: Stress-induced cardiomyopathy with dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
data.description: A catecholamine- and stress-associated transient cardiac syndrome that can cause chest pain, dyspnea, ECG changes, troponin elevation, systolic dysfunction, and dynamic LV outflow obstruction with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve.
symptoms_in_common: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Severe physiologic and emotional stress related to advanced malignancy and immunotherapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Ejection fraction of 50% without a described characteristic regional wall-motion pattern is less typical
Pruritus, diarrhea, lethargy, and malaise after ipilimumab suggest systemic immune toxicity rather than isolated stress cardiomyopathy
Abnormal PET myocardial uptake is more suggestive of inflammation than stress cardiomyopathy

data.description: 33-year-old bisexual Brazilian man with a 4-month history of painful bowel movements and bright red rectal bleeding on toilet paper, with one daily stool. He denied abdominal pain and weight loss. He reported a same-sex sexual encounter about 6 weeks before presentation. Initial exam showed a tender external hemorrhoid and normal vital signs. Follow-up and surgical evaluation revealed bleeding hemorrhoids, large superficial anal fissures at the anterior and posterior midline anal verge with sentinel skin tags, and moderate tenderness on digital rectal exam. Anoscopy showed fissures and small internal hemorrhoids. Flexible sigmoidoscopy showed mild-to-moderate distal rectal mucosal inflammation with edema and patchy erythema. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV tests were negative.

Rectal infection with Treponema pallidum acquired through sexual contact, which can cause painful proctitis, rectal bleeding, fissure-like anal lesions, and inflammatory rectal mucosa. The biopsy pattern and brown spirochete immunostaining are highly supportive of this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Distal rectal mucosal inflammation with edema and erythema
Biopsy showing prominent inflammatory infiltrate consistent with syphilitic proctitis
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemical staining in rectal tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding external and internal hemorrhoids
Absence of systemic symptoms such as rash, fever, or generalized lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Lymphogranuloma venereum proctitis (rectal Chlamydia trachomatis infection)
data.description: An invasive sexually transmitted rectal infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1-L3, most commonly affecting men who have sex with men. It may cause painful proctitis, bleeding, rectal ulcers, and inflammatory endoscopic findings.
symptoms_in_common: Distal proctitis with erythema and edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Large chronic midline anal fissures with sentinel skin tags are less characteristic
No reported rectal discharge, mucus, tenesmus, fever, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Spirochete-positive tissue staining is not typical of chlamydial infection

data.description: Sexually acquired HSV infection of the anus and rectum that can produce severe anorectal pain, painful defecation, rectal bleeding, ulcerations, and distal proctitis.
symptoms_in_common: Superficial anal ulceration or fissure-like lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No grouped vesicles or characteristic painful perianal ulcer clusters were reported
Four-month persistent course is less typical for untreated acute HSV proctitis
Sentinel skin tags and chronic-appearing midline fissures are not classic HSV findings
Spirochete immunostaining is not consistent with HSV

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory bowel disease, particularly Crohn disease with perianal involvement
data.description: Crohn disease is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can involve the rectum and anus, producing proctitis, fissures, skin tags, rectal bleeding, and pain with defecation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain, weight loss, diarrhea, or increased stool frequency
Only one stool daily
Fissures are anterior and posterior midline rather than the more often multiple/lateral fissures of Crohn disease
No granulomas, chronic architectural distortion, or other classic Crohn disease histology is described
Spirochete-positive staining favors an infectious etiology rather than inflammatory bowel disease

data.description: Rectal infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae acquired through anal sexual contact. It can cause anorectal pain, rectal bleeding, inflammation, discharge, and tenesmus.
symptoms_not_in_common: No purulent rectal discharge or mucus was reported
No tenesmus or frequent stools
Large chronic fissures with sentinel tags are not typical manifestations
Spirochete-positive immunohistochemistry is not compatible with gonococcal proctitis

data.description: 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and prior laminectomy, never smoker, with a family history of prostate cancer in his father. He presented for evaluation; PSA and digital rectal examination were normal. Urine dipstick showed trace blood, with otherwise normal findings.
The presence of blood detected on urine testing without visible blood in the urine or urinary symptoms; it may be transient or due to urinary tract, kidney, or prostate conditions.

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder or upper urinary tract
data.description: Cancer arising from the lining of the bladder, ureters, or renal pelvis. Microscopic or visible hematuria can be the presenting finding, particularly in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Never smoker
No gross visible hematuria reported
No urinary frequency, urgency, dysuria, or pelvic pain reported

data.description: Mineral stones in the kidney or ureter that can cause microscopic hematuria, often with flank pain, nausea, or urinary symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank or abdominal pain reported
No nausea or vomiting reported
No dysuria or urinary urgency reported

data.description: Noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that commonly occurs with aging and may occasionally be associated with hematuria or urinary obstruction symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: No weak urinary stream reported
No hesitancy, nocturia, frequency, or incomplete bladder emptying reported
Digital rectal examination was normal

data.description: A kidney cancer that may present with microscopic hematuria; classic findings such as flank pain, a palpable mass, and visible hematuria are often absent early.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank pain reported
No visible hematuria reported
No palpable abdominal mass or constitutional symptoms reported

data.description: 20-year-old male with a history of neonatal bleeding tendency and conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis, evaluated preoperatively for chronic maxillary sinusitis surgery. He reported a family history of easy bruising in his father. Physical and routine laboratory tests were otherwise normal, but coagulation screening showed prolonged PT and aPTT with normal bleeding time; mixing studies suggested factor deficiency. Fibrinogen activity was markedly low by Clauss assay with normal fibrinogen antigen level. Parents had normal coagulation studies and fibrinogen activity.

data.diagnosis: Congenital dysfibrinogenemia due to an FGG gene variant
data.description: An inherited qualitative fibrinogen disorder in which fibrinogen antigen concentration is normal or near normal, but the fibrinogen molecule functions poorly. The sequencing image indicates an FGG gene sequence abnormality, supporting a genetic fibrinogen disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing study consistent with a coagulation factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor
Markedly low functional fibrinogen by Clauss assay
symptoms_not_in_common: Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A hereditary fibrinogen disorder characterized by both impaired fibrinogen function and reduced fibrinogen quantity. It may be caused by variants in FGA, FGB, or FGG and can cause bleeding, thrombosis, or no symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: History of bleeding since the neonatal period
Possible inherited pattern suggested by family history
Possible FGG sequence variant on genetic testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level, which favors dysfibrinogenemia rather than hypodysfibrinogenemia
Conductive hearing loss after meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: A severe inherited quantitative fibrinogen deficiency that usually presents early in life with significant bleeding and markedly reduced or absent fibrinogen antigen and activity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level
Relatively mild clinical bleeding history despite survival to adulthood without major reported hemorrhage
Normal bleeding time
Conductive hearing loss after meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: An acquired qualitative fibrinogen abnormality, most often associated with liver disease, plasma-cell disorders, autoimmune disease, or certain medications. It can produce disproportionately low functional fibrinogen with a normal antigen concentration.
symptoms_in_common: Low functional fibrinogen by Clauss assay
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding tendency beginning in the neonatal period
Family history of easy bruising
Genetic sequencing evidence involving FGG
No reported liver disease, malignancy, autoimmune disease, or other acquired cause
Conductive hearing loss after meningitis
Chronic maxillary sinusitis

data.description: 60-year-old man with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnea, worsening over the past 4 months, with persistent nonproductive cough. He developed a 5-day history of sore throat, neck and bilateral arm swelling, orthopnea, and facial flushing/redness, and was transferred for evaluation of new dyspnea, cough, neck swelling, and a lung mass. On examination at the outside hospital, he was afebrile, hemodynamically stable, with flushed face, swollen neck, and absent breath sounds in the right lung fields. History notable for heavy tobacco use (2 packs/day for 40 years), occasional marijuana use, and regular alcohol intake.

data.diagnosis: Large cell carcinoma of the lung (poorly differentiated non-small-cell lung carcinoma)
data.description: An aggressive non-small-cell lung cancer composed of large poorly differentiated malignant cells, often occurring in older heavy smokers. It may present as a central hilar mass with mediastinal invasion and metastases.
symptoms_in_common: Right hilar/central lung mass on imaging
Absent right-sided breath sounds consistent with major right-lung obstruction or collapse
Hypermetabolic lung mass on PET imaging
Cytology/histology showing large pleomorphic malignant cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 5-day onset of neck and bilateral arm swelling
Facial flushing/redness
Sore throat

data.diagnosis: Superior vena cava syndrome secondary to malignant mediastinal compression
data.description: A syndrome caused by obstruction of the superior vena cava, most commonly from lung cancer or mediastinal malignancy, resulting in impaired venous drainage from the head, neck, and upper extremities. Imaging demonstrates severe SVC narrowing/occlusion with collateral venous channels.
symptoms_in_common: Mediastinal/right hilar mass compressing or invading the superior vena cava
Prominent collateral venous circulation on contrast-enhanced CT
symptoms_not_in_common: One year of progressive exertional dyspnea preceding the acute swelling
Persistent nonproductive cough as the predominant chronic symptom
Absent breath sounds throughout the right lung fields
Sore throat

data.description: A highly aggressive neuroendocrine lung cancer strongly associated with cigarette smoking. It commonly arises centrally, causes bulky hilar and mediastinal disease, and frequently produces superior vena cava syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Neck and upper-extremity swelling from superior vena cava obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology showing relatively large pleomorphic tumor cells rather than classic small hyperchromatic cells with scant cytoplasm
No reported paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome
Sore throat
Absent right-sided breath sounds, which more specifically suggests major airway obstruction or lung collapse

data.description: A non-small-cell lung carcinoma associated with smoking that often arises in central bronchi. It can form an endobronchial obstructing mass and invade mediastinal structures, including the superior vena cava.
symptoms_in_common: Absent breath sounds on the right suggesting bronchial obstruction or atelectasis
Superior vena cava syndrome manifestations including neck swelling, arm swelling, and facial redness
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hemoptysis
No reported cavitary lung lesion
Pathology description does not clearly show keratinization or intercellular bridges
Sore throat
