The focal pontine hyperdensity on CT is compatible with acute blood, and ventricular dilatation may reflect obstructive hydrocephalus from posterior fossa hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Ataxia, tremor, and dysdiadochokinesia from pontocerebellar involvement
CT evidence of focal pontine hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 29 years
Only mild hypertension rather than longstanding severe hypertension
Alertness and preserved consciousness despite pontine bleeding
Absence of severe cranial-nerve palsies, pinpoint pupils, coma, or quadriplegia that may occur with larger hypertensive pontine hemorrhages

data.diagnosis: Posterior circulation ischemic stroke from vertebral artery dissection, with hemorrhagic transformation
data.description: Vertebral artery dissection can occur in young adults and often presents with unilateral neck pain or headache followed by posterior-circulation ischemia involving the brainstem or cerebellum. Infarcted tissue can occasionally undergo hemorrhagic transformation, producing a focal hyperdense area on CT.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided neck pain radiating to the head
Upper motor neuron sign with right extensor plantar response
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appearance is more directly suggestive of primary focal pontine hemorrhage than a clearly demonstrated ischemic infarct
No reported recent neck trauma, chiropractic manipulation, or strenuous neck movement
No vascular imaging evidence of vertebral artery dissection is provided
Ventricular enlargement is less typical of a small ischemic brainstem stroke

data.description: 18-year-old male with 4 days of fatigue, subjective fever, chills, headache, non-bilious nonbloody vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, low back pain, dysuria, and fever with pain in the lower abdomen, groin, and scrotum. Past history includes exercise-induced asthma and childhood hospitalization for diarrhea; born in Central America and moved to the US at age 15. Recent tests were negative for tuberculosis IGRA, HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia. On examination, he was tired-appearing, febrile to 39.4°C, tachycardic, tachypneic, and had tenderness of the low paraspinal muscles.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with bone marrow involvement
data.description: Systemic infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. The images are compatible with small intracellular yeast forms within macrophages in bone marrow, highlighted by fungal staining, which is characteristic of disseminated histoplasmosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible reticuloendothelial or bone marrow involvement suggested by the histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria
Groin and scrotal pain
Acute focal paraspinal muscle tenderness

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania species, acquired through sandfly exposure. Amastigotes may be seen within macrophages in bone marrow and can resemble Histoplasma on routine microscopy.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intracellular organisms in marrow macrophages
Birth in Central America, where some Leishmania species are endemic
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute 4-day presentation
Dysuria
Groin and scrotal pain
Low paraspinal muscle tenderness
No reported splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, pancytopenia, or prolonged weight loss

data.diagnosis: Iliopsoas or pelvic pyomyositis with sepsis
data.description: Bacterial infection of pelvic or paraspinal muscles, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus, producing fever, systemic illness, abdominal or back pain, and pain radiating to the groin. The pelvic imaging suggests inflammatory change involving pelvic musculature.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Dysuria
Scrotal pain
Bone marrow intracellular yeast-like organisms on pathology

data.diagnosis: Genitourinary bacterial infection with acute prostatitis or epididymo-orchitis
data.description: A bacterial infection of the prostate, epididymis, testis, or urinary tract can cause fever, dysuria, pelvic pain, groin pain, scrotal pain, and systemic inflammatory symptoms. Negative gonorrhea and chlamydia testing reduces the likelihood of common sexually transmitted causes but does not exclude enteric urinary pathogens.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea as a prominent early symptom
Low paraspinal muscle tenderness
Bone marrow findings showing intracellular fungal or protozoal organisms
Imaging evidence suggestive of deeper pelvic muscular inflammation rather than isolated genitourinary disease

data.description: This is a 56-year-old woman who underwent radical nephrectomy and lymph-node resection for clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma in February 2012. During subsequent follow-up, a single metastasis to the body of the left mandible was detected. She was referred in October 2012 for resection of the mandibular metastasis and fibular free-flap reconstruction. Two months later, bone scintigraphy revealed good vascularization of the flap, though additional bone metastases to the right humerus and pelvis were detected. In January 2014, the patient presented with visible bone exposure in the area of the graft with inflammation of surrounding tissues. Over days, there was an increase in bone exposure and necrosis without evidence of acute secondary infection.

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), likely antiresorptive-associated
data.description: Progressive jawbone necrosis with exposed nonhealing bone, commonly associated with bisphosphonates or denosumab used for skeletal metastases. It may occur without acute infection and can affect reconstructed bone.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive visible bone exposure in the mandibular graft region
Inflammation of surrounding oral soft tissues
No evidence of acute secondary infection
History of metastatic cancer with additional humeral and pelvic bone metastases, a setting in which antiresorptive therapy is commonly used
CT appearance consistent with destructive and sequestrum-like mandibular bone changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No antiresorptive medication history is explicitly provided
The affected bone is a vascularized fibular free flap rather than native mandible
Prior mandibular metastasis and major reconstructive surgery provide alternative local causes

data.diagnosis: Chronic osteomyelitis of the reconstructed mandible
data.description: Chronic infection and inflammation of bone that can cause sequestration, bone exposure, fistula formation, and progressive osseous destruction, particularly after major mandibular surgery or reconstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of irregular destructive osseous changes and possible sequestration
symptoms_not_in_common: No evidence of acute secondary infection
No reported fever, purulent drainage, severe pain, or systemic inflammatory symptoms
Rapid progression of exposed necrotic bone without overt infection is more suggestive of osteonecrosis than primary infectious osteomyelitis

data.diagnosis: Recurrent or progressive metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma involving the mandible/fibular graft
data.description: Clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma can metastasize to bone and may produce destructive, often hypervascular osteolytic lesions. Local recurrence or metastatic involvement of the reconstructed mandibular region could cause bone destruction and mucosal breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Prior metastasis to the left mandibular body
Additional documented skeletal metastases in the right humerus and pelvis
Progressive destructive changes in the mandibular reconstruction region
Inflammation and mucosal breakdown over the affected bone
symptoms_not_in_common: Exposed devitalized bone and sequestrum-like necrosis are not the most typical primary presentation of metastatic renal-cell carcinoma
No reported enhancing soft-tissue mass, bleeding lesion, or new tumor mass
No acute infection does not specifically support metastatic recurrence

data.diagnosis: Ischemic necrosis or failure of the fibular free-flap bone graft
data.description: Compromised perfusion, chronic vascular insufficiency, mechanical stress, or impaired healing of a vascularized osseous flap can lead to graft bone necrosis, exposure, and progressive loss of reconstructed mandibular bone.
symptoms_in_common: Necrosis located specifically in the fibular graft area
Prior complex mandibular resection and fibular free-flap reconstruction
Destructive appearance of the reconstructed mandibular segment
symptoms_not_in_common: Bone scintigraphy two months after reconstruction showed good flap vascularization
The late timing, more than a year after flap reconstruction, is less typical of early flap vascular failure
Concurrent metastatic disease and possible antiresorptive treatment provide competing explanations for osteonecrosis

data.description: 67-year-old man with 10 days of nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain initially treated with omeprazole without relief, followed on presentation day by exertional substernal nonradiating chest heaviness that progressed to rest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea. History includes mild asthma, hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps, ventral abdominal hernia, and remote 20 pack-year smoking. Exam showed tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnea, mild hypoxemia on oxygen, pallor, diaphoresis, accessory muscle use, elevated jugular venous pressure, grade 2/6 holosystolic apical murmur, left basilar rales, palpable hepatomegaly, and cool, clammy extremities with thready pulses.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized histologically by multinucleated giant cells, extensive myocardial inflammation, and myocyte necrosis. It can cause fulminant heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and can mimic acute coronary syndrome. The myocardial biopsy image is highly supportive, showing inflammatory infiltrates, myocyte injury, and giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal chest heaviness progressing from exertional to rest pain
Holosystolic apical murmur compatible with functional mitral regurgitation
Left basilar rales consistent with pulmonary congestion
Hepatomegaly consistent with congestive heart failure
Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
ECG abnormalities with poor anterior R-wave progression/QS-type anterior complexes
Chest radiograph findings compatible with pulmonary vascular/interstitial congestion
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of prominent nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain are not classic presenting features, although they may reflect low cardiac output or hepatic/intestinal congestion

data.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle, often viral or immune mediated, producing chest pain, heart failure, arrhythmias, and occasionally shock. Biopsy typically shows lymphocytic inflammation with myocyte necrosis; however, the presence of numerous giant cells would favor giant cell myocarditis over routine lymphocytic myocarditis.
symptoms_in_common: Cool extremities and poor peripheral perfusion
Possible new functional mitral regurgitation from ventricular dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported preceding viral syndrome, fever, myalgias, or upper-respiratory symptoms
The biopsy appearance of multinucleated giant cells is not typical of ordinary lymphocytic myocarditis
Prolonged nausea, vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain are not typical primary manifestations

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock
data.description: Acute coronary artery occlusion causes myocardial ischemia and necrosis, typically presenting with chest pressure, diaphoresis, dyspnea, ECG ischemic changes, and potentially cardiogenic shock with pulmonary edema and functional mitral regurgitation. The clinical syndrome strongly resembles this condition, but biopsy evidence of inflammatory giant-cell myocarditis argues against infarction as the primary diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional substernal chest heaviness progressing to rest pain
Hypotension and cool clammy extremities suggesting cardiogenic shock
Pulmonary rales and hypoxemia suggesting acute left-sided heart failure
Elevated jugular venous pressure and hepatomegaly suggesting biventricular congestion
New apical holosystolic murmur, which may occur with ischemic functional mitral regurgitation
Remote smoking history as a coronary risk factor
Anterior ECG abnormalities that could raise concern for prior or acute anterior ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of nausea, vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain before the chest symptoms are atypical for a single abrupt infarction
Myocardial biopsy showing diffuse inflammatory infiltrates and multinucleated giant cells is not typical of ischemic infarction
No described focal ST-segment elevation pattern typical of an acute transmural STEMI

data.description: An inflammatory myocardial disease caused by eosinophil-rich infiltration, sometimes related to medications, hypersensitivity reactions, infections, autoimmune disease, or hypereosinophilic syndromes. It may present with chest pain, heart failure, arrhythmias, and cardiogenic shock. Histology generally demonstrates prominent eosinophils rather than giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiogenic shock physiology with cool clammy extremities
ECG abnormalities compatible with myocardial inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported rash, fever, peripheral eosinophilia, allergic reaction, or recent new medication exposure
The biopsy is more suggestive of giant cell myocarditis than eosinophil-predominant inflammation
Nausea, vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain are not characteristic presenting symptoms

data.description: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before plastic surgery on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A rare autosomal-dominant calcium-channel disorder caused by pathogenic CACNA1C variants, classically including marked QT prolongation, ventricular arrhythmias/sudden cardiac arrest, syndactyly, characteristic facial appearance, and variable developmental or extracardiac abnormalities. The depicted heterozygous CACNA1C c.1216G>A (p.Gly406Arg) variant is the classic Timothy syndrome variant.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
ECG evidence of prolonged QT interval and abnormal T-wave morphology
Likely ventricular electrical instability, including T-wave alternans
Characteristic facial features including round face, small upper jaw/teeth, and sparse scalp hair
Normal echocardiogram without structural heart disease
Normal electrolytes and biochemical testing, supporting a primary electrical disorder
Family member with paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine stress testing
Heterozygous CACNA1C p.Gly406Arg variant shown in the genetic image
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal toes without syndactyly, whereas classic Timothy syndrome usually has hand and foot syndactyly
Normal neurodevelopment, whereas developmental delay and neurodevelopmental abnormalities are common in classic Timothy syndrome
No history of seizures
No prior syncope despite severe arrhythmic risk

data.diagnosis: Atypical Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related disorder without syndactyly)
data.description: An atypical form of CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome in which severe QT prolongation and malignant ventricular arrhythmias occur with some Timothy syndrome facial features but without the classic syndactyly. This phenotype can be associated with the p.Gly406Arg CACNA1C variant depending on transcript involvement and tissue expression.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest precipitated by anesthetic exposure
QT prolongation and abnormal T-wave findings on ECG
No structural cardiac abnormality on echocardiography
Characteristic craniofacial appearance and sparse hair
Family evidence of latent catecholamine-associated QT prolongation
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior syncope or documented arrhythmia before anesthesia
No seizures
Normal neurodevelopment, although neurologic involvement can occur in CACNA1C-related disease

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome due to CACNA1C (LQT8)
data.description: A congenital cardiac channelopathy caused by CACNA1C variants that prolong ventricular repolarization and predispose to torsades de pointes, ventricular fibrillation, syncope, and sudden cardiac arrest. Timothy syndrome is the syndromic form of LQT8.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal T-wave morphology and apparent beat-to-beat T-wave variability
Normal cardiac structure and ventricular function
Family member with abnormal QT response to epinephrine
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinctive facial features are not typical of isolated nonsyndromic long QT syndrome
Sparse scalp hair is not typical of isolated nonsyndromic long QT syndrome
No history of syncope, palpitations, or seizures before the arrest

data.description: 27-year-old man with a history of ulcerative colitis presented with 2 weeks of fatigue and persistent nonbloody diarrhea with bloating starting after moving from Indonesia to the United States 11 days before admission. He reported decreased exercise tolerance and about 4.5 kg weight loss over recent weeks. He had traveled to rural India in the prior month. Medications included mesalamine and acetaminophen. On examination, vital signs were normal; the spleen tip was palpable, and an erythematous papular rash was present on the anterior thorax. Labs showed marked leukocytosis with severe eosinophilia, thrombocytosis, mild hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, hypoalbuminemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase and AST, and mild coagulopathy.

A soil-transmitted intestinal nematode infection acquired in tropical and subtropical regions. Chronic infection can cause intermittent diarrhea, abdominal symptoms, rash, weight loss, and prominent eosinophilia; gastrointestinal biopsies may show eosinophil-rich inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent residence in Indonesia and travel to rural India
Eosinophil-rich peripheral blood, bone marrow, and colonic inflammatory infiltrates on the images
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported serpiginous rapidly migrating rash (larva currens)
No cough, wheezing, or pulmonary infiltrates
No immunosuppressive corticosteroid exposure or features of hyperinfection syndrome
Hypoglycemia is not a typical presenting feature

data.diagnosis: Secondary hypereosinophilic syndrome due to parasitic infection
data.description: A marked and persistent elevation in eosinophils caused by a reactive process, commonly helminth infection. Eosinophils may infiltrate the gastrointestinal tract, skin, liver, spleen, and bone marrow, producing systemic symptoms and organ dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Bone marrow image showing marked eosinophilic hyperplasia
symptoms_not_in_common: A definite duration of eosinophilia longer than 6 months is not described
No documented cardiac, neurologic, pulmonary, or thrombotic eosinophil-mediated organ injury
Recent tropical travel favors a secondary parasitic cause rather than primary idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome

data.description: An eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorder in which eosinophils infiltrate the bowel wall and cause diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, malabsorption, protein loss, and sometimes peripheral eosinophilia. It may be primary or secondary to parasites, drugs, or inflammatory bowel disease.
symptoms_in_common: Colonic biopsy image showing dense eosinophilic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent exposure in helminth-endemic areas suggests a parasitic trigger rather than isolated primary eosinophilic colitis
Marked splenomegaly is not typical
Marked thrombocytosis and severe systemic leukocytosis are less typical
Papular rash and liver-test abnormalities are not core manifestations

data.description: A trematode infection acquired through freshwater exposure in endemic regions. Intestinal disease may cause diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, eosinophilia, and hepatosplenic involvement; diagnosis is supported by ova in stool or tissue biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to rural India and prior residence in Indonesia
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported freshwater exposure
No schistosome eggs are identified in the provided colonic biopsy image
No fever, urticaria, or acute Katayama syndrome symptoms
Papular thoracic rash is not the typical cercarial dermatitis distribution

data.description: A relapse of chronic ulcerative colitis causes colonic mucosal inflammation, diarrhea, urgency, abdominal pain, and systemic effects such as fatigue and weight loss. However, pronounced eosinophilia should prompt evaluation for a superimposed parasitic or eosinophilic disorder.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is nonbloody
Severe eosinophilia is unusual for a routine ulcerative colitis flare
Papular rash is not typical of an uncomplicated flare
Palpable splenomegaly is not typical
Recent travel to helminth-endemic areas strongly suggests an alternative or superimposed infectious cause
Bone marrow eosinophilic hyperplasia is not typical of isolated ulcerative colitis

data.description: 28-year-old male who suddenly went into coma for 9 hours preceded by tonic-clonic seizures lasting 10 minutes. No fever, vomiting or micturition. No focal neurological signs. Past medical history was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed normal cranial nerves, normal power and reflexes. Routine laboratory tests were normal.

An aggressive diffuse astrocytic glioma that can present as a necrotic, ring-enhancing intra-axial mass with extensive vasogenic edema and intratumoral hemorrhage. The pathology images show glial-marker positivity (GFAP and Olig2), absent IDH1 staining, retained ATRX expression, p53 positivity, and elevated proliferative activity, supporting a high-grade IDH-wildtype glioma.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged postictal coma or depressed consciousness
Ring-enhancing lesion with central necrosis and surrounding edema on MRI
No focal neurological deficit can occur despite a frontal glioma
symptoms_not_in_common: Very sudden presentation without preceding headache or progressive neurological symptoms
Young age of 28 years is less typical than older-adult presentation
No reported cognitive, personality, language, or focal motor symptoms

data.description: A histologic variant of glioblastoma that often affects relatively younger patients and may present as a superficially located cerebral hemispheric mass with hemorrhage, necrosis, edema, and seizures. Molecular testing, particularly for BRAF V600E mutation, would be needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Age younger than typical conventional glioblastoma patients
Glial immunophenotype with GFAP and Olig2 positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding headache or other signs of raised intracranial pressure
No persistent focal deficit
Epithelioid cellular morphology and BRAF V600E molecular result are not provided

data.description: A malignant infiltrating astrocytic tumor that can cause seizures and may enhance after contrast administration. Some tumors can undergo necrosis or hemorrhage, although the marked ring enhancement and central necrosis in this case favor glioblastoma over a lower-grade or grade 3 astrocytoma.
symptoms_in_common: Astrocytic differentiation suggested by GFAP positivity
Possible normal neurological examination early in the disease course
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent intratumoral hemorrhage is less typical
Well-developed necrotic ring-enhancing appearance is more typical of glioblastoma
Abrupt coma is less typical without major hemorrhage or severe mass effect
Extensive edema relative to lesion size favors a more aggressive lesion

data.description: Metastatic tumors can produce a sharply demarcated ring-enhancing brain lesion with marked vasogenic edema, seizures, and hemorrhage. However, the young age, absence of known systemic cancer, solitary frontal lesion, and glial-marker-positive pathology make metastasis substantially less likely than a primary glioma.
symptoms_in_common: Ring enhancement with surrounding vasogenic edema
No focal neurological signs may occur initially
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy
Young age
Solitary lesion rather than multiple lesions
GFAP and Olig2 positivity supports glial origin rather than metastatic carcinoma
No systemic symptoms or abnormal routine laboratory findings

data.description: 82-year-old man with 6 months of worsening back and left hip pain, worse with activity and sometimes waking him from sleep, without leg radiation, morning stiffness, fever, chills, night sweats, or bowel/bladder incontinence. He reported 9 kg weight loss over several months, and the pain began after recovery from pneumonia treated with levofloxacin. Past history includes sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary fibrosis, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, gout, herpes zoster with postherpetic neuralgia, and basal-cell carcinoma. On exam, he was afebrile and in no acute distress, with no spinal or sacroiliac tenderness, normal hip exam, no neurologic deficits, slightly diminished patellar reflexes bilaterally, intact sensation, normal rectal tone, and negative straight-leg raise.

Disseminated infection with Blastomyces species, a dimorphic fungus that can begin as pulmonary disease and spread hematogenously to bone, causing destructive vertebral osteomyelitis and paraspinal soft-tissue infection. The imaging shows destructive lumbar endplate/vertebral changes with adjacent soft-tissue abnormality, and the histology is consistent with thick-walled budding yeast.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic progressive back and left hip pain
Pain that sometimes wakes him from sleep
History of pneumonia preceding onset of musculoskeletal symptoms
Lumbar vertebral destructive lesion with adjacent soft-tissue involvement on CT
Absence of radicular pain or major neurologic deficits can occur in vertebral blastomycosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No chills
No night sweats
No focal spinal tenderness
No bowel or bladder dysfunction

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine, typically causing an indolent destructive spondylodiscitis with paravertebral soft-tissue collections, constitutional symptoms, and possible pulmonary involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute to chronic worsening back pain
Vertebral body and endplate destruction with paraspinal soft-tissue abnormality on imaging
Pulmonary abnormalities could be compatible with prior or active granulomatous infection
Lack of neurologic deficits early in the course
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No chills
No known tuberculosis exposure or prior tuberculosis history
No spinal tenderness
No neurologic compromise despite prolonged symptoms

data.description: Bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates, commonly due to Staphylococcus aureus or gram-negative organisms. It causes back pain and may produce epidural or paraspinal inflammatory collections.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced age and multiple chronic illnesses increase susceptibility
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No chills
No systemic toxic appearance
No focal spinal tenderness
Six-month indolent course is less typical for routine pyogenic infection
No neurologic deficits or bowel/bladder symptoms

data.description: Disseminated infection with Coccidioides species can cause pulmonary disease followed by skeletal dissemination, including destructive vertebral osteomyelitis. Tissue usually shows characteristic spherules containing endospores rather than budding yeast.
symptoms_in_common: History of pulmonary illness before onset of bone symptoms
Destructive vertebral lesion with soft-tissue extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No chills
No reported residence in or travel to an endemic desert region
Histologic appearance of budding yeast would favor blastomycosis rather than Coccidioides spherules

data.diagnosis: Metastatic malignancy involving the lumbar spine
data.description: Metastatic cancer can produce progressive, activity-related or nocturnal back pain, weight loss, and destructive vertebral lesions. Common primary sites in older men include prostate, lung, kidney, thyroid, and multiple myeloma-related disease.
symptoms_in_common: History of prior basal-cell carcinoma, although this rarely metastasizes
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging pattern involving disc/endplate destruction and paraspinal inflammatory soft tissue is more suggestive of infection
No known primary metastatic cancer
No neurologic deficits
No focal spinal tenderness
Tissue fungal forms on pathology would not be expected in metastatic cancer

data.description: A 47-year-old woman presented with intermittent cough, shortness of breath, fever (body temperature up to 38.5°C), accompanied by right eyelid swelling around June 17, 2017, which worsened day by day. Weight loss was about 9 kg. Physical examination included high body temperature of 39°C, right eyelid swelling, and a painless enlarged lymph node about 2 cm × 2 cm in size in the left axilla. Auscultation of lungs revealed coarse respiratory sounds with moist rale. No hepatosplenomegaly and edema in lower limbs.

A systemic fungal infection that commonly begins in the lungs after inhalation and can disseminate to skin, lymph nodes, eyes/orbits, and the central nervous system. The pulmonary CT pattern of multiple nodules and the tissue images showing yeast-like organisms are highly compatible.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and infiltrative opacities on CT
Right eyelid swelling, which can occur with orbital or cutaneous dissemination
Histologic appearance of fungal yeast-like organisms within inflamed adipose/soft tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, altered mental status, neck stiffness, or other reported symptoms of cryptococcal meningitis
No reported hepatosplenomegaly
No lower-limb edema

data.description: A systemic dimorphic fungal infection that may cause fever, weight loss, diffuse pulmonary disease, lymphadenopathy, and skin or soft-tissue lesions, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Histology may show numerous small yeast-like organisms in tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary nodules and diffuse lung infiltrates
Fungal organisms seen in tissue sections
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical disseminated papular skin lesions with central umbilication were described
No hepatosplenomegaly
No stated immunodeficiency or HIV infection
Orbital/eyelid involvement is less typical than cutaneous lesions

data.description: A fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species that can produce constitutional symptoms, diffuse pulmonary nodules, lymph-node enlargement, and dissemination to skin and soft tissue. Tissue typically shows small intracellular yeast forms in macrophages.
symptoms_in_common: Possible yeast-form fungal organisms in tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Right eyelid swelling is an uncommon manifestation
No hepatosplenomegaly
No oral ulcers, gastrointestinal symptoms, or cytopenia information was reported
No known exposure history to bat or bird droppings was provided

data.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Nocardia bacteria that can cause nodular or cavitary lung disease and can spread to skin, soft tissue, brain, and eyes. It may resemble fungal infection on imaging and can cause prolonged fever and weight loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: The tissue images appear more suggestive of yeast-like fungal organisms than branching filamentous bacteria
No brain abscess symptoms or neurologic symptoms were reported
No immunosuppressive condition was stated
Painless axillary lymphadenopathy is less characteristic

data.description: A 19-year-old previously healthy gravida 3 para 2002 female presented at 28 weeks' gestation after emigrating to the U.S. at 25 weeks of gestation. During the 20th week of gestation, she experienced a maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache. She and her spouse had unprotected intercourse through the first and second trimester. The patient's initial fetal ultrasound with neurosonography revealed cerebral ventriculomegaly (20-25 mm) with dangling choroid, prominent 3rd ventricle, and a widened cavum septum pellucidum. Amniocentesis showed negative NAT for ZIKV with no evidence of chromosomal variations by CMA; TORCH panel was negative.

data.diagnosis: Congenital Zika syndrome due to in utero Zika virus infection
data.description: A congenital viral infection caused by transplacental Zika virus transmission, associated with fetal brain injury including ventriculomegaly, cortical malformations, corpus callosum/cavum septum pellucidum abnormalities, calcifications, and sometimes microcephaly. Maternal infection is often mild and may be sexually transmitted.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in a Zika-endemic area during pregnancy
Unprotected sexual intercourse with spouse during the first and second trimesters, supporting possible sexual transmission
Severe bilateral fetal cerebral ventriculomegaly with dangling choroid
Fetal MRI/ultrasound evidence of major central nervous system structural abnormality
Negative TORCH evaluation and normal chromosomal microarray, supporting a non-TORCH infectious cause
symptoms_not_in_common: No fetal microcephaly was identified
Amniotic-fluid Zika NAT was negative, although this does not exclude congenital Zika infection because viral shedding in amniotic fluid may be intermittent or absent

data.description: Congenital CMV is a common fetal viral infection that can cause ventriculomegaly, periventricular calcifications, cortical developmental abnormalities, growth restriction, microcephaly, hearing loss, and hepatosplenomegaly.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal viral-like illness with fever and headache can occur with primary CMV infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are less characteristic of CMV than of Zika virus infection
TORCH testing was negative for CMV
No reported fetal intracranial calcifications
No reported fetal growth restriction
No fetal microcephaly
No reported hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, anemia, or placental enlargement

data.diagnosis: Fetal aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct can cause enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, producing severe ventriculomegaly and dangling choroid plexuses. It may be isolated, genetic, or secondary to infection or hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Dangling choroid plexus, consistent with severe ventriculomegaly
Prominent third ventricle, which can occur with obstruction at the cerebral aqueduct
Absence of chromosomal abnormalities on chromosomal microarray
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, fever, headache, and conjunctivitis are not explained by isolated aqueductal stenosis
The widened/dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum and broader brain abnormalities suggest a more diffuse congenital brain injury rather than isolated obstruction
Epidemiologic exposure in a Zika-endemic region and possible sexual transmission are not typical features of isolated aqueductal stenosis

data.description: This case is a 26-year-old Chinese female patient who presented with a 2-year history of progressive weakness of lower limbs and scissors gait that began at age 24. As her gait abnormality progressed, she developed dysphagia and severe cognitive impairment with a mini-mental state examination (MMSE) score of 16/30. The spasticity was severe in the lower extremities and mild in the upper extremities. Physical examination revealed patellar clonus on the left side. Her birth history and developmental milestones were normal. She was initially classified as sporadic HSP, though genetic testing later revealed she had compound heterozygous mutations indicating autosomal recessive inheritance.

data.diagnosis: SPG11-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (Spastic paraplegia type 11, Kjellin syndrome spectrum)
data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 mutations. It commonly produces progressive lower-limb spasticity, cognitive decline, dysphagia/dysarthria, peripheral neuropathy, and characteristic thinning of the corpus callosum with periventricular white-matter abnormalities on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment with low MMSE score
MRI appearance consistent with thinning of the corpus callosum and periventricular white-matter changes
Compound heterozygous SPG11 variants (p.M245fs and p.F2343fs), consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

data.diagnosis: SPG15-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (Spastic paraplegia type 15)
data.description: A complicated autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by ZFYVE26 mutations. It can closely resemble SPG11, with progressive spastic paraparesis, cognitive decline, dysphagia, peripheral neuropathy, and thinning of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic weakness of the lower limbs
Possible corpus callosum thinning and white-matter abnormalities on MRI
Autosomal recessive pattern is compatible with compound heterozygous variants
symptoms_not_in_common: Genetic testing identifies pathogenic variants in SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26

data.diagnosis: SPG47-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia (Spastic paraplegia type 47)
data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by AP4B1 mutations. It is associated with spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability, speech or swallowing difficulties, and sometimes corpus callosum or white-matter abnormalities, although onset is usually earlier in childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Spastic paraplegia with severe lower-limb involvement
White-matter and corpus callosum abnormalities can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal childhood development and developmental milestones
Onset at age 24 rather than the usual childhood onset
Genetic testing supports SPG11 rather than AP4B1 mutations

data.description: A peroxisomal disorder caused by ABCD1 mutations that may cause progressive spastic paraparesis, gait impairment, bladder dysfunction, peripheral neuropathy, and cerebral white-matter disease. Female carriers can develop myelopathy, but severe early cognitive disease is less typical in women.
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex with severe cognitive impairment at a young age is less typical
Dysphagia is not a usual early feature
MRI finding of corpus callosum thinning is more characteristic of SPG11-related disease
Compound heterozygous SPG11 mutations provide a more direct genetic explanation

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: A 25-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension up to 230/130 for three weeks. Her medical history was negative for previous hypertension, and physical examination was unremarkable. Initial work-up excluded pre-eclampsia. Her urine catecholamines were markedly elevated: Dopamine 607 μg/24 hours (range 65-400), Norepinephrine 978 μg/24 hours (range 15-80), Metanephrine 108 μg/24 hours (range 24-96), Normetanephrine 4067 μg/24 hours (range 75-375), and Vanillyl mandelic acid 13.6 mg/24 hours (range 2-7). Epinephrine level was normal at 0.8 μg/24 hours (range 0.0-20.0). Initial abdominal MRI showed a 28×19 mm left juxta-adrenal mass that was later found to be brown fat.

A rare extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumor arising from sympathetic paraganglia in the mediastinum, often near the heart or great vessels. It can secrete norepinephrine and cause catecholamine crises. The intensely avid mediastinal mass on functional imaging and the enhancing para-cardiac mass on MRI support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Normal epinephrine, which is compatible with many extra-adrenal sympathetic paragangliomas
Mediastinal mass adjacent to the heart/great vessels with intense functional-imaging uptake
No convincing adrenal tumor after the initial juxta-adrenal finding was identified as brown fat

data.description: A subtype of mediastinal paraganglioma located in or adjacent to the heart, commonly near the left atrium, aortic root, pulmonary artery, or coronary vessels. Functional cardiac paragangliomas can produce predominantly norepinephrine and present with episodic adrenergic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Para-cardiac mass demonstrated on cardiac MRI
Marked tracer uptake in a mass located centrally in the mediastinum near the heart
Lack of an adrenal pheochromocytoma on subsequent evaluation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported arrhythmia, chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, or heart-failure symptoms, which can occur with cardiac involvement

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of the adrenal medulla that classically causes episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and severe hypertension. It is an important consideration in pregnancy but is less supported here because the apparent juxta-adrenal lesion was brown fat and imaging identifies a mediastinal lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Marked elevation of urinary catecholamines and catecholamine metabolites
symptoms_not_in_common: No confirmed adrenal mass
Initial left juxta-adrenal lesion was subsequently identified as brown fat
Dominant lesion is in the mediastinum near the heart rather than the adrenal gland
Normal epinephrine level, whereas many adrenal pheochromocytomas produce epinephrine

data.description: A pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder occurring after 20 weeks of gestation, usually associated with proteinuria and/or maternal end-organ dysfunction. It is a critical alternative diagnosis for third-trimester severe hypertension but does not explain marked catecholamine excess or the mediastinal functional mass.
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal palpitations and sweating
Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine, normetanephrine, dopamine, and vanillylmandelic acid
Intensely tracer-avid mediastinal para-cardiac mass
Pre-eclampsia was excluded during the initial work-up
No reported proteinuria, thrombocytopenia, liver dysfunction, renal impairment, or fetal-growth concerns

data.description: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of headache and fatigue, followed by sudden onset of confusion and language production difficulties while typing at work. The confusion resolved briefly but recurred later that evening. She had a history of myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 18 years prior, treated with mycophenolate mofetil for 7 years), vitamin B12 deficiency, and hypertension. Past surgical history included supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (31 years prior), transsternal thymectomy and wedge resection of right upper lobe for cortical thymoma (22 years prior), and sigmoid colectomy for recurrent diverticulitis (7 years prior). On examination at the current hospital, she had severe expressive aphasia, followed commands intermittently, disconjugate gaze at rest, motor strength 5/5 in left extremities and 4/5 in right extremities. Blood phosphorus was 2.2 mg/dL (reference range 2.6-4.5); other routine labs were normal.

data.diagnosis: Nocardia brain abscess (cerebral nocardiosis, possibly Nocardia farcinica)
data.description: An opportunistic bacterial infection caused by Nocardia species, often occurring in patients with impaired cell-mediated immunity. It can produce a multiloculated, ring-enhancing cerebral abscess with surrounding edema, hemorrhage, and neutrophilic inflammation. The imaging and microbiology images are compatible with a brain abscess caused by branching gram-positive organisms.
symptoms_in_common: Brain lesion with edema and ring-like enhancement
Immunosuppression from long-term mycophenolate mofetil therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Disconjugate gaze
Mild hypophosphatemia
Brief spontaneous resolution of confusion before recurrence

data.description: A localized intracranial collection of pus caused by bacterial infection. MRI commonly shows a ring-enhancing lesion with central restricted diffusion, surrounding vasogenic edema, and mass effect; pathology typically demonstrates extensive neutrophilic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: MRI appearance of a ring-enhancing lesion with surrounding edema
Histologic appearance of suppurative or neutrophilic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported leukocytosis or other routine laboratory abnormalities
Disconjugate gaze
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: Toxoplasma gondii reactivation can cause ring-enhancing brain lesions in immunocompromised patients, particularly those receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Lesions may cause focal neurologic deficits, cognitive changes, seizures, and headache.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Single dominant lesion rather than multiple lesions
Histology suggestive of neutrophilic abscess rather than identifiable tachyzoites or bradyzoite cysts
No reported seizures
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: Primary CNS lymphoma is a malignant lymphoid tumor of the brain that is more common in immunosuppressed patients. It can produce focal neurologic deficits, neurocognitive symptoms, and enhancing brain masses, although lesions are more often solidly enhancing than abscess-like.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 3-day onset is less typical
Imaging appearance more suggestive of a multiloculated abscess
Neutrophilic inflammatory pathology is not typical of lymphoma
Headache and fatigue alone are nonspecific
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: Glioblastoma is an aggressive primary brain tumor that may appear as an irregular ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis and extensive surrounding edema. It can cause headache, aphasia, confusion, and focal weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing cerebral lesion with edema and possible central necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Very abrupt episodic onset of neurologic deficits is less typical
Immunosuppression favors opportunistic infection rather than glioblastoma
Histology showing prominent acute neutrophilic inflammation is not typical
Microbiologic images compatible with bacteria are not typical
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: 36-year-old obese woman with type 2 diabetes for 5 years, positive Mantoux test history, and smoking history (1 pack/day), presented with a 5-day history of fever, chills, productive cough with yellow sputum, and sharp right lower chest pain worsened by deep breathing, beginning about a week after an overnight stay at a lakeside cottage. On initial exam she was afebrile with clear lungs, but 5 days later returned with persistent symptoms, fever to 39°C, mild tachycardia, and decreased air entry with bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest.

A severe atypical bacterial pneumonia caused by Legionella species, often acquired by inhaling aerosolized contaminated freshwater from plumbing, spas, fountains, or other water systems. Imaging may show rapidly progressive, patchy or multilobar consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent overnight stay at a lakeside cottage with potential freshwater or plumbing-water exposure
Progressive right lower lobe air-space consolidation on chest radiographs
Patchy bilateral lower-lung consolidative and nodular infiltrates on CT and later radiograph
Diabetes, which increases risk of severe Legionella infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Yellow sputum is possible but Legionella often causes scant or nonpurulent sputum
No reported diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, confusion, hyponatremia, or relative bradycardia
Initial examination with clear lungs despite symptoms is less characteristic of established severe pneumonia

data.diagnosis: Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, especially pneumococcal pneumonia
data.description: An acute bacterial infection of the lung parenchyma, commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, producing fever, productive cough, pleuritic pain, focal bronchial breathing, and lobar or segmental consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain worsened by deep breathing
Decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds over the right lower chest
Right lower lobe consolidation on chest radiograph
Diabetes and smoking history, which predispose to bacterial pneumonia
symptoms_not_in_common: The substantial freshwater/cottage exposure is not specifically typical for pneumococcal pneumonia
Rapid evolution toward bilateral patchy lower-lobe infiltrates is less classically lobar than typical pneumococcal disease
No mention of rusty sputum, which can occur in pneumococcal pneumonia

data.description: A potentially severe pneumonia caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, acquired from contaminated soil or surface water in endemic regions. Diabetes is a major risk factor, and disease can cause multifocal, rapidly progressive pulmonary consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Type 2 diabetes, a major predisposing condition for melioidosis
Possible exposure to surface water during a lakeside stay
Multifocal lower-lung nodular and consolidative opacities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No stated travel or residence in a melioidosis-endemic area
No reported direct soil or muddy-water inoculation/exposure
No reported septic shock, abscesses, chronic constitutional symptoms, or disseminated infection

data.description: A chronic infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It commonly produces prolonged cough, fever, weight loss, night sweats, and upper-lobe infiltrates or cavitation, although lower-lobe disease can occur in some patients, including those with diabetes.
symptoms_in_common: History of a positive Mantoux test
Diabetes, which increases the risk of active tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute 5-day onset with chills is atypical for pulmonary tuberculosis
Productive yellow sputum and acute pleuritic pain are more typical of acute bacterial pneumonia
No reported chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, hemoptysis, or known tuberculosis exposure
Imaging shows predominantly acute lower-lobe consolidative disease rather than typical upper-lobe cavitation or chronic fibronodular changes

data.description: 19-year-old female with neonatal hypotonia and weak breathing/crying at birth, developing respiratory failure in the first month requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation. History includes patent ductus arteriosus repaired at age 2, recurrent respiratory infections, and scoliosis surgery at age 12. At age 4, nerve stimulation showed a 36% decrement in compound muscle action potential area, with no repetitive CMAPs after single nerve stimulation; AChR and MuSK antibodies were negative. Recent examination showed normal cognition, bilateral ptosis, mild limitation of upward gaze, facial-bulbar-neck-proximal limb weakness, and preserved deep tendon reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to RAPSN deficiency
data.description: An inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction disorder caused by impaired clustering of acetylcholine receptors. It commonly presents at birth or in infancy with severe weakness, respiratory failure, ptosis, and fatigable bulbar weakness. Ultrastructural studies may show abnormal neuromuscular-junction architecture and simplified postsynaptic folds.
symptoms_in_common: Weak cry and weak breathing at birth
Respiratory failure during the first month of life requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Negative acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies
Electron-microscopy evidence of abnormal neuromuscular-junction/postsynaptic-fold structure
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus
Scoliosis requiring surgery

data.description: A rare inherited congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in MUSK, impairing formation and maintenance of the neuromuscular junction. It can cause severe neonatal respiratory and bulbar weakness, ptosis, ophthalmoparesis, and abnormal postsynaptic junctional folds. This is distinct from autoimmune MuSK-antibody myasthenia gravis.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal respiratory insufficiency requiring long-term ventilation
Decremental compound muscle action potential response
Negative serum AChR and MuSK antibodies
Abnormal ultrastructural appearance of the neuromuscular junction
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus
Scoliosis requiring surgery
Recurrent respiratory infections are secondary complications rather than a primary defining feature

data.description: An inherited postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome due to impaired agrin-LRP4-MuSK signaling, which is necessary for acetylcholine-receptor clustering and postsynaptic-fold maturation. Severe early-onset cases can have respiratory failure, ocular and bulbar weakness, and structural abnormalities at the endplate.
symptoms_in_common: Severe weakness beginning in the neonatal period
Respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation
Recurrent respiratory infections due to respiratory-muscle weakness
Electron-microscopy findings compatible with impaired postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction development
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus
Scoliosis requiring surgery

data.description: A congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by AGRN variants that disrupt agrin signaling at the neuromuscular junction. It produces impaired acetylcholine-receptor clustering and may lead to neonatal or childhood-onset fatigable weakness, ptosis, respiratory involvement, and abnormal endplate morphology.
symptoms_in_common: Weak respiratory effort and cry at birth
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Absence of AChR and MuSK autoantibodies
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus
Scoliosis requiring surgery
Very severe persistent ventilator dependence is less common in many agrin-related cases

data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by defective DOK7-MuSK signaling. It often causes limb-girdle and axial weakness, respiratory compromise, scoliosis, and a decremental response on nerve stimulation; ocular symptoms are usually mild or absent compared with other congenital myasthenic syndromes.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory failure and recurrent respiratory infections
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent neonatal respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy is less typical
Bilateral ptosis
Limitation of upward gaze
Prominent facial and bulbar weakness
Patent ductus arteriosus

data.description: A 52-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with acute onset shortness of breath and confusion. On physical examination, he was agitated and taking deep breaths at a rate of 28/min. Initial venous blood gas on ambient air showed pH 7.02, partial pressure of carbon dioxide 3.4 kPa, and partial pressure of oxygen 4.1 kPa. Laboratory studies revealed blood glucose 7.1 mmol/L (reference range 4.4-6.1), lactic acid 6.6 mmol/L (0.5-2.2), serum anion gap 19 mmol/L (8-16), serum osmolality 318 mmol/kg (275-295), serum osmolal gap 20 mmol/kg (<10), and acute kidney injury with creatinine 141 μmol/L (70-120). Blood ethanol was undetectable and urine drug screen was negative. Urinalysis showed haematuria and no ketones.
Toxic alcohol ingestion causing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, elevated osmolal gap, acute kidney injury, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition in urine.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing consistent with respiratory compensation for severe metabolic acidosis
Acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine
Urine microscopy showing calcium oxalate-type crystals
Undetectable ethanol level and negative routine urine drug screen
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated blood glucose is not a characteristic finding
No reported history of toxic alcohol ingestion

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion that produces an elevated osmolal gap followed by high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis due to formic acid accumulation, often causing neurologic and visual toxicity.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated serum osmolality and osmolal gap
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary calcium oxalate crystals are not typical of methanol poisoning
Haematuria and acute kidney injury are less characteristic than in ethylene glycol poisoning
No visual symptoms such as blurred vision, photophobia, or vision loss are reported

data.diagnosis: Lactic acidosis due to tissue hypoperfusion or sepsis
data.description: Accumulation of lactate from impaired oxygen delivery or severe systemic illness, producing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and compensatory hyperventilation.
symptoms_in_common: Shortness of breath with deep rapid breathing
symptoms_not_in_common: An elevated osmolal gap is not typical of uncomplicated lactic acidosis
Calcium oxalate crystals in urine are not typical
Haematuria is not a typical primary feature
No fever, hypotension, infectious symptoms, or shock findings are described

data.description: A diabetic metabolic emergency caused by insulin deficiency, leading to hyperglycemia, ketone production, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, dehydration, and Kussmaul respirations.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing resembling Kussmaul respirations
Acute kidney injury that can occur with dehydration
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood glucose of 7.1 mmol/L is far below the usual level for diabetic ketoacidosis
Urinalysis shows no ketones
Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Calcium oxalate crystals and haematuria are not typical
Marked lactate elevation is not the primary expected abnormality

data.description: 36-year-old man with 18 days of fever up to 39.5°C preceded by throat swelling. Three days after onset, fever began and persisted despite amoxicillin-clavulanic acid given for presumed streptococcal pharyngitis. Associated symptoms included headaches, fatigue, and a sensation of lower neck swelling with discomfort on neck movement. He denied dysphagia, odynophagia, rhinorrhea, and rash. History notable for seasonal allergies and travel to the southwestern United States 2 weeks before symptom onset; his wife had fever and sore throat during the trip that resolved spontaneously. On examination, he was afebrile but tachycardic, with a normal oropharynx, no lymphadenopathy, and firm, nontender thyroid tissue palpable in the anterior neck.

data.diagnosis: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (de Quervain thyroiditis), likely post-viral
data.description: A self-limited inflammatory thyroid disorder, often following a viral upper-respiratory illness, that can cause fever, constitutional symptoms, diffuse thyroid enlargement, and inflammatory changes within the thyroid on CT.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior lower-neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement
Firm enlarged thyroid tissue on examination
CT appearance of diffuse thyroid enlargement with heterogeneous low-attenuation/inflammatory change
Recent possible viral exposure, as his wife had a self-limited fever and sore throat
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid on examination, whereas subacute thyroiditis is usually painful and tender
No preceding rhinorrhea or clear upper-respiratory symptoms
No reported symptoms of thyrotoxicosis such as tremor, palpitations, heat intolerance, or weight loss

data.description: A rare bacterial infection of the thyroid that produces fever, neck swelling, and thyroid inflammation; CT may show thyroid enlargement, heterogeneous enhancement, edema, or an evolving abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement
CT evidence of inflammatory thyroid enlargement
symptoms_not_in_common: Thyroid was nontender, while infectious thyroiditis is usually markedly painful and tender
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No visible focal thyroid abscess described on CT
Lack of improvement with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid may be atypical for susceptible routine bacterial infection

data.diagnosis: Acute coccidioidomycosis (Valley fever) with associated inflammatory thyroiditis
data.description: Coccidioidomycosis is a fungal infection acquired in the southwestern United States. Acute illness commonly causes fever, fatigue, headache, sore throat, and respiratory symptoms; thyroid involvement is uncommon but systemic inflammation may trigger or coincide with thyroiditis.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to the southwestern United States shortly before illness
Potential shared exposure because his wife developed a transient febrile sore-throat illness during the trip
Failure to improve with antibacterial therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough, dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, or other pulmonary symptoms
No rash, including erythema nodosum or erythema multiforme
Prominent thyroid enlargement is unusual for uncomplicated acute coccidioidomycosis
No lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Viral thyroiditis associated with an acute viral infection
data.description: Viruses such as enteroviruses, adenovirus, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, Epstein-Barr virus, or other respiratory viruses can precede thyroid inflammation and cause fever, malaise, neck discomfort, and diffuse thyroid enlargement.
symptoms_in_common: Febrile illness with headache and fatigue
Possible contagious viral exposure from his wife
Diffuse firm thyroid enlargement and neck discomfort
Imaging findings compatible with thyroid inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No rhinorrhea or other prominent upper-respiratory symptoms
No thyroid tenderness despite inflammatory thyroid enlargement
Fever persisting for 18 days is longer than many uncomplicated viral syndromes
No rash or lymphadenopathy

data.description: 42-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia presented with 2 days of sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back in a bandlike pattern, worsened by movement, with nausea and early satiety. He also reported substernal chest pressure similar to his usual angina but not relieved by one sublingual nitroglycerin tablet. He denied trauma, vomiting, rectal bleeding, or melena. Chronic symptoms included diarrhea since coronary bypass surgery, worsened after a cholesterol medication dose increase 6 months earlier, 16 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, intermittent early satiety, daily headaches, frequent nocturia, and feeling warm at night without fever or night sweats. Exam showed mild left upper quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs. Vitals were stable. Labs showed mildly elevated amylase, lipase, AST, and ALT with otherwise normal electrolytes, renal function, blood counts, bilirubin, and triglycerides. ECG showed normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes, and chest radiograph was normal.

A rare systemic infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei, usually involving the small intestine and causing malabsorption. The CT appearance of mesenteric lymphadenopathy and small-bowel involvement, together with biopsy showing lamina propria packed with macrophage-like cells, is highly suggestive.
symptoms_in_common: Possible systemic symptoms of feeling warm at night
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden severe left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina
Mildly elevated amylase and lipase
Frequent nocturia
Daily headaches

data.description: An immune-mediated gluten-sensitive enteropathy causing chronic inflammation and malabsorption of the small intestine. It can produce diarrhea, weight loss, abdominal discomfort, and nutritional deficiency, although the illustrated biopsy and nodal findings are more supportive of Whipple disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute bandlike left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy with the described imaging appearance
Substernal angina-like chest pressure
Mild amylase and lipase elevation
Frequent nocturia
Daily headaches

data.diagnosis: Chronic mesenteric ischemia with possible acute-on-chronic intestinal ischemia
data.description: Reduced intestinal blood flow caused by atherosclerotic mesenteric arterial disease. His known coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia increase risk. It can cause postprandial abdominal symptoms, food avoidance, diarrhea, and weight loss; acute worsening can cause sudden abdominal pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Mesenteric lymphadenopathy and macrophage-rich small-bowel biopsy findings
No reported postprandial pain pattern or food fear
Stable vital signs and no peritoneal signs despite acute pain
Substernal chest pressure not relieved by nitroglycerin
Frequent nocturia
Daily headaches

data.description: Inflammation of the pancreas that classically causes acute epigastric or left upper abdominal pain radiating to the back with nausea and elevated pancreatic enzymes. The enzyme elevations here are only mild, and the chronic diarrhea, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, and biopsy findings suggest an additional underlying intestinal disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back
Mild elevation of AST and ALT
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhea
Six-month 16 kg unintentional weight loss
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy/small-bowel abnormalities on CT
Biopsy findings suggestive of an infiltrative intestinal infection
Early satiety predating the acute episode
Frequent nocturia
Daily headaches

data.description: A 59-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of stiffness, swelling, and severe pain beginning in the metacarpophalangeal joint of the right thumb, followed by bilateral ankle involvement 3 days later. She had a history of stroke, glaucoma, and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 7 years prior. The patient lived in New England, worked in health care, and reported unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before presentation. Physical examination showed the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint was erythematous, warm, and painful with movement. Both ankles showed effusion and warmth without erythema, with pain on all range of motion. No fever, chills, night sweats, or systemic symptoms were reported. Joint stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve throughout the day. Symptoms had not improved despite 4 days of methylprednisolone therapy.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated gonococcal infection with gonococcal septic arthritis
data.description: Hematogenous dissemination of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that can cause migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis, or purulent septic arthritis. The recent unprotected sexual exposure and microbiologic images consistent with diplococcal bacterial growth strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Initial involvement of the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Warmth, swelling, joint effusions, and pain with range of motion
Absence of fever or systemic symptoms can occur in disseminated gonococcal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No skin lesions or pustular rash were reported
No tenosynovitis was specifically described
Age 59 years is less typical than the younger age groups most commonly affected

data.description: Infection of a joint by pyogenic bacteria, commonly Staphylococcus aureus or streptococci, producing acute painful swelling, warmth, effusion, and restricted movement. Bacteremia can occasionally cause more than one involved joint.
symptoms_in_common: Erythema and warmth of the thumb joint
Marked pain with all range of motion
Failure to improve with corticosteroid therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential involvement of multiple joints is less typical than single-joint disease
No fever, chills, or systemic illness
Recent unprotected intercourse specifically favors gonococcal infection over common pyogenic pathogens
Thumb metacarpophalangeal involvement followed by bilateral ankles is an unusual pattern for typical staphylococcal septic arthritis

data.diagnosis: Reactive arthritis triggered by a sexually transmitted infection
data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis occurring after genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection, classically associated with Chlamydia trachomatis. It often affects the lower extremities asymmetrically and may be accompanied by urethritis, conjunctivitis, mucocutaneous lesions, or enthesitis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute inflammatory joint pain and swelling
Lack of a typical prolonged morning-stiffness pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent erythematous swelling of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Joint effusions with severe pain on all range of motion suggesting septic arthritis
No urethritis, cervicitis, conjunctivitis, rash, enthesitis, or mucosal lesions reported
Microbiologic findings suggesting active bacterial infection rather than sterile postinfectious arthritis
Onset only about 2 weeks after sexual exposure is relatively short for many reactive arthritis presentations

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that usually causes symmetric small-joint synovitis, prolonged morning stiffness, and progressive joint damage if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: Joint swelling, warmth, stiffness, and pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset over days
Severe sequential onset beginning in one thumb joint and rapidly involving both ankles
Stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve during the day
Marked ankle effusions and acute pain with all range of motion
Recent unprotected sexual exposure and microbiologic evidence favor an infectious cause
No improvement with methylprednisolone

data.description: A 29-year-old man presented to the hospital after several weeks of lumbar pain and fever up to 38°C. He had no significant past medical history. Physical examination revealed vital signs of blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 121/min, and body temperature 38.2°C. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected on examination. Laboratory tests showed anemia with hematocrit 31.8% and hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, white blood cell count 3.92 × 10³/μL, elevated liver enzymes with AST 78 IU/L and ALT 71 IU/L, and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase 1,591 IU/L. Serum cortisol level was 17.47 μg/dL at 8 AM and ACTH level was 12.1 pg/mL (normal range: 10-90). Ten days after admission, the patient developed pancytopenia with WBC 2.88 × 10³/μL, Hb 10.7 g/dL, and platelets 129 × 10³/μL. Bone marrow biopsy was negative for specific hematologic or malignant disorder.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with bilateral adrenal involvement
data.description: Systemic infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, which can involve the reticuloendothelial system, bone marrow, liver, spleen, lungs, and adrenal glands. Imaging may show bilateral adrenal enlargement and multiple small hepatic and splenic lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Lumbar or flank pain potentially related to enlarged adrenal glands
Pulmonary infiltrative abnormalities on chest radiographs
Multiple small liver and splenic lesions on abdominal imaging
Bilateral adrenal enlargement or masses on CT/MRI
Absence of a diagnostic malignant process on bone marrow biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly on physical examination
No lymphadenopathy
Normal morning cortisol and ACTH levels despite apparent adrenal involvement

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with bilateral adrenal tuberculosis
data.description: Hematogenous Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can affect the lungs, liver, spleen, bone marrow, and adrenal glands. Bilateral adrenal enlargement may occur and can eventually lead to adrenal insufficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Mild elevation of AST and ALT
Bilateral adrenal enlargement on cross-sectional imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported cough, sputum production, weight loss, or night sweats
No documented adrenal insufficiency
Normal cortisol and ACTH levels
No granulomatous or mycobacterial findings reported on bone marrow biopsy
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected clinically

data.diagnosis: Primary adrenal lymphoma with systemic involvement
data.description: Aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma can present as bilateral adrenal masses and may involve the liver, spleen, lungs, and bone marrow. It is often associated with fever, cytopenias, and markedly elevated LDH.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral adrenal masses or enlargement on CT/MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age, as primary adrenal lymphoma is more common in older adults
No lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Bone marrow biopsy negative for hematologic malignancy
Normal adrenal hormonal testing

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection that infiltrates macrophage-rich organs, especially the spleen, liver, and bone marrow, producing prolonged fever, cytopenias, and elevated inflammatory markers. Adrenal involvement is uncommon but possible in disseminated disease.
symptoms_in_common: Negative initial bone marrow assessment for malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly, which is usually prominent
No reported travel or exposure history to endemic areas
Bilateral adrenal enlargement is not a typical major feature
Pulmonary infiltrates are less typical
Lumbar pain is not a typical presenting symptom

diagnoses.name: Non-Hodgkin T-cell lymphoma, natural killer (NK)/T-cell, nasal type
diagnoses.title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type

data.description: A 23-year-old female presented with a complaint of intermittent dyspnea (New York Heart Association NYHA grade, II), which aggravates on exertion and mild chest pain. No past significant medical and surgical history was given by the patient. On clinical examination, bruit was heard on auscultation in the left mid-zone.

data.diagnosis: Complex pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (pulmonary arteriovenous fistula) of the left lung
data.description: A congenital abnormal direct connection between a pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein, bypassing the normal capillary bed. The CT angiographic images show markedly enlarged, tortuous left hilar pulmonary vessels consistent with a high-flow vascular malformation.
symptoms_in_common: Bruit heard over the left mid-lung zone
symptoms_not_in_common: None of the reported symptoms is strongly atypical, although chest pain is less common than dyspnea or a pulmonary bruit

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary artery aneurysm involving the left pulmonary arterial circulation
data.description: A pulmonary artery aneurysm is abnormal focal or diffuse enlargement of the pulmonary artery, sometimes associated with congenital shunts or pulmonary vascular malformations. The imaging appearance of prominent enlarged left hilar pulmonary vessels may represent aneurysmal dilatation in a high-flow lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Bruit caused by turbulent flow through enlarged pulmonary vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent symptoms without signs of pulmonary hypertension or right-heart failure are less typical in a large symptomatic pulmonary artery aneurysm

data.diagnosis: Patent ductus arteriosus with pulmonary arterial dilatation
data.description: Patent ductus arteriosus is persistence of a fetal communication between the aorta and pulmonary artery, producing a left-to-right shunt and increased pulmonary blood flow. It can cause enlarged pulmonary arteries and a thoracic continuous murmur or bruit.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent pulmonary vascular structures on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The bruit is described in the left mid-zone rather than the classic left upper parasternal or infraclavicular location
Mild chest pain is not a classic presenting symptom

data.description: A 65-year-old man presented with bilateral leg swelling that had worsened over six weeks. He reported vague abdominal discomfort and tiredness. Physical examination revealed bilateral pitting edema up to the groin, without erythema, tenderness, or warmth. The patient was systemically well with normal heart sounds and clear chest examination. No palpable masses or lymphadenopathy were found in the abdomen. Laboratory testing showed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 95 g/L; normal range 130-180), elevated C-reactive protein of 33.0 mg/L (normal range 0-5.0), and raised IgG4 level (3.55 g/L; normal range 0.08-1.4). Doppler ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis.

A fibroinflammatory manifestation of IgG4-related disease in which retroperitoneal soft tissue surrounds major vessels and/or ureters. The CT appearance is consistent with infiltrative retroperitoneal soft tissue, which can compress the inferior vena cava or iliac veins and produce severe bilateral leg edema.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral pitting leg edema extending to the groin
CT evidence of retroperitoneal soft-tissue infiltration around major abdominal vessels
No deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No other typical organ manifestations of IgG4-related disease were described, such as autoimmune pancreatitis, salivary gland enlargement, orbital disease, or renal lesions

data.description: A chronic inflammatory and fibrosing disorder producing a plaque-like retroperitoneal mass, often centered around the infrarenal aorta and iliac vessels. It can obstruct venous or ureteric structures; in this case, venous compression could account for bilateral leg swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Normocytic anemia consistent with chronic inflammation
Retroperitoneal infiltrative soft tissue on CT
Bilateral leg edema potentially caused by iliocaval venous compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated serum IgG4, which more strongly suggests an IgG4-related subtype rather than purely idiopathic disease
No reported flank pain, renal impairment, hydronephrosis, or urinary obstruction

data.description: Lymphoma can present as infiltrative retroperitoneal soft tissue or confluent lymphadenopathy that encases vessels and causes venous obstruction. Compression of the inferior vena cava or iliac veins may result in marked bilateral lower-limb edema.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema that could result from pelvic or retroperitoneal venous compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy
No fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss reported
Raised serum IgG4 is not a typical primary finding in lymphoma
The imaging appearance of a plaque-like perivascular infiltrate is more suggestive of retroperitoneal fibrosis than bulky nodal lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Malignant retroperitoneal or pelvic venous obstruction
data.description: A retroperitoneal malignancy, metastatic nodal disease, or pelvic cancer can compress the inferior vena cava or iliac veins, producing bilateral pitting edema. Such processes may also cause anemia, inflammation, and nonspecific abdominal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: No deep vein thrombosis despite severe leg edema, supporting possible proximal venous compression
